browser automation
multi-IDE support
notes: Apache-2.0 client: VS Code-family extension, CLI (also usable as the agent in Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim and Emacs via ACP) and a beta Desktop app (announced 14 Sep 2026), with direct-provider and local-model routes; releases ship several times a week. The JetBrains Marketplace plugin is free but is licensed under Cline's ToS with no public source. Cline Cloud agents (docs added 7 Oct 2026) run tasks in Cline's cloud sandbox with Cline-managed models only. Scope privacy claims to the selected route; enterprise governance runs through Cline's hosted admin console, and enterprise does not by itself mean self-hosted inference. Openness is recorded as open-core for the whole record: the clients in cline/cline are Apache-2.0, while the JetBrains Marketplace plugin, Cloud agents and the hosted enterprise console are not open source.

required_controls: Configure only a local runtime (Ollama, LM Studio or Atomic Chat) on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers; no Cline, ClinePass, free-model, subscription/CLI-login or cloud BYOK provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Use the Apache-2.0 client (VS Code extension, CLI or Desktop) without a Cline account; Cline's ToS states no User Content is collected with telemetry when calls stay on your infrastructure and no account exists.
Turn telemetry off (extension: Allow error and usage reporting; Desktop: Settings > General; CLI: telemetryOptOut), also turn off editor telemetry, and restart Desktop/the Cline hub.
Restrict outbound network traffic: with telemetry off, Cline still contacts its servers for sign-in and feature flags.

Do not use Cloud agents, web search, the Cline API, CLI messaging connectors (cline connect: Slack, Telegram, etc.), remote MCP servers or marketplace add-ons that send data off the host; keep auto-approve/YOLO off for sensitive workspaces.
residual_risks: Telemetry is on by default, including with own keys and local models. The Desktop v0.0.26 release note (11 Sep 2026) says prompt tracing was then limited to Cline/ClinePass requests, implying earlier Desktop builds traced own-key turns; keep installs current.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so prompts can leave the machine unless Ollama's cloud features are disabled and the log check is repeated after updates.
Desktop and the CLI ignore the organization's telemetry and provider settings, so these controls must be enforced on each machine.

Task and session histories are stored locally (~/.cline/data/tasks; hub sessions in ~/.cline/data). Enterprise Prompt Storage can sync them to S3/R2. Institutional access, retention and backup controls are required.

Offline or air-gapped operation of the open-source client is not publicly documented; enterprise VPC/on-prem/air-gapped deployment is advertised only, and enterprise governance uses Cline's hosted admin console.
Agent terminal, browser and MCP tools can move data off the host if egress is not blocked.

name: Tabnine
deployment: Enterprise only: Tabnine-hosted SaaS, or private installation in the customer's own VPC (AWS/GCP/Azure) or on-premises, optionally fully air-gapped
model_backend: Tabnine Universal model for code completions. Chat/agent use admin-enabled models: on SaaS, Tabnine-served GPT, Claude and Gemini families plus open-weight models. Private installations use self-hosted open-weight models, admin-configured private endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible) or, optionally, Tabnine-hosted inference over Private Service Connect. Model lists change frequently.
data_handling_note: Docs state a no-train/no-retain policy: inference context is processed ephemerally and deleted after the answer, including in private installations (privacy page last updated 2025-07-30). Exceptions: the global RAG (repository connection) index, an admin-enabled feature marked private preview, is retained on the Tabnine server, which on SaaS is Tabnine-operated. On Enterprise SaaS, Tabnine trains on customer code only if a private custom model is chosen. The privacy page says the policy applies regardless of the model used, but the AI Models page warns that third-party chat/agent models (GPT, Claude, Gemini families on SaaS) may have different privacy terms, and no provider-level retention terms are published. For self-hosted, non-air-gapped clusters, the privacy page says operational metrics and logs (kept one week) and one-way-hashed client telemetry (user email, hostname, IP) go to Tabnine, never code. A v4.6.0 release note says telemetry to Tabnine is optional and off by default. Air-gapped installs can send metrics and logs to the customer's own Prometheus and log aggregator.

suitability_notes.personal: Enterprise SaaS main datacenters are in the US (AWS North Virginia, GCP Council Bluffs Iowa, Heroku Virginia). Chat/agent can use third-party model families, and the global RAG index is retained server-side. Use only under a DPA covering subprocessors and transfers (DPA and subprocessor list are not public), with admin-restricted models and no repository connection; prefer a private installation.
suitability_notes.special: Only a private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or the institution's own cloud account; air-gapped preferred) serving self-hosted open-weight models. Tabnine SaaS, Tabnine-hosted inference and third-party cloud model endpoints do not qualify.

compliance: Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001:2015 and GDPR, with reports gated; docs state SOC 2 and GDPR compliance. No report type or dates are public; verify the current report and that its scope covers the contracted deployment.
pricing: No public price list on 2026-10-10: tabnine.com/pricing returned HTTP 502 and the tabnine.com homepage redirects to Tricentis. Enterprise SaaS accounts are set up with the Tabnine team; private installation is an Enterprise option. The September list prices ($39 and $59 per user/month, annual) could not be re-confirmed (UNVERIFIED); obtain a quote.
academic: None found: no academic or student offer in current first-party docs; the public pricing page was unavailable on 2026-10-10

notes: Enterprise-only commercial coding assistant (IDE plugins, agent, OpenCode-based CLI) with documented on-premises and air-gapped installation. Tricentis acquired Tabnine (announced 2026-07-30); the tabnine.com homepage now redirects to Tricentis, while docs and private-installation releases continue (v6.6.9, 2026-10-08). The public IDE plugins no longer onboard new users; the legacy Tabnine CLI gets only critical fixes until 2026-12-31.
tier_gate: Tabnine Enterprise private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or own cloud account, air-gapped preferred) with self-hosted open-weight models; Tabnine SaaS, Tabnine-hosted inference and third-party cloud model endpoints do not qualify

required_controls: Tabnine Enterprise private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or the institution's own AWS/GCP/Azure account); fully air-gapped mode preferred.

Serve chat, agent and Context Engine models from self-hosted open-weight models on institution GPUs; leave third-party endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, OpenAI) and Tabnine-hosted inference or proxy options disabled.

Keep cluster metrics, logs and client telemetry inside the institution (air-gapped Prometheus/log aggregator, or confirmed-disabled telemetry to Tabnine) and block egress to Tabnine and third parties.
Restrict MCP servers, native tools and repository connections through admin governance; connect only institution-hosted repositories.

For the OpenCode-based CLI: do not use session sharing (--share), which Tabnine docs do not list as an admin-governed control; check that users' existing OpenCode configs and MCP servers are not carried into Tabnine sessions; keep sign-in and updates pointed at the institution's Tabnine console.
residual_risks: Docs conflict on self-hosted telemetry: the privacy page says non-air-gapped clusters send metrics, logs and hashed user identifiers to Tabnine, while a v4.6.0 release note says this telemetry is optional and off by default.
Ownership changed (Tricentis, July 2026); contract terms, roadmap and long-term support for standalone private installations are not publicly documented.
Self-hosted open-weight models need multi-GPU H100/H200/B200-class servers and may be less capable than the frontier models offered on SaaS.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
No air-gapped install or update path is documented for the OpenCode-based CLI.

name: Tabby
deployment: self-hostable / cloud
model_backend: Tabby server: local models through its bundled llama.cpp (model registry), or HTTP connectors to self-hosted endpoints (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp) or remote provider APIs (docs name Claude and OpenAI). Pochi: BYOK OpenAI-compatible providers, including local Ollama or LM Studio, or Pochi-hosted models after account sign-in.
data_handling_note: Self-hosted Tabby with a local model, or Pochi in BYOK mode with a local model, keeps code and prompts on controlled infrastructure. Pochi BYOK needs no account and stores task history locally by default. Telemetry is on by default: the Tabby server and IDE extensions send non-code usage statistics (server and hardware info, completion counts and latency) under a random ID to app.tabbyml.com, and each can be disabled. Pochi's extension source sends PostHog analytics only after a Pochi account sign-in (the signed-in user's email and name are attached). Remote model connectors fall under the chosen provider's own terms; Pochi-hosted models and Pochi cloud task storage leave this boundary and have no readable first-party retention or training terms. The tabbyml.com privacy policy (last modified 2024-11-11) covers only website visits and orders.

suitability_notes.personal: Use self-hosted Tabby or Pochi BYOK with a self-hosted model, and disable both server and extension usage collection. Assess any remote model API or Pochi cloud account separately.
suitability_notes.special: Only with self-hosted Tabby, or Pochi BYOK, using a local model on institution-controlled infrastructure (Ollama, if used, in local-only mode), with all telemetry disabled and no Pochi account, remote model API, web search or web fetch. Tabby's free Community plan covers up to 5 users; more users need Team or Enterprise. Tabby server has had no commits since 2026-06-30, so institutional security review must account for patching.

compliance: No compliance certification asserted in the first-party sources reviewed; self-hosted deployment
SSO, authentication domain and enforcement of IDE/extension telemetry policy are listed for Enterprise only (pricing comparison)
pricing: Community: free, open source, local deployment, up to 5 users. Team: $19/seat/month, up to 50 users, 'flexible deployment'. Enterprise: custom pricing, unlimited users. Tabby Cloud (Pochi): usage-based on LLM token cost, with $20 in free monthly credits. The pricing page still calls Pochi tab completion free, but Pochi docs say tab completion is switched off in current releases. A yearly-billing toggle shows annual plans that do not map to these tiers; they are not relied on here.
academic: Community self-hosted use is available; no separate academic entitlement is asserted.
use_cases: coding
code completion
inline chat
answer engine
agentic coding (Pochi)
notes: Two TabbyML products. Tabby is a self-hosted completion and chat server with no development activity since mid-2026: its latest stable release is v0.32.0 (2026-01-25), main has had no commits since 2026-06-30, and recent community PRs got no maintainer replies; no first-party announcement deprecates it. On main (not in v0.32.0), PR #4425 (2026-01-23) hard-disabled chat, Answer Engine search and Pages in the bundled web UI; the server-side code was not removed. Pochi, an Apache-2.0 VS Code agent and CLI, is under active development, with releases through 2026-10-10; its tab completion has been switched off since July 2026. Keep Pochi BYOK/local-model use apart from the Pochi cloud account route. Licensing: Tabby is Apache-2.0 outside its ee/ directory; ee/ (including tabby-webserver and tabby-ui) is under the separate Tabby Enterprise licence, which ties production use to TabbyML subscription terms that are not published on the Tabby terms page. Pochi is Apache-2.0. Third-party components keep their own licences.
tier_gate: self-hosted Tabby (Community up to 5 users; Team or Enterprise beyond) or Pochi BYOK, with a local model and telemetry off, for regulated data; a Pochi cloud account does not qualify

required_controls: Run the Tabby server on institution-controlled hardware with a local model (bundled llama.cpp, or a local Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp endpoint), or use Pochi in BYOK mode with a local Ollama or LM Studio model.

Point every Tabby model role (completion, chat and any embedding model) and every Pochi model setting at that local endpoint, keep no cloud provider API keys in server or client configuration or environment, and verify the effective server and client configuration after deployment and after each update.
Set TABBY_DISABLE_USAGE_COLLECTION=1 on the server and anonymousUsageTracking disable = true in every IDE extension config; both send usage data to app.tabbyml.com by default.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models. Keep Ollama bound to localhost or behind an allow list; Pochi's Ollama setup guide sets OLLAMA_ORIGINS='*' and itself warns about public exposure.
Do not configure remote model APIs, sign in to a Pochi account, use Pochi sharing or cloud task storage, or enable Answer Engine web search; do not use Pochi's webFetch tool or remote MCP servers.
Manage Tabby server and IDE-extension updates centrally instead of through unmanaged auto-update.
Block outbound network egress from servers and clients at host or network level, and test that the block holds.
residual_risks: Tabby server shows no development since 2026-06-30 (last stable release 2026-01-25). A request for private security reporting (issue #4528) was closed as not planned, private vulnerability reporting is disabled and the repository has no SECURITY.md, so patching and security review fall to the institution.
On Tabby's main branch, chat, Answer Engine search and Pages are hard-disabled in the bundled web UI (PR #4425, not in v0.32.0); future releases may drop these features.
Central enforcement of the IDE/extension telemetry policy is listed only for Enterprise; on Community and Team each client must be configured.
The Pochi agent runs commands, edits files, can fetch web URLs (webFetch tool) and can call local or remote MCP servers, any of which can move data outside the boundary.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a Tabby or Pochi setting that points at local Ollama does not by itself show that inference stays local.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Devin
deployment: Cloud. Devin Cloud runs the agent brain and Devbox in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud. Enterprise Customer Dedicated Deployment is a Cognition-hosted single-tenant VPC reached by AWS PrivateLink or IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on dedicated tenants) executes commands on machines the customer operates or on partner platforms (e.g. Modal, Daytona, E2B, Cloudflare), while inference and planning stay in Devin's cloud.
model_backend: Compound system operated by Cognition: Cognition SWE models (SWE-2 entered research preview on 21 Sep 2026) plus third-party models. The DPA lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft/Azure and Google/Vertex as US model subprocessors; release notes (8 Apr 2026) also offer Cerebras as an optional enterprise inference provider, which the DPA list does not name. No customer LLM API keys; Pro, Max and Teams users can link a ChatGPT plan to pay for GPT usage.
data_handling_note: Platform terms (updated 30 Jun 2026) allow training on Customer Data by default, and only paid tiers can opt out (Teams: admin only). After opt-out, data is not used for training and ZDR is enabled with model providers; ZDR does not cover data flagged by abuse classifiers, safety/security/AUP review, or legal process. Enterprise terms: no training without prior written consent. Product-level retention remains: data processed through Devin is kept for the customer relationship, and the DPA retention period runs to 30 days after termination. Enterprise terms add a security exhibit with deletion within 90 days of a request or termination and audit logs kept at least one year; the self-serve platform terms only say Cognition may delete Customer Data at its option on termination. Feedback and interaction data are kept as Cognition decides. Anonymised, aggregated Usage Data is collected. Optional ChatGPT-plan linking sends GPT calls through the user's ChatGPT subscription; the docs do not say whether provider ZDR covers that route. Dedicated deployments and Outposts keep inference in Cognition Cloud.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-held Teams or Enterprise plan: Pro and Max are individual plans, and the Cognition DPA treats the contracting customer as data controller. On Teams an admin must opt out of training; Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. Keep ChatGPT-plan linking off and rely on the Cognition DPA with an appropriate legal basis. Platform terms bar medical information and sensitive personal data such as birth dates; Enterprise terms bar protected health information and such data unless a separate written agreement permits it; the Acceptable Use Policy also bars special-category, biometric and government-ID data without a separate written agreement. DPA-listed subprocessors are in the US (one support subprocessor in India); EEA transfers rely on SCCs.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate: Cognition documents that inference and planning always run in its cloud, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Outposts, and its Acceptable Use Policy prohibits uploading special-category data without a separate written agreement.

compliance: Cognition's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (reports access-gated); the DPA states SOC 2 Type II.
DPA (updated 23 Jul 2026) incorporates EU SCCs (Modules 2 and 3) and the UK Addendum; listed subprocessors are US-based, plus one support subprocessor in India.
Signed DPA and exact service/model scope require confirmation.
pricing: Free; Pro $20/month; Max $200/month; Teams for up to 200 users with $40/month full seats and free flex seats that draw on shared on-demand credits. Teams wording conflicts: the pricing page reads “$80/month for team plan + $40/mo per full dev seat”, while billing docs describe $80/month as a minimum met by full seats and/or prepaid credits (two full seats = $80); confirm at checkout. Usage beyond quota is bought as on-demand credits at API pricing. Enterprise: contractual ACU pricing.
academic: No academic or student discount program documented.

notes: Autonomous cloud software engineer, used from the web app, Slack/Teams, the API, or `devin --cloud` in the Devin CLI; the Data Analyst agent (paid plans) queries connected data sources. Customer Dedicated Deployment is vendor-hosted, not customer-controlled on-prem. Outposts (introduced July 2026) lets sessions execute on a lab or institutional machine, but inference stays in Cognition's cloud, so it does not change the special-category classification. The local Devin Desktop IDE has its own catalog entry.
tier_gate: institution-held Teams or Enterprise plan (Pro/Max are individual plans) + training opt-out (Teams: admin only; Enterprise terms bar training without written consent) + Cognition DPA + ChatGPT-plan linking off; no medical or sensitive personal data (e.g., birth dates) and no special-category data under the terms and AUP unless a separate written agreement permits it

residual_risks: Inference and planning always run in Cognition's cloud, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Outposts; Outposts moves only command execution to customer-operated or partner machines.

Cognition's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits uploading special-category data and regulated health information without a separate written agreement; the DPA records that the customer does not intend to submit such data, and Cognition assumes no additional obligations for it beyond the DPA security measures.

name: Replit Agent
deployment: cloud (Replit platform hosted primarily on Google Cloud in the US, with an opt-in India hosting region; Agent inference via third-party AI model providers; Enterprise can restrict published-app deployment geography; the sales-assisted Enterprise dedicated GCP project / single-tenant option is vendor-managed and not documented as customer-controlled)
model_backend: Replit-managed multi-provider stack with intelligent model routing across Free, Power and Max modes. The Agent's own model cannot be swapped (BYOK applies only to models an app calls, not to Agent). Agent uses third-party models: the subprocessor list names Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for AI models, and its AI-infrastructure entries include Baseten, Fireworks AI and Parallel Web Systems. Enterprise model settings also list DeepSeek, Kimi and Z.ai; open-source model providers are off by default. The model catalog changes frequently.
data_handling_note: Plan-specific. Starter/Core (Terms of Service): Replit's model-improvement page says prompts, instructions, context and generated responses are used to develop and improve its models and AI features, and the Privacy Policy names improving its machine-learning technologies such as code generation as a legitimate interest; no opt-out is documented for these plans. Pro (Pro Agreement C.2.c): Customer Content may be used to train models and AI features by default; the opt-out in Settings > Personalization covers new content only, deletes nothing, and leaves Replit's licence to use Customer Content to improve the Platform in place. Enterprise (Enterprise Agreement, last updated September 9, 2026, B.2.g): Replit will not use Customer Content to improve products or train machine-learning models except as expressly permitted in that agreement; the B.2.c licence still covers troubleshooting, improving and securing the Platform. No fixed product retention period is published; Enterprise prompt text is retained and retrievable through the Compliance API, and Enterprise audit logs are kept 30 days by default; the DPA allows a return or deletion request up to 90 days after termination, except where law requires retention. De-identified Usage Data may be used and shared with third parties. No zero-data-retention commitment was found. All Agent inference is cloud-based: Replit's managed stack calls third-party model providers (the subprocessor list names Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for AI models and Fireworks AI and Baseten as AI infrastructure, all US).

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Starter/Core content feeds model improvement with no documented opt-out. For unpublished code or data, use Pro with the model-improvement opt-out set, or Enterprise.
suitability_notes.personal: Only through Enterprise (self-serve or sales-assisted) under the Enterprise Agreement and DPA, with admin controls set (approved model providers, private deployments, deployment geography) and review of retention and connected third-party services. Enterprise model controls are enabled through Replit sales, and Replit's rule that at least one model from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google must remain enabled means these three providers cannot all be switched off (whether one model per provider is required is not stated). Pro's opt-out is an account setting, not the Enterprise contractual no-training term.
suitability_notes.special: Agent inference runs in vendor cloud (Replit's platform plus third-party AI model providers); Replit states the Agent model cannot be swapped and no local, self-hosted or customer-controlled inference route is documented, so it does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: Replit states SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance and says it is working toward ISO 27001; audit reports sit in the Trust Center and were not reviewed.
Enterprise Agreement (no-training term) and DPA (referenced by the Pro and Enterprise agreements; SCCs for international transfers) must be confirmed for the exact Replit plan.
No HIPAA/BAA offering found in the reviewed first-party sources.
pricing: Starter: free, with daily Agent credits up to a monthly cap and one published app that goes down after 30 days. Core: $20/month, or $18/month billed annually. Pro: displayed at $100/month, or $90/month billed annually (base tier; larger credit tiers exist). Core and Pro include a Free Mode allowance and monthly credits; Power/Max modes, publishing and cloud resources draw on credits with effort-based pricing. Enterprise: self-serve (pay-as-you-go or annual credit commitment) or custom via sales. Prices exclude tax; confirm at checkout.
academic: Replit for Education (replit.com/edu) advertises free access for verified educators at approved schools and 50% off Core for students with a .edu email; eligibility depends on an approved school-domain list, to which institutions can request addition. Terms and data handling for education accounts are not documented, and education access does not give the Enterprise no-training term.

notes: Agent 4 launched in March 2026. Since August 2026, Agent work runs in Free, Power or Max mode with intelligent model routing, inside a wider Replit platform (Chat, Design, Routines, and inline data charts from Atta, whose acquisition was announced September 25, 2026). New OpenAI and Anthropic models were added in late September and October 2026, so model identities should not be frozen. Enterprise admins can restrict providers and models, require private deployments, set deployment geography and stream audit logs (30-day default audit-log retention). Scope note: kept for research coding use, although Replit now positions itself as a platform to create, launch and grow apps, sites, tools and businesses.
tier_gate: Enterprise (self-serve or sales-assisted) with Enterprise Agreement + DPA; Pro opt-out is not equivalent; Starter/Core not for personal data

residual_risks: The Agent model cannot be swapped and is served through Replit's managed stack and third-party AI subprocessors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AI-infrastructure providers); no local, self-hosted or customer-controlled inference endpoint is documented.
The sales-assisted Enterprise dedicated GCP project / single-tenant option is vendor-managed and not documented as customer-controlled infrastructure.

name: OpenHands
deployment: local (Agent Canvas via npm/npx or Docker; desktop app preview build for macOS, Windows and Linux) / self-hosted (VM, Docker, Kubernetes Helm) / OpenHands Cloud SaaS / OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted on-premises, private cloud or VPC, or SaaS)
model_backend: BYO key for LiteLLM-supported providers or a custom base URL (OpenAI-compatible endpoints); documented local model servers (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang); OpenHands LLM provider via a Cloud account at provider rates. Agent Canvas can also run third-party ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode), which use their own providers and terms.
data_handling_note: Self-hosted Agent Canvas/Agent Server with a local model keeps code, prompts and conversation history on your machines. Outbound traffic then comes from optional integrations, MCP servers, ACP agents and product telemetry. Agent Canvas asks for analytics consent but sends one anonymous install event before consent unless telemetry is disabled (AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry, since v1.17.0). The launcher and Docker image also pre-configure consent-gated PostHog telemetry for the automation and agent-server services unless VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1 is set. OpenHands Cloud: the privacy policy (effective 3 Sep 2025) allows All Hands AI to use content and feedback to train and tune its models, shares content with third-party AI providers, keeps data as long as reasonably necessary, and documents no training opt-out. Using the OpenHands LLM provider from the CLI may send usage metadata to All Hands AI. OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted): the docs say code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure. The same docs also list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance, a Replicated licence-verification component, and required outbound access to vendor endpoints. The chosen LLM provider's terms also apply.

suitability_notes.personal: Do not use OpenHands Cloud (Individual) for personal data: its privacy policy allows training on content and documents no opt-out. Self-host with a local model, or use self-hosted Enterprise with an LLM provider covered by an appropriate contract/DPA; check every ACP agent, MCP server and integration you enable.
suitability_notes.special: Only self-hosted open-source Agent Canvas/Agent Server on institution-controlled infrastructure with a local model server (Ollama only in local-only mode), all product telemetry disabled and no cloud LLM, Cloud backend or third-party ACP agent. Self-hosted OpenHands Enterprise needs extra checks: its documented install has licence verification, periodic usage metrics to the vendor and required outbound vendor endpoints, and no air-gapped install is documented. Confirm in the contract what leaves the environment before any special-category use. Cloud OpenHands and cloud LLM routes are not acceptable.

compliance: Customer-operated deployment is distinct from OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise licensing.

Enterprise docs state that self-hosted code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure, but the same docs list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance and required outbound vendor endpoints; neither covers the selected LLM provider.
No certification confirmed from first-party sources; the linked Vanta trust centre is not machine-readable (checked 2026-10-10).
pricing: Open Source (local): free. Individual (OpenHands Cloud): free, 1 user, up to 10 conversations per day per the plan comparison table; BYO key or OpenHands LLM provider billed pay-as-you-go at provider rates with no markup. Enterprise (SaaS or self-hosted in your VPC): custom pricing; a free 30-day self-hosted trial is documented.
academic: No academic discount on the pricing or Enterprise pages; the local open-source option is free.
use_cases: coding
software engineering automation
agentic task execution
scheduled and event-driven automations
CI/CD integration
data analysis
notes: The OpenHands/OpenHands repository is now Agent Canvas (MIT; README badge 'beta'), a self-hosted control centre that runs the OpenHands agent from the MIT Software Agent SDK and can also drive third-party ACP agents. The docs describe the CLI as feature-complete and maintained for stability; it sits with the Local GUI under 'Deprecated Projects'. Enterprise code (OpenHands/enterprise) is under the PolyForm Free Trial License 1.0.0, i.e. source-available, not open source. Active: releases v1.18.0 to v1.26.0 between 11 Sep and 8 Oct 2026. Check the licence of each repository you deploy.
tier_gate: personal data: self-hosted with a local model, or self-hosted Enterprise with a DPA-covered LLM provider (not OpenHands Cloud); special-category: self-hosted MIT Agent Canvas/Agent Server + local model + all telemetry off, no ACP agents

required_controls: Self-host the open-source Agent Canvas/Agent Server (local, Docker, VM or Kubernetes) on infrastructure the institution controls; do not add an OpenHands Cloud backend.

If OpenHands Enterprise is used instead: its documented install includes Replicated licence verification, periodic usage metrics and required outbound vendor endpoints, and no air-gapped install is documented. Obtain contractual confirmation of what is sent and restrict egress before special-category use.
Configure only a local model server (e.g. LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang) on that infrastructure; no cloud LLM provider and no OpenHands LLM provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Use the built-in OpenHands agent only; do not enable third-party ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode), which run their vendors' CLIs with their own LLM, tools and terms.

Disable product telemetry: AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry for the Canvas frontend; VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 so the launcher/Docker image do not set the default automation PostHog key; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 for Agent Server; and decline analytics consent.
Keep listeners on loopback or behind a strong LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY plus network access control; prefer the Docker sandbox runtime.
Enable only integrations and MCP servers that stay inside the institutional boundary; enforce egress filtering.

Deny or disable built-in web browsing, search and fetch tools; disable or centrally manage auto-update and version checks; point every model role at the local model server and keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env; verify the effective configuration; block egress at host or network level and verify it.
residual_risks: The agent executes shell commands with filesystem and network access; the no-sandbox install gives it full access to the host filesystem.
Conversation history, settings, secrets and optional completion logs (full prompts) persist on local disk and need institutional access and retention controls.
Telemetry is controlled separately for the Canvas frontend, the Agent Server and the automation service; verify actual egress after each upgrade.
Self-hosted Enterprise sends licence/usage metrics to the vendor; their content is not documented publicly.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost model URL alone does not guarantee local inference.
Local models can have limited functionality compared with frontier cloud models, which may push users toward cloud routes.
Frequent releases (several per month) and Agent Canvas beta status mean configuration must be re-checked after updates.

name: Jupyter AI
deployment: local-capable
model_backend: No agent ships by default. Built-in ACP personas (jupyter-ai-acp-client 0.3.x): Claude, Codex, Copilot, Goose, Kilo, Kiro, Mistral Vibe and OpenCode; each uses its own authentication, model configuration and data terms. The optional, experimental Jupyternaut persona and the optional %%ai magics call models through LiteLLM; the docs describe a local Ollama route (default 127.0.0.1:11434) and, for Jupyternaut, a self-hosted vLLM route. Customer-controlled inference needs that route or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent.
data_handling_note: Jupyter AI routes notebook context, attachments and tool calls to the selected persona; the ACP agent or Jupyternaut's model provider then applies its own retention and training terms. A local Jupyter server does not keep data local if the persona uses a cloud model. Chats are saved as .chat files in the workspace; Jupyternaut's persistent memory (local SQLite) is opt-in. The ACP client emits operational events to Jupyter Server's EventLogger, which records them only where an operator registers handlers; the code describes them as free of customer content and PII, though failure events carry error messages. Project Jupyter's policy says telemetry is opt-in and does not cover third-party hosted Jupyter.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-controlled model route (Jupyternaut with local Ollama or self-hosted vLLM, or a reviewed ACP agent with such inference), or separately approve the complete agent/provider route. Local JupyterLab alone does not keep notebook context local.
suitability_notes.special: Requires JupyterLab on institution-controlled infrastructure with local inference (experimental Jupyternaut with local Ollama/vLLM, or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent), isolated notebook execution and approved MCP integrations; a local notebook UI with a cloud agent does not qualify.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free and open source (BSD-3-Clause); costs come only from any connected agent subscription or cloud model provider
academic: free
use_cases: data analysis
coding
notebook AI assistant
agentic workflows in notebooks
multi-agent collaboration
notes: Notebook chat host for separately installed ACP coding agents, plus an optional experimental Jupyternaut persona whose future is under maintainer review (jupyter-ai#1618). Where context goes is set by the connected agent or model provider, wherever the notebook runs. v3.2.0 (3 Sep 2026) made real-time collaboration optional and fixed frontend tool calls running in every connected browser.

required_controls: Run JupyterLab on institution-controlled infrastructure with local inference only: the optional Jupyternaut persona pointed at a local Ollama/vLLM server, or a separately reviewed ACP agent configured for local models. Do not install cloud-backed ACP agents or providers; restrict Jupyternaut with JupyternautExtension.allowed_providers/allowed_models (the docs still show the older AiExtension prefix).

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Set LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True for Jupyternaut and magics, so LiteLLM does not fetch its model cost map from GitHub at import.

Keep Jupyter AI at v3.2.0 or later (frontend tool calls limited to the requesting browser; MCP server Host/Origin protection on by default), review .jupyter/mcp_settings.json, require tool-permission prompts, and isolate notebook execution.
residual_risks: Jupyternaut is documented as experimental, its docs are flagged out of date, and its future is under discussion; the ACP route depends on each agent's own local-model support and policies.

An institution-hosted Ollama/vLLM endpoint reached via api_base needs a separate network and access review; other outbound behaviour of LiteLLM and its dependencies beyond the cost-map fetch was not reviewed, so air-gapped operation is unverified.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

Chat files, opt-in Jupyternaut memory, Jupyternaut API keys saved to a .env file, logs, tools and MCP integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls, especially on shared JupyterHub servers.

name: Julius AI
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Julius models (default): Lite on all plans, the standard and Max variants on paid plans, Ultra on the Max plan and above. Third-party general models from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Meta and Moonshot AI (docs: paid plans; the pricing comparison table gives Plus only a subset and Pro and above all models). Image generation uses an OpenAI image model; video generation supports a Seedance model (changelog 2026-08-07); the text-to-speech provider is not named. The lineup changes often (swaps on 2026-09-22, 09-29 and 10-01). The public subprocessor list names Anthropic and OpenAI but not xAI, Meta, Moonshot AI or the video-model provider.
data_handling_note: Julius states that user data is never used to train models, internally or externally, and that its AI providers are contractually bound not to train on it (docs, privacy policy updated 2026-07-01, ToS updated 2026-03-06). The ToS also allows Julius to collect and use inputs and outputs to maintain, improve, modify and develop its AI features and grants Julius a broad licence to uploaded content; it states that the terms of an executed DPA apply to customer personal data processed on the customer's behalf (the DPA text is not public). The docs state that all data is stored and processed in the US; the privacy policy (s.10) allows personal information to be transferred to and stored in other countries by service providers, and the trust-centre subprocessor list gives no processing location for Raindrop. Listed subprocessors include AWS and Google Cloud (user storage), E2B (code sandbox; may process or store workspace content), Raindrop (customer prompts, AI responses, agent traces), and PostHog and Sentry. File retention statements conflict: the Files docs say Free-plan files are retained for up to 1 h of inactivity and paid-plan files remain available for up to 7 days of inactivity, while the pricing page lists permanent file storage on paid plans. The privacy policy offers a DPA with standard contractual clauses (the former public DPA URL returns 404), says Julius will delete information accessible to it within seven business days of an account-cancellation and deletion request, subject to legally required retention (s.11), and asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data. No public HIPAA BAA or product-level ZDR is documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only under an executed institutional DPA (offered via the privacy policy; plan eligibility is not stated publicly, so confirm with the vendor) that covers processing locations and international transfers, the listed subprocessors (including Raindrop, which receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces), retention and deletion, and that limits the ToS clause allowing inputs/outputs to be used to improve AI features. Do not publish artifacts or share conversation replay links; anyone with such a link can view them. A no-training statement alone does not authorize personal-data processing.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only service: inference, code execution and storage run on vendor and third-party infrastructure (US per the docs; the privacy policy permits transfers to service providers in other countries); no self-hosted, on-premises or customer-controlled deployment is documented, and the privacy policy asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data. Not appropriate under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II stated on security and pricing pages; trust centre shows SOC 2 (Type 2) as compliant, report available on request; verify scope before procurement

TX-RAMP stated on the security page (level not stated there); the trust centre lists a public 'TX-RAMP Level 2 Certification' document (not opened); Texas state programme, not relevant to GDPR or health-data approval
pricing: Free (daily credits); Plus $20 monthly or $16/month billed annually; Pro $45/$37; Max $200/$166; Business $450/$375 (up to 50 members); Enterprise custom. Monthly credits: Plus 2,000, Pro 5,000, Max 25,000, Business 60,000; unused credits do not roll over and top-ups are not offered. The pricing page has no Ultra or Growth plan cards (the Business card refers only to 'Everything in Ultra'), but the credits help page lists Ultra ($500, 70,000 credits) and Growth 1-4 ($750-$5,000; 100,000-850,000 credits).
academic: No student or educator discount appears on the pricing page, the education use-case page or the docs FAQ (which mentions startup pricing only). The docs describe redeeming institutional codes supplied by an instructor or workplace; their terms are not public.
use_cases: natural language data analysis
data visualization
Python/R code execution in a cloud sandbox (code visible and copyable)
database querying (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Supabase)
scheduled/automated reports
slide/presentation generation
Excel/CSV/PDF analysis
website/web app and image/video generation (AI workspace features)
notes: Cloud AI workspace (data analysis with Python/R plus presentations, reports, websites, images and video) with a public no-training commitment. Material boundaries: US processing and storage per the docs (the privacy policy permits transfers to service providers in other countries); the ToS allows inputs/outputs to be used to improve AI features; a listed observability subprocessor receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces; first-party sources conflict on paid-plan file retention; published artifacts and conversation replay links are viewable by anyone with the link. A DPA is offered via the privacy policy, but no public DPA text or HIPAA BAA was found.
tier_gate: Personal data only under an executed DPA (offered via the privacy policy; plan eligibility not stated publicly, so confirm with the vendor). Enterprise (custom) adds SSO, audit logging and fine-grained RBAC; the pricing table shows audit logs as Enterprise-only. Verify file retention (docs: 7 days of inactivity; pricing: permanent storage) and the ToS improvement-use clause in the contract.

residual_risks: Cloud-only: inference, code execution and storage run on vendor and third-party infrastructure (US per docs; privacy policy permits transfers to other countries), outside customer-controlled infrastructure.
Prompts and outputs pass to multiple third-party model providers and subprocessors, including an observability service that receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces.
The privacy policy asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data; no public HIPAA BAA or self-hosted option is documented.

name: Hex
deployment: cloud (Hex-operated on AWS: US multi-tenant; EU multi-tenant on Team by contract or on Enterprise; HIPAA and single-tenant stacks as Enterprise add-ons, still run by Hex)
model_backend: Hosted Anthropic and OpenAI models by default; models Hex hosts itself (e.g. Kimi 2.7, on US infrastructure; FAQ names Baseten hosting for certain features) and Hex-run typeahead models; the subprocessor list also names Google, Modal and Parallel as AI services; Grok 4.6 added to the model picker 2026-09-23 (serving route not documented; no xAI entry on the subprocessor list of 2026-08-04). Enterprise BYOK: Anthropic or OpenAI direct, or Claude models via AWS Bedrock or Google GEAP, optionally through a wire-compatible gateway.
data_handling_note: Self-serve plans (Community, Professional, Team not under an Order Form; ToS last modified 2026-05-14): unless the customer opts out in Settings > AI & agents, Hex may use AI inputs and outputs to develop, improve and evaluate its services. Enterprise (Hex Service Agreement for Order Forms from 2026-06-24): neither Hex nor its AI providers use Customer Data to train, improve or develop AI models, except models kept for that customer only; the previous Enterprise version (Feb 2025 to Jun 2026) only excluded training models offered to other parties. Hex's FAQ adds that staff may review AI prompts and related project data when needed to fix bugs or improve AI features. LLM providers do not train and run under zero data retention by default; an Admin toggle enables models that require provider safety retention (Anthropic: 30 days for Fable 5; Fable 5.1, added 2026-09-23, also needs the toggle). Product-level storage is separate: prompts carry project code, cell outputs, schema and table/column names; cell outputs are stored indefinitely unless custom retention (7-90 days, select Enterprise plans) is enabled; schema embeddings (OpenAI Ada) sit in a vector database on Hex infrastructure. The subprocessor list gives Anthropic's processing location as USA, not the deployment region. BYOK (Enterprise) reroutes third-party inference only: typeahead still runs on Hex-run models, and Hex-hosted models such as Kimi are unavailable while BYOK is on.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Team or Enterprise with the DPA (EU/UK/Swiss transfers rely on Hex's Data Privacy Framework certification, with SCCs as fallback) and the EU stack where residency matters (Team: by contract). The EU stack does not keep all AI processing in the EU: the subprocessor list gives Anthropic and Parallel processing as USA, and Kimi runs on US infrastructure. On self-serve plans switch off AI-session improvement use, which is on by default; Enterprise Order Forms from 2026-06-24 exclude it contractually (check which agreement version an older contract uses). Keep 'Allow data retention for specific models' off, mark connections holding personal data as Sensitive (this governs Slack, MCP, API and CLI access only; MCP/API/CLI access to them is off by default), and consider disabling agent web search. Confirm with Hex how Grok 4.6 and Kimi 2.7 are covered by the subprocessor list and DPA before personal data reaches them.
suitability_notes.special: Every documented route, including the HIPAA add-on, single-tenant and BYOK, keeps processing on Hex-operated cloud, with inference at third-party or Hex-hosted model providers (under BYOK, Claude can be served from the customer's Bedrock/GEAP account, but typeahead, storage and orchestration stay with Hex). The DPA lists no permitted sensitive-data categories unless agreed in writing, and the terms treat genetic data and health data outside a BAA as At-Risk Data at the customer's risk. A BAA does not create a customer-controlled boundary, so Hex does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II and annual HIPAA audit stated by Hex; Trust Center shows SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI, GDPR, CCPA and EU-US/UK-US/Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework badges (reports access-gated)
HIPAA (US customers): PHI only after a BAA and, on Enterprise, a HIPAA environment on the order form; Hex states a BAA with its LLM providers
GDPR DPA (last modified 2026-06-01): EU/UK/Swiss transfers rely on Hex's Data Privacy Framework certification, with SCCs as fallback; current contract, deployment and add-on scope must be checked
pricing: Community (free) - Professional ($36/editor/month) - Team ($75/editor/month, 14-day free trial) - Enterprise (custom). AI use is metered in credits: monthly per-seat grants (Community 5, Professional 30, Team editor 40 / explorer 10; Enterprise per order form) plus purchasable add-on credits. Academic: Professional plan free for students and educators at universities and bootcamps (contact support@hex.tech); discounted program for qualified non-profits.
academic: Students and educators at universities and bootcamps can get the Professional plan free (contact support@hex.tech). Professional runs under the self-serve terms, so the AI-session improvement opt-out has to be set; verify eligibility and terms with Hex.
use_cases: collaborative data analysis
SQL/Python notebooks
AI-assisted code and query generation
data app publishing
warehouse-native analytics
notes: Collaborative cloud analytics platform positioned as an 'AI Analytics Platform'. Hex documents that its AI features were formerly called Hex Magic; the agent suite now covers the Notebook Agent, Threads, Chat with App, the Modeling Agent and Generative Apps (beta). The Hex agent is on Professional and above, with a trial on Community; per-feature availability varies by plan. Since September: six models added on 2026-09-23 (including Grok 4.6 and Fable 5.1), a 'Skip approvals' agent mode (2026-09-15) and project create/edit via the Hex MCP server. Provider ZDR does not mean Hex deletes or never uses AI-session data; plan terms, opt-out and contract scope must be checked.
tier_gate: Team/Enterprise + DPA, AI-session improvement opt-out (self-serve plans) and appropriate data stack

residual_risks: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

Hex's terms (self-serve ToS s7.3b; Enterprise agreement s7.3.3) treat genetic data and health-related data not governed by a BAA as At-Risk Data at the customer's risk, and DPA Annex 1 lists no permitted sensitive-data categories unless provided in writing.
The subprocessor list (last modified 2026-08-04) gives USA as Anthropic's location of processing, so an EU-stack workspace still sends Anthropic-model inference to the USA.

name: Kiro
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Amazon Bedrock-hosted models chosen in Kiro: the Auto router, Anthropic Claude models, OpenAI GPT-5.6 tiers (experimental, Global inference scope) and open-weight models (e.g., DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen). Claude Fable 5.1 is an Enterprise-only Preview served from us-east-1. The list and credit multipliers change; AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog. No local or customer-hosted model endpoint is documented.
data_handling_note: Free Tier and individual subscribers (paid accounts using GitHub/Google social login or AWS Builder ID): content may be used for service improvement, including model training, and client telemetry is collected unless opted out (IDE, CLI and Web each have their own opt-out); their content is stored in us-east-1, and Free Tier inputs may also be kept up to 60 days for abuse detection. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center, Okta or Microsoft Entra ID): content is not used for service improvement and users are auto-opted out of telemetry/content collection (administrators control user-activity telemetry); content may be stored in the profile Region (commercial: us-east-1 or eu-central-1) to operate the service, and admin-enabled IDE/CLI prompt logs and activity reports go to a customer-selected S3 bucket. Cloud sessions (Kiro Web/Mobile, kiro-cli --cloud) keep conversation history, repositories and sandbox files in the cloud, in us-east-1 only for Identity Center organizations; Kiro Web data-collection preferences are set by each user. All users: operational signals may be collected and Bedrock abuse detection applies; OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic is kept up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 Preview traffic (Enterprise only) is kept up to 30 days, and AWS may review classifier-flagged traffic by hand. Inference Region can differ from storage Region. Local IDE/CLI/Crew execution does not make inference local.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Kiro Enterprise profile (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) under institutional AWS terms; paid social-login, Builder ID and Students accounts are not the Enterprise route. For EU data, use a Frankfurt profile. Model governance is off by default (all models allowed): restrict Global-scope (GPT-5.6) and Preview (Claude Fable 5.1: us-east-1 only, all traffic retained up to 30 days) models, and if the approved list must bind, block Auto and set an approved default model (Auto can route to models outside the list). Keep Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off unless separately assessed: cloud sessions run in us-east-1 only for Identity Center organizations, and model governance and customer-managed keys do not apply to Kiro Web. Confirm prompt-logging and retention settings.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud inference only (Amazon Bedrock); local IDE, CLI or Crew clients do not change this. HIPAA eligibility (AWS lists Kiro excluding Kiro Web) or contractual controls do not satisfy this index's controlled-infrastructure requirement.

compliance: HIPAA eligible for Kiro IDE and CLI; AWS's HIPAA-eligible list names Kiro excluding Kiro Web. PHI use requires an AWS BAA; account, Region and contract scope still apply. Coverage of cloud sessions started from the IDE or CLI is not stated.

Kiro docs state Kiro is in scope of AWS's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification; AWS's ISO services-in-scope list shows Kiro excluding Fable. AWS Artifact reports require Builder ID or IAM Identity Center sign-in.
pricing: Free: 50 credits/month; Pro $20/user/month: 1,000; Pro+ $40: 2,000; Pro Max $100: 5,000; Power $200: 10,000 (excluding taxes). Add-on credits are $0.04 each on individual paid plans. Enterprise uses the same paid tiers billed through AWS, with optional admin-enabled overages at $0.04/credit and no Free tier. AWS GovCloud (US) pricing is about 20% higher.
academic: Kiro for Students gives verified students (18+) at listed universities 1,000 credits/month free for one year (SheerID check; GitHub, Google or Builder ID sign-in with a university email; no add-on credits), then reverts to Free. No Czech institution appeared in the eligible-school list in the page HTML on 2026-10-10. Student accounts are not Enterprise accounts; the Students FAQ points to the training opt-out, so content may be used for service improvement unless the student opts out. Kiro does not state whether Students-tier users count as individual subscribers.
use_cases: Spec-driven agentic software development (requirements.md or bugfix.md -> design.md -> tasks.md -> code)
Background coding in cloud sessions (Kiro Web/Mobile, attachable from IDE/CLI) with pull-request delivery via GitHub/GitLab
Terminal and CI/CD automation via CLI headless mode (e.g., automated code reviews, test generation)
AWS-native development via Powers (e.g., Lambda, CDK/CloudFormation, ECS, Bedrock, HealthOmics)
Multi-tool integration via MCP and Powers (e.g., Figma, Postman, Datadog, Terraform)
Property-based testing of implementations against specs (IDE)
Parallel sub-agents and Workflows across large codebases
Persistent, scheduled agent work on own hardware via Kiro Crew (inference still via Kiro)
notes: Kiro IDE and CLI plus Web, Mobile (iOS, Preview) and Crew surfaces; models served through Kiro run on Amazon Bedrock cloud inference. The Enterprise route excludes content from service improvement, but operational storage, abuse-detection retention and model-specific routing remain. Kiro Web runs in us-east-1 only, without model governance or customer-managed keys, and AWS's HIPAA-eligible listing excludes Kiro Web. Kiro Crew is an Apache-2.0 runtime on the user's hardware that uses Kiro CLI cloud inference by default (other agent backends are a Developer Mode preview). Paid individual status is not equivalent to Enterprise.
tier_gate: Kiro Enterprise profile (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) under institutional AWS terms, with model governance restricting Global-scope and Preview models (block Auto if the approved list must bind) and Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off or assessed separately; operational storage and model-specific abuse retention still apply

residual_risks: Cloud inference only. HIPAA eligibility or contractual controls do not satisfy this index's controlled-infrastructure requirement.

name: Zed
deployment: local-capable
model_backend: Separate request paths: Zed-hosted models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google; Pro, Student, Business), provider API keys, existing subscriptions, gateways (e.g. OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vercel), local or self-hosted models (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible servers), External Agents via ACP, and Terminal Threads running agent CLIs. Edit prediction has its own provider setting; the default is Zed-hosted Zeta.
data_handling_note: Zed does not retain prompts or code context by default; it stores AI data only when a user rates a response or opts into Edit Prediction training data (open-source projects only). Defaults are hosted: the default agent provider is Zed-hosted and the default edit-prediction provider is hosted Zeta (both need sign-in). Zed-hosted models: provider agreements prohibit training and require ZDR, except provider safety retention for designated Covered Models (Anthropic: at least 30 days); Zed's default settings withhold hosted requests to non-ZDR Anthropic models until the user consents. Zed's subprocessor list states that hosted summarization or commit-message requests may reach Anthropic, Google or OpenAI even when another model is selected. BYOK, subscriptions, gateways, External Agents, Terminal Threads and third-party edit prediction follow their own terms. Client telemetry (diagnostics, metrics) is on by default and can be disabled; server-side telemetry is collected whenever hosted AI or collaboration is used.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model, or a hosted/BYOK route the institution has approved. A DPA is available on request (Zed acts as processor for Zed Business). Hosted Zed models send prompts and code context to US-hosted providers under no-training/ZDR commitments, with provider safety retention for Covered Models.
suitability_notes.special: Only the fully local route qualifies: Zed Agent, all feature-specific models and edit prediction on Ollama (in local-only mode), llama.cpp, LM Studio or a self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure that forwards nothing to external providers, signed out of Zed, telemetry off. Hosted Zed/provider models are not acceptable; Zed's Terms also bar HIPAA PHI from Customer Data sent to its hosted Service.

compliance: GDPR rights and EEA/UK complaint route in Privacy Policy (last updated 2026-06-09); DPA available on request (processor role for Zed Business)
Services hosted in the US; EEA/UK transfers under Standard Contractual Clauses
SOC 2 Type 1 in progress, not certified
Terms (last updated 2026-03-02) prohibit HIPAA PHI in Customer Data submitted to the hosted Service
pricing: Personal $0: unlimited use with own API keys or External Agents. Hosted Zeta edit predictions: the pricing page still lists 2,000 accepted per month, but Zed's merged PR #65258 (2026-10-07) states the Free plan no longer includes hosted edit predictions from 7 October 2026 (other providers or a local model remain usable). Pro $10/month with $5 monthly hosted-model token credit, overage at provider list price +10%, 14-day trial; Business $30/seat/month, no bundled AI credit, org-wide AI and data-sharing controls, SSO/SAML/SCIM not yet available. Student plan separately documented.
academic: Student plan: free for 12 months for verified university students (18+, GitHub account older than 30 days, university email); $10/month token credit with usage capped at that amount, unlimited edit predictions; excludes Claude Fable, Claude Opus, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.5 pro and GPT-5.4 pro (list as of 2026-10-10).
use_cases: AI-assisted code editing with agentic multi-file editing
Parallel agent threads for simultaneous tasks across a project
Local/private coding with Ollama, llama.cpp or LM Studio (data stays on machine only when every AI path is local)
BYO API key setup for privacy-conscious researchers
Edit prediction via open-weight Zeta model (self-hostable)
MCP server integration for extended tool access
Terminal Threads for running Claude Code or Amp as sidebar agents
Git commit message generation
Multiplayer real-time collaboration
notes: Desktop editor with hosted, BYOK, gateway and fully local model routes. Licence scope (README): primarily GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components where marked; open-core reflects the open client plus Zed-hosted services. Defaults point to hosted services (Zed-hosted agent model, hosted Zeta edit prediction, client telemetry on), so the local route needs explicit configuration; special-category suitability applies only to that route. SOC 2 Type 1 is in progress, not achieved. Delta, Zed Industries' separate multiplayer agent environment (public beta since 2026-09-16), is not covered by this record.
tier_gate: fully local route (local models for agent, feature models and edit prediction; signed out of Zed) for special-category data; Business for org-enforced data-sharing controls, which cover Zed-hosted services only

required_controls: Point Zed Agent and every feature-specific model (inline assistant, commit message, thread summary, compaction, subagent) to a local or self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers.

Stay signed out of Zed (sign-in is needed only for collaboration and Zed-hosted LLM features), so no Zed-hosted model or hosted edit prediction is used; hosted summarization and commit-message requests can reach cloud providers even when another model is selected.
Set edit prediction to a local provider (Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server) or to none; the default provider is hosted Zeta.

If Ollama serves any model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable client telemetry (diagnostics and metrics), do not rate responses or opt into Edit Prediction training data, and leave collaboration unused.
Configure or avoid External Agents, Terminal Threads, MCP servers, gateways and extensions separately; Zed settings and Business controls do not govern them.
Keep Zed Agent sandboxing on (Linux needs bwrap; Windows needs WSL) and use tool permissions to restrict terminal and fetch network egress.
residual_risks: Defaults point to hosted services (Zed-hosted agent model, hosted Zeta edit prediction, client telemetry on); signing in or a missed setting can re-enable cloud egress.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so pointing Zed at local Ollama alone does not show that inference stays local.
External Agents, Terminal Threads, MCP servers, extensions and agent fetch/terminal tools run under their own configuration and can send data off-machine.
Sandboxing covers only the Zed Agent terminal and fetch tools and may be weaker on Windows.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Amp
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Amp-managed routing per mode and subagent; the current /modes page lists Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini and GLM models, and routing changes over time. Per the security page, Amp-managed inference runs on Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, Meta, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex), Amazon Bedrock, Baseten and Fireworks (US servers). Customer connections: provider API keys (BYOK); cloud platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Agent Platform, which Amp accesses with its own federated identity; routers/gateways and Custom URL endpoints (documented as needing to be reachable from Amp); and linked ChatGPT or Grok subscriptions. A Claude Pro/Max plan is used only by the Claude Code mode, which runs the Claude Agent SDK in the orb or, on a runner, with that machine's Claude login. Some system models (e.g. image generation) are not moved by tuning.
data_handling_note: Training: per Amp's security page, Amp and its subprocessors do not train on user data unless the user opts in; in a workspace, opting in needs admin approval, and Enterprise workspaces cannot enable it. Provider retention: Minimal Data Retention (MDR) is available to all users on Amp-managed provider connections paid with Amp credits. Under MDR, providers keep prompts/responses only to return a response, except safety/abuse data, longer model- or feature-specific retention (docs: up to 30 days), short-lived cached artifacts and legal requirements; some models and features are not eligible for MDR (flagged in-product). Amp's docs state Anthropic requires data retention for Claude Fable models, which the default high (Oracle) and ultra (agent) routing currently uses. Only the Enterprise Terms define ZDR contractually: ZDR for models and features Amp's documentation lists as eligible, MDR otherwise; workspace-wide ZDR applies only if the customer enables a workspace setting restricting selection to eligible models, where offered (the public docs do not describe that setting). The pricing FAQ and a 13 Sep 2026 post say the zero and minimal data retention policy covers all users and workspaces. BYOK, cloud-platform, gateway and linked subscriptions (ChatGPT, Grok; Claude Pro/Max in Claude Code mode) follow that provider account's retention and training terms. Product retention (not covered by MDR): Amp stores threads (messages, responses, code snippets, tool results, attachments), user information and telemetry in a multi-tenant Google Cloud project in the US. Explicitly deleted threads are removed within 30 days; Enterprise workspace threads stay with the workspace after a user leaves until the contract ends; configurable thread retention is offered to Enterprise on request. Paused orb filesystems and memory are stored until the thread is deleted; project snapshots are reused for up to 72 hours, and a replaced snapshot is deleted only after all orbs created from it are deleted. The privacy policy (last modified 10 Sep 2026) describes event analytics and a server ping; no telemetry opt-out was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Only on an Enterprise contract with a signed DPA (no public DPA found; the Trust Center is gated) and after accepting US storage of thread data (SCC-based transfers per the privacy policy). Use Amp-managed or institution-held model connections, not linked consumer subscriptions. MDR is not end-to-end deletion: confirm retention for the selected models (e.g. Claude Fable) and set thread deletion/retention terms.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate. Amp's Terms say the Services are not designed to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI and users must not use them to store it; Amp is not a HIPAA Business Associate. There is no self-hosted deployment. Local runners move execution only: Amp still stores the thread in its US cloud, and in Amp's own modes inference is routed through Amp Server (Claude Code mode instead uses the linked or runner-local Claude consumer plan).

compliance: Security page states SOC 2 Type II certification and annual penetration testing; reports are available on request through a gated Trust Center (scope not reviewed).
Terms: the Services are not designed for Sensitive Data (GDPR Art. 9 special categories, HIPAA PHI, government IDs, financial account data, credentials) and Amp is not a HIPAA Business Associate.
No public DPA found; the privacy policy names SCCs or consent for EEA/UK/Swiss transfers. An enterprise DPA and audit-report scope must match the selected service.
pricing: Hobby: free; orbs pay-as-you-go, or own runners free; BYOK and linked subscriptions carry no Amp token fee; Amp-served inference uses paid credits at provider API prices without markup. Individual: Megawatt $20/month and Gigawatt $200/month, each including orb time and Amp credits. Teams: no extra workspace charge; members can be on Hobby, Megawatt or Gigawatt; SAML/OIDC SSO needs at least one paid member. Enterprise: custom pricing, pooled credits only; BYOK token fees may apply (waived on all other tiers). Purchased credits expire after 12 months.
academic: Education discount: students and teachers can get Megawatt for $10/month (half the $20 price) via ampcode.com/edu after signing in and filling in a form. Eligibility criteria (e.g. whether research staff qualify) are not stated publicly.
use_cases: Agentic software development in local repositories or cloud orbs
Multi-platform agent management (start in CLI, web or iOS; monitor and continue from another client)
Running agents on your own machines via runners, including shared workspace runners (e.g. GPU boxes)
Parallel subagent workloads
Code review and diff staging
MCP server integration for custom tooling
Long-running autonomous coding tasks with context compaction
notes: Web app, macOS/iOS apps and CLI share one cloud thread store. Work runs in Amp cloud orbs (e2b compute), locally in the CLI, or on the user's own runners (including the Mac app and runners shared with a workspace); in every case Amp stores the thread in its cloud, and Amp's own modes route inference through Amp Server (Claude Code mode runs the Claude Agent SDK under the user's Claude plan). Amp states it does not offer self-hosted deployments. The former /manual URL now redirects to /docs. The CLI package licence notice still names Sourcegraph Inc., while the Terms and privacy policy name Amp Frontier Corporation.
tier_gate: Enterprise (training cannot be enabled; ZDR for eligible models under the Enterprise Terms, MDR otherwise; Allowed Models control (rolling out) and configurable thread retention on request) + confirm signed DPA and retention terms; never special-category data (prohibited by Terms)

residual_risks: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.
Amp offers no self-hosted deployment: threads and telemetry are stored in Amp's US cloud, and even customer-held endpoints are called from Amp's servers.
Amp's Terms prohibit using the Services to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI; Amp is not a HIPAA Business Associate.

name: Sourcegraph Cody
deployment: cloud / self-hostable / on-prem
model_backend: Sourcegraph Model Provider (Cody Gateway) gives Enterprise instances hosted Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models. It is configured by default on Sourcegraph Cloud; self-hosted customers confirm access with their account manager. Autocomplete and Smart Apply models include Fireworks-hosted models (US Iowa). Self-hosted instances can instead configure BYOK providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini/Vertex, Fireworks), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Hugging Face TGI; the docs say BYOK with managed services is supported only on self-hosted instances. The model list changes often; check the current supported-models page and the instance's modelConfiguration.
data_handling_note: Enterprise only. The Cody FAQ states Sourcegraph will not train on Enterprise customers' data; the ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) allows fine-tuning only if enabled for the instance and says Partner LLMs reached through Sourcegraph keep zero retention (temporary abuse/harm retention excepted) and do not train. Product-level retention is separate: the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) lists maintaining AI conversation history during the subscription term as a processing purpose; after expiry Sourcegraph returns or deletes data on the customer's instruction, and without an instruction within 60 days deletes all Customer Personal Data, including AI conversation data, within 90 days. The partner zero-retention commitment applies only to access through Sourcegraph's Partner LLMs, so with BYOK the customer's own provider agreement sets retention. The AI Terms (2026-06-12) apply only to agreements signed before 2024-02-15 or Order Forms that incorporate them; the Cody notice (2024-02-15) applies only to older Cody licences. Self-hosted instances send aggregated pings (no code, but including the installer/admin email, instance URL and IP) and license verification checks, and export telemetry events (numeric metadata, anonymized user IDs) to Sourcegraph by default.

suitability_notes.personal: Requires an Enterprise Order Form and the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05; EEA/UK transfer terms). The subprocessor list names Anthropic, Fireworks AI and Google (all USA) for AI queries and code snippets. OpenAI is listed only for embeddings when the customer enables them. Amp (USA) is listed for error data that can include customer code. Confirm which AI terms the Order Form incorporates, the model routing (Cody Gateway vs BYOK), conversation-history retention and deletion on request. Context Filters can restrict which repositories Cody sends as context. BYOK to a cloud model is still an external processor. Agentic context fetching is on by default and its review step defaults to Gemini 2.5 Flash (fallback Claude Haiku or GPT 4.1 mini), so a Claude-only chat setup can still send context to Google or OpenAI; include it in the routing check. The subprocessor page says self-hosted personal data is processed only when shared for support, but self-hosted instances using Cody Gateway still send prompts and code snippets to the LLM providers.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate. The ToS, which also covers self-hosted Software, says the product is not designed to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI and must not be used to store it; the DPA marks special-category data as not processed. Default routing also sends code snippets to cloud LLMs, and no first-party source documents an end-to-end deployment with inference on customer-controlled infrastructure.

compliance: SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 listed on the Sourcegraph Security Portal; reports are access-gated and Cody/AI-feature scope is not confirmed
Standard DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) with EEA/UK restricted-transfer terms
ToS: Sourcegraph is not a HIPAA Business Associate; GDPR Art. 9 special-category data excluded
Applicable Order Form and AI terms require confirmation
pricing: Sourcegraph Enterprise only: the pricing page lists a $16K minimum annual contract that includes credits for AI features and scales with team size; contact sales. The pricing page does not name Cody. Cody access on Free, Pro and Enterprise Starter ended 2025-07-23.
academic: No published academic or student discount. Cody is available only with Sourcegraph Enterprise ($16K minimum annual contract on the pricing page). The pricing FAQ offers sales-led trials with credits; contact sales about institutional pricing.
use_cases: Multi-repo codebase understanding and architecture queries
AI chat, inline edit, and autocomplete in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio (experimental)
Context-aware code generation using Sourcegraph Search context from local and remote repositories
Automated prompt workflows (custom Prompts feature)
Debug, explain, and refactor code with enterprise codebase context
Run suggested terminal commands from chat; agentic terminal context is experimental and off by default on Enterprise
Large-scale research or bioinformatics pipelines with complex cross-repo dependencies
notes: Active, Enterprise-only. Sourcegraph 8.0 (2026-09-17) added a supported Cody model. The Cody FAQ still carries its 2025 line that Sourcegraph is fully committed to Cody Enterprise, but its 2026-10-05 edit removed the longer sunset section, including the statement that Cody Enterprise will be actively supported, developed and maintained. The VS Code and JetBrains extensions were last released on 2026-06-17. Since Sourcegraph 7.0 (2026-02-25), Deep Search replaces Cody in the browser for Deep Search customers; the editor extensions are unaffected. Current AI use is governed by the Sourcegraph ToS and DPA. The AI Terms apply only to pre-2024-02-15 agreements or Order Forms that incorporate them, and the Cody notice (last modified 2024-02-15) only to older Cody licences. The model-provider docs nonetheless say the AI Terms apply to all Model Provider use. The Ollama local-model page is scoped to the discontinued Free/Pro plans. The extension package ships an Apache-2.0 licence file, but the client source repository is no longer public (an archived 2025 snapshot remains) and the required Sourcegraph Enterprise server is proprietary.
tier_gate: current Enterprise contract + DPA + verified model routing

residual_risks: The ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) excludes GDPR Art. 9 special-category data and HIPAA PHI for hosted Services and self-hosted Software; the DPA (2026-10-05) marks special-category data as not processed.
