suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.

compliance: Contract-, cloud-, region-, and compliance-profile dependent; verify exact Databricks service scope
HIPAA requires the compliance security profile and an active BAA with Databricks; Genie Code and Genie Code Agent Mode are listed in the HIPAA regional feature-support table (AWS)
Designated Service under Databricks Geos: content is processed in the workspace Geo unless cross-Geo processing is enabled
pricing: Pay-as-you-go since 2026-07-08. Each user (service principals excluded) gets 150 DBUs of free Genie LLM usage per month; Genie compute (e.g. SQL Serverless) is billed separately. Usage above the allowance is billed in DBUs under the Serverless Real-Time Inference SKU; the pricing page's example is 150 DBUs = $10.50 in US East, and the dollar equivalent varies by region. A 25% promotional discount applies to billed Genie usage until 2027-01-31. Genie Code CLI (Beta) is billed as Unity Gateway model usage, not under Genie pricing.
academic: No research discount or trial-credit amount is asserted. Databricks Free Edition (no cost, quota-limited, non-commercial) includes Genie Code but lacks compliance enforcement, SSO and security customisation, so it suits learning with non-sensitive data only. Institutional programmes require current vendor confirmation.
use_cases: Autonomous multi-step data pipeline engineering (Lakeflow)
Exploratory data analysis and model training in notebooks
AI/BI dashboard generation and analysis
SQL query building and optimization in SQL Editor
Agentic debugging of pipeline failures and errors
Scheduled autonomous data operations (overnight jobs, pipeline summarization)
GenAI application debugging and evaluation in MLflow
Document processing pipelines (parse, classify, extract) from unstructured files
notes: Cloud data-platform agent in the Databricks workspace (notebooks, SQL editor, Lakeflow, dashboards, MLflow). Chat history and notebook/control-plane content are kept separately from partner-model retention; automatic cross-session memory is also kept by Databricks (storage location and retention period not documented; users can ask Genie Code to forget or delete memories). Agent mode reads data samples and cell outputs and, on first use, defaults to classifier-based auto-approve, which Databricks says is not a security boundary; scheduled tasks always auto-approve. It can also reach MCP servers, native SaaS connectors and (Beta, admin-enabled) web search. For research data, set 'Ask first' and scope permissions narrowly. Genie Code CLI (Beta, Databricks License) adds a local terminal client with cloud inference.
tier_gate: Full (non-Free-Edition) Databricks account under an appropriate contract; Agent mode needs partner-powered AI features and a supported Geo; regulated data needs the compliance security profile (plus an active BAA for PHI) and workspace governance

residual_risks: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.
Genie Code CLI (Beta) runs locally, but prompts and any file content it reads are processed by Databricks-hosted inference via Unity Gateway; it is not a local-inference route.

name: Posit AI Pass / Posit Assistant
deployment: Hosted model service (Posit AI Pass) used from a local client in RStudio, Positron or the pa terminal; local-capable with Ollama/LM Studio; self-managed Posit Workbench with Preview admin provider controls
model_backend: Posit AI Pass: Anthropic Claude models (ZDR agreement) plus open-weights GLM and Kimi models served through Baseten; Next Edit Suggestions use Posit-hosted models. The lineup changes (Gemma 4 26B retired September 2026); the in-app model picker is authoritative. Own-provider routes include Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry and others (some Preview); local Ollama and LM Studio; custom OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic endpoints are Preview.
data_handling_note: Posit AI Pass: training on user Content is opt-in at sign-up (Help Improve Posit AI). Opt-in trace data may be used for up to 5 years to train models and improve the service. Opted-out accounts: Posit keeps basic operational data, excluding prompts and responses, for 30 days and does not use it for training or improvement (FAQ). The Service Terms (1 Oct 2026) state that Posit will use Content to provide, maintain, develop, train and improve Posit AI; their Opting Out clause limits training of Posit's models to accounts that opt in. First-party pages disagree on ZDR scope. The FAQ, models page and Responsible Use Policy say every AI Pass model is covered (Anthropic for Claude; Baseten for GLM/Kimi). The Service Terms say some, not all, models, and the product page says select models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models. Provider ZDR does not remove Posit's own retention. With own-provider or local Ollama/LM Studio routes, Positron documentation states that Posit receives no AI traffic, and the chosen provider's terms apply.

suitability_notes.personal: AI Pass route: leave trace collection off and review the click-through Service Terms (no AI Pass DPA found). The FAQ and the Service Terms disagree on ZDR scope. Alternatively, use an institution-approved provider agreement or a local model.
suitability_notes.special: Only Posit Assistant with an Ollama (in local-only mode) or LM Studio model server on institution-controlled hardware qualifies; on Workbench, enforce it with ai-providers-enforced. Cloud providers do not qualify, including Workbench managed-credential routes (Amazon Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex, Microsoft Foundry). Posit AI Pass, NES, web search and remote MCP servers must be off. The AI Pass Service Terms prohibit health data.

compliance: Posit AI Pass Service Terms and Responsible Use Policy (both 1 Oct 2026) prohibit inputting health information, financial information, government ID numbers or other highly sensitive data.

ZDR scope conflict: the FAQ, models page and Responsible Use Policy say every AI Pass model is covered; the Service Terms say some, not all, and the product page says select models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models under Posit's own retention terms.

AI Pass uses individual click-through terms (Massachusetts law; separate EU consumer terms); no DPA for AI Pass was found on fetched first-party pages. Posit's GDPR page offers a DPA on request for Posit Cloud Services (posit.cloud, shinyapps.io); whether it covers AI Pass is unconfirmed.
Workbench Posit Assistant and its admin provider/settings controls are Preview; Posit describes these controls as best-effort policy, not a security boundary.
pricing: Posit AI Pass Pro: $20/month including $15 of monthly Posit Assistant credits (no rollover) and unlimited NES; credit usage is charged at a 10% premium over model-provider rates. The free trial ended in September 2026; eligible new subscribers pay $5 for the first month, and a payment card is required. Extra credits: one-time purchases of $20-$250, or opt-in auto-recharge with an optional monthly cap of $15-$500; purchased credits expire after 12 months and need an active subscription. Own-provider or local use: the provider is paid directly; no separate Posit Assistant fee is stated on fetched pages. Workbench licensing is separate.
academic: The FAQ states there is no education discount at this time; Posit says it is exploring options for the academic community. Check institutional Workbench terms separately.
use_cases: R and Python code writing and debugging in RStudio and Positron
Exploratory data analysis with live session context (data frames, variables, plots)
Shiny and Streamlit app scaffolding and Quarto reports (/report)
Next Edit Suggestions inline completions (Posit AI Pass only)
Multi-step agentic tasks with Plan Mode, permissions and skills
Codebase understanding and refactoring
Terminal and headless use via the pa client
Local-model analysis via Ollama or LM Studio when data must stay on controlled infrastructure
notes: Posit Assistant is Posit's proprietary data-science agent for RStudio (2026.04+), Positron and the pa terminal client. Since Positron 2026.07 it is the default, replacing Positron Assistant and Databot. Posit AI Pass is the paid hosted model subscription; it also unlocks NES. On Posit Workbench, Posit Assistant and its admin provider/settings controls are Preview. Positron console auditing is on the roadmap and not shipped.
tier_gate: Cloud use: Posit AI Pass Pro with trace collection not opted in; special-category data: Posit Assistant with local Ollama (local-only mode)/LM Studio only, with AI Pass, NES and cloud providers disabled

required_controls: Configure Posit Assistant with Ollama or LM Studio running on institution-controlled hardware; do not sign in to Posit AI Pass and keep Next Edit Suggestions (Posit-hosted) off.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable every cloud provider: in providers.json set providers.default.enabled to false and enable only ollama or lmstudio; on Workbench put this in the ai-providers-enforced file (Preview).
Keep web search off, deny web fetch and allow only local MCP servers.

Block outbound network egress at host or network level. In Workbench RStudio Pro sessions, set assistant-installation-enabled = 0 to stop update checks to cdn.posit.co. In Positron, set update.mode to none and turn off update.anonymousUsageReporting, update.primaryLanguageReporting and extensions.autoCheckUpdates.
Confirm with Posit what Posit Assistant telemetry collects and disable it.
residual_risks: Posit Assistant telemetry is undocumented. A Workbench Helm example sets assistant.telemetry to false, but the published settings schema has no assistant key and rejects unknown top-level keys, so the setting's effect, default and content are unconfirmed.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so pointing Posit Assistant at local Ollama alone does not show that inference stays local.
Workbench Posit Assistant and its admin controls are Preview, and Posit describes administrator-managed settings as best-effort policy, not a security boundary.
Positron's own provider guide lists no Ollama/LM Studio entry (custom providers are Experimental); confirm the local provider works in the build in use.
The explicit no-AI-traffic statement covers Positron; no equivalent statement was found for RStudio Desktop.
Operation with all outbound egress blocked is not documented, and RStudio Desktop's own update and crash-reporting calls on the local route were not reviewed.
Local sessions, conversation history, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: marimo
vendor: Marimo Inc. (part of CoreWeave, Inc.); open-source Apache-2.0 notebook
deployment: Local (CLI via pip/uv/conda, VS Code) / self-hosted edit or app servers (Docker, Kubernetes operator, JupyterHub extension, Slurm) / marimohub self-hostable team platform (Apache-2.0, launched 2026-10-02) / cloud: molab (free hosted service on CoreWeave infrastructure)
model_backend: No model or key is set in the default config. The open-source editor uses providers you configure: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google AI/Vertex, Azure, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Weights & Biases, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI and others, local Ollama or LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If no chat model is set, the server falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini and others) paired via marimo pair or the experimental ACP panel use their own backends. molab supplies free hosted open-source models (Weights & Biases listed as AI subprocessor). marimohub managed AI is operator-configured and off by default.
data_handling_note: Local/self-hosted: marimo's default config sets no model or key and copilot completion off, and marimohub managed AI is off by default. When AI is used, notebook code, @-referenced variable values and whatever the chat's Ask/Agent/Code-mode tools read from the notebook or kernel go to the configured provider under that provider's terms; if no model is set, marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Paired agent CLIs send notebook context to their own backends. Core telemetry: no usage analytics found in a source search; OpenTelemetry tracing is opt-in (MARIMO_TRACING) and writes to a local file by default; the CLI checks marimo.io for a new release once a day unless --skip-update-check or MARIMO_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 is set (per the source code, a plain request without notebook content). molab is a separate hosted service: notebooks are 'public but undiscoverable by default'; built-in AI uses free hosted models (Weights & Biases subprocessor); the subprocessor list for molab, Community Cloud and marimo's websites also names Sentry (error/performance tracing) and PostHog (product analytics). molab terms (last updated 2022-09-22) prohibit HIPAA PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) data and grant Marimo a licence to use submitted content to operate, improve and provide the services; after account cancellation (molab terms) or an honoured deletion request (marimo data-requests page), content is deleted from active systems within 30 days and from backups within 60 days. Marimo's privacy URL redirects to CoreWeave's privacy policy (updated 2026-02-24), which permits AI/ML processing to improve and develop services; no molab-specific statement on training with notebook content or AI prompts was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local or self-hosted marimo/marimohub with a local or institution-approved model endpoint and approved integrations; any cloud model provider or paired agent CLI receives notebook code and referenced variable values under its own terms. molab notebooks are public-but-unlisted by default and molab is covered by CoreWeave's privacy policy; it needs separate institutional review.
suitability_notes.special: Only local/self-hosted marimo, or marimohub on institution-controlled compute and storage, with customer-controlled model inference (Ollama only in local-only mode) and approved integrations. molab does not qualify: it is pure cloud and its terms prohibit HIPAA PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) data. No local configuration is itself institutional approval.

compliance: Local installation, self-hosted marimohub and molab are separate governance boundaries; verify hosted-service contractual scope
molab terms prohibit HIPAA-regulated PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) special-category data
molab privacy is governed by CoreWeave's privacy policy; no public DPA or security attestation for molab was found on the fetched first-party pages
pricing: marimo and marimohub are Apache-2.0 and free to self-host; you pay for your own infrastructure and any model provider. molab is free per its docs (default 4 CPUs and 32 GB RAM, optional NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell GPU, sessions up to 12 h, limited persistent storage, free hosted AI models). No public paid plan or price list was found; cached-file size and persistence limits may change at molab's discretion.
academic: No academic licence needed: the notebook and marimohub are Apache-2.0. marimo's 'For researchers' page invites researchers to contact the team for help; molab is free but bound by its own terms.
use_cases: Reactive Python notebook with auto-rerunning cells on dependency change
SQL querying of dataframes (Polars, Pandas, DuckDB, SQLite, Postgres, MySQL)
Interactive data exploration with UI elements (sliders, plots, tables) synchronized with Python
Deployment of notebooks as web apps or WebAssembly HTML files
Git-friendly reproducible research (stored as pure .py files)
AI-assisted coding with BYO model key (local or cloud)
Pairing agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) with a running notebook via marimo pair; experimental in-editor ACP agents panel
JupyterHub/JupyterLab integration via marimo-jupyter-extension
Kubernetes deployment via marimo-operator and Slurm on HPC clusters
Self-hosted team notebook platform (marimohub) with projects, version history, scheduled jobs and SSO
notes: Open-source reactive Python notebook (Apache-2.0) from Marimo Inc., part of CoreWeave: CoreWeave announced a definitive agreement to acquire Marimo on 2025-10-30, and marimo's subprocessors page states 'Marimo is part of CoreWeave'. Actively maintained (0.25.1 released 2026-10-01; commits through 2026-10-09). marimohub, an Apache-2.0 self-hostable team platform, launched 2026-10-02 and adds a customer-controlled team deployment option; its compute backends also include third-party clouds.

required_controls: Run marimo locally or self-host it (edit/app server, JupyterHub, Kubernetes, Slurm or marimohub) on institution-controlled compute and storage; for marimohub use only local, Docker, Podman or Kubernetes compute and filesystem or institutional S3-compatible storage.

Configure only a local model endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio or an OpenAI-compatible server inside the institutional network that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers) and set it explicitly as the chat, edit and autocomplete model; remove cloud provider keys (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) from the server environment and .env files, because marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o with OPENAI_API_KEY when no model is set; leave marimohub managed AI off or point it at that endpoint; set ai.allow_provider_config=false to lock provider setup in the settings UI. ai.enabled=false only hides AI panels; code-completion settings stay available, so also keep completion.copilot off.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep token authentication on (do not expose servers started with --no-token) and run a current release; 0.23.0 fixed a critical pre-auth remote code execution via the terminal websocket (GHSA-2679-6mx9-h9xc).

Disable or restrict molab, cloud AI providers, paired cloud agent CLIs, MCP servers, GitHub and remote-storage connections; start servers with --skip-update-check or MARIMO_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 where egress to marimo.io is not allowed; apply institutional access, retention and logging controls.

Before use, check the effective AI configuration on the server (marimo.toml, .env files and environment variables), then block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block.
residual_risks: molab, third-party marimohub backends (e.g. CoreWeave Sandboxes, W&B, Modal, AWS ECS Fargate, E2B, Cloudflare) and cloud model providers are outside the customer-controlled boundary and do not qualify for special-category data.
The provider lock applies to the settings UI; users with access to marimo.toml, .env files or environment variables can still point AI at external endpoints, so enforce network egress controls.
Paired agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini) read variable values and outputs and send them to their own model providers unless run against a local model.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Local session files, caches, logs and marimohub version history, snapshots and audit events retain data and need institutional retention and backup rules.
No local configuration is itself institutional (DPO, ethics or security) approval.

name: Runcell
deployment: cloud: JupyterLab 4.4+ extension (pip, conda/uv or JupyterLab Extension Manager; Docker recipes documented). Notebook code runs in the user's Jupyter kernel; every AI request goes through Runcell's cloud orchestrator; offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported. Also: macOS desktop beta (v0.3.4, 2026-09-22; data flow undocumented) and a preview headless Agent runtime that calls service.runcell.dev. Stricter isolation or self-deployment only on request ('contact us').
model_backend: Runcell-hosted model access through Runcell's cloud orchestrator. No BYO key is needed, and no BYO-key or custom/local endpoint option is documented. The token-credit table (snapshot 2026-09-05) lists Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini models plus models from xAI, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Xiaomi, Z.ai and a Dolphin-Mistral (Venice edition) model; the inventory changes with each release. Some models are served through OpenRouter, and which ones is not documented. Hobby has limited model access; paid plans unlock advanced models.
data_handling_note: Paid plans: Privacy Mode is on by default and Runcell does not use prompts, context or outputs to train or fine-tune models. The policy names Pro and Team; the pricing page also lists Privacy Mode for Pro+ and Ultra. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and Runcell may retain and use prompts, context and outputs for training. Prompts, selected notebook context and short interaction history are assembled on Runcell's cloud and sent to the chosen model provider, for some models via OpenRouter. Runcell instructs providers not to train only where their controls allow it, and providers may run abuse/quality checks. No ZDR commitment is stated. Optional chat cloud sync stores conversations server-side; neither its default state nor a retention period is stated. Turning sync off stops new uploads; per policy section 5, previously synced content can be deleted from the account, and no automatic removal is stated. Storage of long-running Agent job state and of cross-session Agent Memory is not documented. Product analytics (Microsoft Clarity) and payload-free telemetry exclude notebook and chat content; no opt-out is documented. No public DPA or subprocessor list was found.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Use a paid plan. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and its inputs/outputs may be used for training.
suitability_notes.personal: No public DPA or subprocessor list was found. Treat personal-data use as blocked unless the institution obtains and approves a signed processor agreement.
suitability_notes.special: Inference always runs through Runcell's cloud and third-party model providers. Offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported, and self-deployment is offered only on request. Not suitable.

pricing: Pricing page (checked 2026-10-10): Hobby free (20 credits/month, limited model access; no Privacy Mode per the privacy policy); Pro $20/month (500 credits); Pro+ $60/month (2,000 credits); Ultra $200/month (10,000 credits); Teams $40/seat/month (500 credits per seat). Annual billing is offered (Pro $180, Pro+ $600, Ultra $2,000, Teams $400 per seat per year). Ask/Chat and Agent use token-based credits at 30 credits per USD of provider-equivalent model cost (changed from 100 on 2026-07-15); other AI features use fixed or model-rate-based feature credits. Privacy Mode is listed on Pro, Pro+ and Ultra; Teams includes 'Everything in Pro'.
academic: No academic or student entitlement was found on first-party pages.
use_cases: Autonomous multi-step data analysis in JupyterLab
Long-running ML training jobs (multi-hour, end-to-end)
Cross-session project memory for iterative research workflows
Output-aware reasoning (reads charts, plots, DataFrame previews)
Automated cell execution, debugging, and error recovery
Domain-driven research analyses and figures (e.g. genomics circos plots) and risk/quantitative-finance modelling
Interactive learning and algorithm explanation in notebooks
Exploratory analysis, data wrangling, visualisation and model building in notebooks
notes: Cloud-connected notebook agent: code runs in the local Jupyter kernel, but inference always goes through Runcell's cloud. Paid Privacy Mode gives a no-training commitment; no public DPA was found. No public Enterprise plan is listed; stricter isolation or self-deployment is available only on request ('contact us'). Other surfaces: a macOS desktop beta (v0.3.1-0.3.4, Sep 2026; binary-only GitHub repo, no stated licence, data flow undocumented) and a preview headless Agent runtime that uses the Runcell cloud backend. A sign-in 'Cloud Agents' web app (runcell.dev/agents, listed in the public sitemap) also exists; its page code points to a server-side Python workspace with file attachments. It is undocumented and was not assessed. Some first-party pages overstate locality: the docs landing page says 'Your data stays local', and the Jupyter AI agent page says AI processing happens 'locally or through secure encrypted connections'. The privacy policy states that prompts and relevant snippets go to Runcell's cloud and the model provider.
tier_gate: Paid plan (Pro, Pro+, Ultra or Teams) for Privacy Mode; personal data blocked pending a signed DPA

residual_risks: AI requests always pass through Runcell's cloud orchestrator and third-party model providers (some via OpenRouter); offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported.
Self-deployment is offered only as 'contact us', with no documented customer-controlled boundary.

name: JetBrains Datalore
deployment: Datalore Cloud (JetBrains-hosted) or Datalore On-Premises: Docker Compose or Kubernetes/Helm on 64-bit Linux, on premises or in the customer's own cloud account. The On-Premises option is also offered as a JetBrains-managed dedicated instance, which is not customer-controlled.
model_backend: Cloud: JetBrains AI service (FAQ: Anthropic Claude and JetBrains-trained models by default; can also use OpenAI and Google models); Datalore AI only on the paid Cloud plan, not Cloud Free. On-Premises: admin selects JetBrains AI (relayed through JetBrains) or Bring Your Own Key (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API, including a self-hosted LLM); AI needs an active paid On-Premises licence.
data_handling_note: 'local' applies only to customer-operated On-Premises with BYOK pointed at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLM; with BYOK the FAQ says data goes directly from the instance to the configured provider. AI is off by default in both editions (Cloud: until the user accepts AI terms; On-Premises: until an admin enables it instance-wide). Cloud: AI is relayed through JetBrains; Datalore states it does not use LLM providers that train on customer data and does not take part in Detailed Data Collection, but it records users' prompts as prompt history (retention period not stated), and under the Cloud terms JetBrains keeps a backup of deleted hosted data for one month unless the customer asks for the backup to be deleted too. On-Premises with JetBrains AI: context is relayed through JetBrains infrastructure (stated not stored, not used for training). On-Premises with a cloud BYOK provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible service such as OpenRouter) sends prompts, selected cells, optional outputs, runtime-variable fragments and a list of attached file names to that provider under its terms. The AI setup page lists auth.grazie.ai and api.jetbrains.ai for the JetBrains AI option only (for BYOK it asks to allow the provider or local LLM), but the server configuration keeps them as Datalore AI default endpoints; whether a BYOK-only instance contacts them is not documented. On-Premises usage telemetry to JetBrains is not documented in the pages reviewed.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer customer-operated On-Premises with a self-hosted model. Cloud is possible after institutional review: AI requires the paid Cloud plan, the Datalore Cloud terms incorporate the JetBrains DPA, AI is relayed through JetBrains and prompts are kept as history. On Cloud team plans the Owner and Admins can access members' Private workspaces, and Cloud plans including Cloud Free list the Notebook API, through which external agents can reach notebook content. Use 'Review prompt' and leave 'Include outputs' off for personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only a customer-operated, paid On-Premises installation (not the JetBrains-managed dedicated instance) with BYOK pointed at a self-hosted LLM, JetBrains AI not selected, and external integrations and agent-skill/API tokens restricted. A locally installed server using JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider does not qualify.

compliance: Deployment- and contract-dependent; verify exact Datalore product scope
Datalore Cloud Terms of Service (v4.0, effective 20 Aug 2024) incorporate the JetBrains Data Processing Addendum (v1.3, with Standard Contractual Clauses)
Datalore security docs point to the JetBrains Trust Center for a non-public SOC 2 report; Datalore-specific scope not confirmed
pricing: Plans: Cloud Free (no Datalore AI; 120 CPU S machine hours, 10 GB), 14-day Cloud trial (up to 3 users), paid Cloud plan (seat-based, monthly or 1-year; includes Datalore AI, 750 CPU L hours and 6 credits per member) and On-Premises (licensed per active editor seat, viewers free, infrastructure costs extra). The buy page renders country-localized prices client-side; no list price is asserted here. Obtain a current Cloud or On-Premises quote.
academic: No Datalore academic programme confirmed. The JetBrains student/teacher Toolbox subscription (v4.2) explicitly excludes Datalore. Cloud Free exists but has no Datalore AI. Ask JetBrains sales about education terms.
use_cases: Jupyter-compatible notebooks in Python (default), R, Kotlin and Scala, with SQL cells for database queries
Collaborative real-time notebook editing for teams
AI-assisted code generation and modification in notebooks (Ask AI, Autopilot; Python, R, SQL and Markdown cells)
No-code DataFrame exploration via Data Explorer cells (2026.1)
Interactive data reports and dashboards shareable without code exposure
Scheduled notebook runs and automation
External AI coding agents working in Datalore notebooks and workspaces via the official agent skill and API (Datalore Cloud and On-Premises 2026.2+; workspace scope since 2026.3)
On-premises deployment for regulated data environments with BYOK AI, including a self-hosted LLM
notes: Notebook data-science platform with Cloud and On-Premises editions; On-Premises 2026.3 server image published 22 Sep 2026. The FAQ defines On-Premises as installation in a customer-controlled environment, including the customer's own cloud. The qualifying route is customer-operated Datalore plus a self-hosted model, with JetBrains AI not selected and external integrations and agent API access restricted. The official agent skill lets external AI agents read, edit and run notebook cells and query workspace databases; that content then goes to the agent's own model provider.
tier_gate: Customer-operated Datalore On-Premises (paid licence) + BYOK self-hosted LLM

required_controls: Use an active paid On-Premises licence on infrastructure the institution operates (own servers or own cloud account), not the JetBrains-managed dedicated instance.

In Admin panel > AI select Bring Your Own Key pointed at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLM running on institution-operated infrastructure (the Datalore host or another institution-controlled server inside the network), reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers; do not select JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider.
Block or monitor egress to auth.grazie.ai, api.jetbrains.ai and cloud LLM endpoints, and confirm AI still works with only the local endpoint reachable.

Restrict API tokens and the Datalore agent skill to agents whose model runs on institution-controlled infrastructure; no instance-wide admin switch for them is documented in the pages reviewed, so enforce this through token issuance policy and network controls. Keep cloud storage, Google Drive and other external integrations disabled unless approved.
residual_risks: A locally installed server using JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider sends prompts, selected cells, optional outputs, runtime-variable fragments and attached file names off-premises.

The AI setup page lists auth.grazie.ai and api.jetbrains.ai under the JetBrains AI option, but the server configuration keeps them as Datalore AI default endpoints; docs do not state whether a BYOK-only instance contacts them. Verify with network monitoring.
The agent skill/API lets an external agent read cell outputs and query workspace databases; if that agent uses a cloud model, data leaves the boundary regardless of Datalore's AI setting.

Datalore stores SQL result slices (first and last 100 values) and rendered outputs in its own database and storage; optional user activity logging records cell content. These need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: ChatGPT Data Analysis
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Managed ChatGPT model selection, varying by plan and rollout; do not infer the exact Python data-analysis backend from the model picker.
data_handling_note: Business, Enterprise, Edu and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspaces are excluded from model training by default. Individual plans (Free/Go/Plus/Pro) may be used for training unless 'Improve the model for everyone' is off; thumbs feedback can still submit the whole conversation. On personal accounts, content on shared Space pages can be used for training through a collaborator's settings even if the owner opted out. Product-level retention applies regardless: saved chats persist until deleted or removed by a workspace retention policy (then scheduled for deletion within 30 days); Library files persist until deleted separately, and deleting a chat does not delete them; in Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare workspaces Library files follow the workspace retention policy. From 2026-09-29 Space replaces Library for eligible Pro/Business/Enterprise accounts; Space file retention is not separately documented. Eligible new Enterprise/Edu workspaces can keep in-scope content (including Code Interpreter & Data Analysis artifacts) at rest in-region, with optional GPU inference residency (help centre: EEA+CH, US, UAE); CPU processing, metadata and external integrations may be outside the region, and the residency article does not say where the Python data-analysis environment runs. ZDR is documented for eligible API endpoints; the Business overview lists ZDR only as an unspecified sales-led option, and no ZDR terms for ChatGPT chats or files were found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace with an executed DPA (Business/Enterprise) or the institution's Edu data-processing terms, accepted retention settings and, where required, EU data residency (Enterprise/Edu only; not offered on Business). Consumer opt-out alone is insufficient; Library/Space files need their own deletion. A ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspace has no-training defaults, but its public page names no DPA: confirm terms before using personal data.
suitability_notes.special: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

compliance: DPA offered for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise; ChatGPT Edu (and Teachers) data processed under OpenAI's Student Data Privacy Agreement per the Enterprise privacy page; confirm the institution's executed terms

OpenAI states that ChatGPT Business and ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare each completed a SOC 2 Type 2 audit, and that its practices align with CSA STAR, SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications; per-plan certification scope not confirmed (Trust Portal reports gated)

Data residency at rest for eligible new Enterprise/Edu workspaces (includes Code Interpreter & Data Analysis artifacts); optional GPU inference residency (help centre: EEA+CH, US, UAE; the business-data page names only U.S. or Europe); not available on Business
BAA offered for ChatGPT for Healthcare (US HIPAA); this does not change the catalog's special-category rule
pricing: Data analysis has separate usage limits on Free, extended access on Go, and is included on Plus, Pro (three plans: Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500), Business, Enterprise and Edu. Business is billed per paid seat (Standard or Premium seat types, at least two paid seats, monthly or annual billing, prices vary by country/currency); Enterprise and Edu are priced through sales. Use the current localized pricing and the institutional order.
academic: ChatGPT Edu is available through institutional agreements. ChatGPT for Academic Researchers (announced 2026-07-29) lets eligible research faculty and postdoctoral researchers at participating institutions in supported countries apply for a complimentary 12-month workspace: up to five seats (owner plus four verified collaborators from the same institution), Pro-level rate limits, no SSO/SCIM and no API credits. Applicants need SheerID verification, an authored arXiv/bioRxiv/ChemRxiv paper from the last three years in an eligible field (incl. Biological Sciences) and a $0 card checkout. Researchers at existing Edu institutions are routed through their Edu organization. No general individual academic discount is asserted.
use_cases: Exploratory analysis of uploaded spreadsheets (CSV/XLS/XLSX), PDFs and text/data files (JSON, XML, YAML, TXT, MD)
Python code generation and execution in a stateful Jupyter environment without external network access
Statistical analysis (comparative tests, correlation and regression, time series), calculations and data transformations
Data cleaning (missing values, outliers, duplicates, data types) and merging datasets on shared identifiers
Charts as static images (downloadable as PNG); interactive bar, line, pie and scatter charts
Interactive table review of pandas DataFrames; tables downloadable as CSV
Summaries of rows, columns, trends and outliers
Conversational iteration on analysis methods and results
Files from connected sources (Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint) where connectors are enabled
notes: OpenAI's help article is now titled 'Data analysis with ChatGPT' (formerly Advanced Data Analysis / Code Interpreter); the catalog name ChatGPT Data Analysis is kept. Cloud-only: Python runs in ChatGPT's Jupyter environment, which cannot make external web requests. From 2026-09-29 Space replaces Library for eligible accounts. Organizational no-training, retention and residency controls do not make it acceptable for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.
tier_gate: Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace with an executed DPA or Edu data-processing terms and accepted retention controls

residual_risks: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

name: Ollama
deployment: local-capable / self-hostable / cloud
model_backend: Open-weight models run locally or on optional Ollama Cloud; model availability is dynamic
data_handling_note: Ollama's privacy policy (last updated March 2026) says Ollama does not receive prompts or data processed with local models; cloud-model prompts and responses are processed transiently and never used for training. The pricing FAQ says cloud models are hosted primarily in the United States, may be routed to Europe for extra capacity, and are served with NVIDIA Cloud Provider partners that Ollama requires to have no-logging, no-training and zero-retention policies. The policy says Ollama may collect limited device and usage metadata, without prompt or response content. These are vendor statements; no public DPA, trust centre or certification was found. Cloud inference and web search can be switched off (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud).

suitability_notes.personal: Run in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud) with local models on controlled hardware, and assess each agent or integration using the runtime. Optional cloud inference is a separate service, hosted primarily in the US with possible routing to Europe, under Ollama's terms; local availability is not institutional approval.
suitability_notes.special: Only local-only mode with locally provisioned models on institution-controlled hardware qualifies. Govern the calling agent, its web tools, local files, the unauthenticated local API and network egress separately.

compliance: Local mode avoids a vendor processor; no exhaustive public cloud certification claim is made
pricing: Free local runtime and starter cloud usage; Pro $20/month ($200/year) includes $60 monthly cloud credits; Max $100/month includes $300; Team early access $500/month for unlimited users includes $1,000 shared credits. Enterprise custom. Included credits do not roll over, top-ups are available, and some models have weekday peak pricing. Local runtime use has no Ollama inference fee.
academic: The MIT local runtime is available without academic eligibility; hardware and separately licensed model costs remain.
use_cases: local-only model infrastructure for coding agents (cloud features can be disabled)
private model serving for research workflows
backend for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Droid, and other compatible clients
local model evaluation and agent pipelines
notes: Local model runtime used by coding agents and notebooks, with a separate optional cloud service (cloud models, web search). The qualifying special-category route requires local-only mode, locally provisioned models and governed agent integrations.

required_controls: Enable local-only mode with OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or "disable_ollama_cloud": true in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the Ollama server (on a Linux systemd install, the ollama service user, not the researcher). This disables cloud inference and web search; confirm the server log shows "Ollama cloud disabled: true".
Provision only local models on institution-controlled hardware, pulled through an approved route or imported from local GGUF/Safetensors weights.
Keep the API bound to 127.0.0.1 or put it behind an authenticating proxy; the local API requires no authentication.
Govern the calling agent and its integrations (web search/fetch, desktop-app connectors) and enforce network egress, update and local-state retention controls.
residual_risks: Agents launched through Ollama can select cloud models or web tools unless cloud features are disabled; the agent's own data flows need separate review.
The privacy policy reserves collection of limited device and usage metadata (e.g. app version, request counts); no separate opt-out is documented, so rely on egress controls.
The privacy policy lists model download metadata among data collected automatically, so pulls from the ollama.com registry are visible to Ollama; use local GGUF/Safetensors import where this matters.
In the source defaults, the unauthenticated API accepts browser requests from localhost, file:// and editor-webview origins, so local web content and editor webviews on the host can reach it.
Local sessions, logs, model files and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Grok Build
deployment: Local CLI/TUI (macOS, Linux, Windows; also headless and ACP). Default inference runs in SpaceXAI cloud (cli-chat-proxy.grok.com, or api.x.ai with an API key). Custom endpoints, including a local Ollama or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server, are set in config.toml. Fleet policy via managed_config.toml, signed requirements.toml or macOS MDM.
model_backend: SpaceXAI models by default (grok-build is the documented recommended default; SpaceXAI states Grok 4.7 now powers Grok Build). Custom [model.*] endpoints speak Chat Completions, Responses or Messages APIs and can point to local Ollama/OpenAI-compatible servers, Amazon Bedrock or other providers. Admins can pin the selectable model set in signed requirements.toml.
data_handling_note: Individual (non-ZDR) accounts: SpaceXAI states the CLI shows a screen asking to retain data to improve the product and model, and /privacy offers Opt in/Opt out for 'Coding data, retention, and training'. The pre-selected default is not documented, so the catalog treats it as opt-out. On team accounts only an admin can change the setting. /privacy does not change product telemetry or session-trace upload; trace upload follows the telemetry switch when unset, and the config reference states only that the enterprise telemetry default is off. Team-level ZDR: SpaceXAI states no Grok Build trace or code data is retained and that ZDR turns off product analytics, session-trace upload and coding-data sharing. Non-ZDR inference-layer retention for Grok Build is not stated (the 30-day audit retention is documented for API requests). Remote session sync and share links use code.grok.com; local history stays in ~/.grok/. Which legal terms govern individual Grok Build accounts is not documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Cloud use only via a team account with admin-enabled ZDR (enabling it accepts the Enterprise Terms) or a negotiated Enterprise agreement, with telemetry, trace upload and feedback pinned off in signed requirements.toml; or use an institution-controlled endpoint. Individual accounts are not recommended for personal data: their governing terms and non-ZDR retention are not documented, and the /privacy opt-out does not stop telemetry or trace upload. Institutional DPA review still applies.
suitability_notes.special: Only with inference on a local model server (e.g., Ollama at localhost) pinned as the only selectable model in signed requirements.toml, SpaceXAI telemetry, trace upload, feedback and remote fetch pinned off, and tested network egress blocking to SpaceXAI hosts. Default SpaceXAI-cloud operation is not acceptable, ZDR notwithstanding.

compliance: Team-level ZDR (admin-enabled, self-serve where available): SpaceXAI states no Grok Build trace or code data is retained; ZDR does not mute a customer-configured external OTEL stream.
ZDR coverage of remote session sync and share links (code.grok.com) is not documented.
Local session history, memory files and logs under ~/.grok/ are outside ZDR and need institutional controls.
pricing: Free tier available (Grok 4.7 Fast excluded). Paid SuperGrok plans use one shared weekly usage pool across Grok products including 'Build' (the FAQ does not separate the CLI from grok.com Build mode); Grok 4.7 Fast is billed through the plan. API-key use is metered at xAI API rates (global endpoint, <200k prompt tokens, per 1M tokens: grok-4.7 $2.00 input / $6.00 output; grok-build-0.1 $1.00 / $2.00; higher at >=200k). Subscription prices not verified.
academic: No academic or student program found in SpaceXAI documentation (checked 2026-10-10).
use_cases: terminal-native agentic coding on large codebases
headless/CI scripting and long-running tasks
Agent Client Protocol integration into third-party editors
BYO/self-hosted model endpoint workflows for controlled environments
notes: Apache-2.0 Rust client published by SpaceXAI, synced periodically from its monorepo; external contributions are not accepted. No GitHub releases: binaries ship via the x.ai installer and npm @xai-official/grok (1.0.50 on 2026-10-06). Enterprise docs list auth.x.ai and cli-chat-proxy.grok.com as required for core functionality, so offline operation with a local model must be tested, not assumed.
tier_gate: Cloud: team account with admin-enabled ZDR (or a negotiated Enterprise agreement) plus telemetry, trace upload and feedback pinned off; individual accounts have only the /privacy coding-data choice, which does not cover telemetry or trace upload. Special-category data: local model server plus signed requirements.toml pins and tested egress blocking.

required_controls: Configure only a local model server (e.g., Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server at localhost) as [model.*]; pin it as models.default and the only entry in models.allowed_models in signed /etc/grok/requirements.toml; an institution-hosted endpoint changes the route and needs its own review.

Point every auxiliary model role (models.web_search, models.image_description, models.session_summary, models.prompt_suggestion) at the local model or disable those features, because they can otherwise resolve to SpaceXAI-served models.

Pin features.telemetry = false, telemetry.trace_upload = false, features.feedback = false, features.remote_fetch = false and cli.auto_update = false in signed requirements.toml; keep external OTEL off or limited to an institutional collector with content gates off.
Opt out of coding-data sharing (/privacy) or use a ZDR team account; disable relay sync and memory unless reviewed; restrict web search/fetch and MCP servers.

Use an external auth provider (auth_provider_command, documented for air-gapped networks) instead of SpaceXAI OAuth; block egress to all SpaceXAI hosts (auth.x.ai, cli-chat-proxy.grok.com, api.x.ai, code.grok.com, assets.grok.com, x.ai) and verify by testing that sessions run without them.
residual_risks: Enterprise docs list auth.x.ai and cli-chat-proxy.grok.com as required for core functionality; running with a local model and no SpaceXAI connectivity is not documented end to end.
The pre-selected default of the first-run data-retention screen and the terms that govern individual accounts are not documented.
Local sessions (~/.grok/sessions/), memory files and logs (~/.grok/logs/; TUI file logging defaults to DEBUG) need institutional access, retention and encryption controls.
Local models may be less capable than the default SpaceXAI models.

name: Muse Code
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Meta-hosted Muse Spark models: Standard muse-spark-1.1/1.2/1.3 and Contributor muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor (1,048,576-token context). Muse Code docs name muse-spark-1.2 as the default model; the API docs recommend 1.3 for new work. The client is provider-aware: the configuration docs and changelog refer to other providers, a --provider flag for muse serve and a keyless custom endpoint, and Meta's MIT SDK quickstart sets an endpoint_transport base URL to a loopback test endpoint. No first-party page documents serving a self-hosted or local model to Muse Code. Meta's open-weight Muse Glimmer runs on your own hardware; its docs do not mention Muse Code.
data_handling_note: The no-train label applies to the personal-data route in tier_gate (organisation API key on a pinned Standard model); a Muse Code subscription on default settings runs under Contributor (training) terms. Terms depend on account route and model tier (Meta Model API Terms of Service, last updated 2026-10-09). Standard models (muse-spark-1.1/1.2/1.3): Meta acts as processor under the Meta Global Processor Terms and does not train on Content. Contributor models (1.2/1.3-contributor) permit training, and the ToS forbids sending personal, sensitive or confidential data (including confidential code) to them. Since the 2026-10-09 ToS, a Muse Code subscription counts as Contributor (training) by default whatever model is selected; Standard terms require changing an Account setting and apply prospectively only. Pay-as-you-go API-key use of the default model (muse-spark-1.2) is Standard. The ToS also warns that the system may route requests to a Contributor model. On every tier Meta may retain and process Content for policy enforcement and to develop safety and security systems, and the Data Commitments page also lists improving and maintaining the Model API. Without ZDR, Content and Usage Data (tool-call sequences, logs, telemetry) are retained 'as needed' with no stated period, and Usage Data may be used to develop and improve Meta products. The Data Commitments page says Content can be viewed and deleted through the account. ZDR is available only to qualified organisations, enabled by Meta through sales; personal accounts are not covered, support may vary by model, ZDR turns off stateful and background requests, file uploads and web search, and flagged content may still be kept up to 2 years. CLI: changelog 1.4.0 refers to a saved opt-out for 'feedback and diagnostic upload', so it appears to be on unless disabled; what it sends is undocumented. A local session event log is kept by default (--no-session-log disables it); voice input is on by default on macOS; four background observer agents make extra model calls by default. By default Muse Code also loads skills from ~/.claude/skills and $CODEX_HOME/skills (or ~/.codex/skills) and from repo-local .claude/.codex skill folders, so other agents' skill files can enter the context sent to Meta; a user preference can disable the personal foreign skill roots. Client guardrails are on by default: approvals (default Auto-review profile, where an automated judge clears eligible requests), OS sandbox, proxy-only network with per-destination approval, workspace-scoped writes.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: On a subscription with default settings, or on any Contributor model, Meta may train on prompts, code and outputs; use only public or non-confidential code there, as the ToS itself requires.
suitability_notes.personal: Configuration-required. Use a Business & Enterprise (managed account) organisation API key on a pinned Standard model, with ZDR enabled by Meta and confirmed in writing to cover Muse Code traffic and the models used. Turn off feedback and diagnostic upload and voice input (on by default on macOS) in settings, and do not attach session logs to /feedback. The institution must review the Meta Global Processor Terms, Data Security Terms, subprocessors, the Usage Data clause and the 2-year flagged-content exception, and check served model IDs because the ToS says requests may be routed to a Contributor model. Never use a personal Meta Account, a subscription on default settings, or a Contributor model. No security certification for Model API or Muse Code was named in the fetched pages.
suitability_notes.special: Inference runs on Meta-hosted Muse Spark. No first-party page documents a supported self-hosted or customer-controlled inference endpoint for Muse Code. Meta's MIT SDK quickstart points the CLI's endpoint_transport setting at a loopback test endpoint, which shows the base URL can be configured, but it is not a documented model-serving route, and ToS 10.1(xiv) bars modifying the harness to operate with non-Meta models. Not acceptable under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule, even with ZDR or processor terms.

compliance: Meta Global Processor Terms apply to Standard Services only (ToS section 5.1); no Model API or Muse Code security certification was named in the fetched legal, help or product pages.
pricing: Muse Code subscriptions: Everyday Usage $5/month, High Usage $15/month (5x Everyday usage), Power Usage $50/month (20x), as listed on the product page and Help Center on 2026-10-10; benefits and availability vary by region. Subscriptions use Contributor (training) terms by default unless the Account setting is changed. Pay-as-you-go per 1M tokens: Standard $1.25 input / $4.25 output / $0.15 cached input; Contributor $0.10 / $0.20 / $0.002, in exchange for training permission.
academic: No academic or student program found.
use_cases: agentic coding on large codebases (1M-token context)
CI/headless automation
parallel sub-agents in isolated git worktrees
sandboxed command execution with staged shell review
notes: Terminal/CI coding agent for macOS, Linux and Windows using Meta-hosted Muse Spark models. The 2026-10-09 ToS made Muse Code subscriptions Contributor (training) by default regardless of the selected model; the Muse Code subscription docs still say data use depends on the selected model, so read the ToS. A personal-data route exists only through an organisation account with Meta-enabled ZDR on Standard models. The programmatic SDK (meta-models/muse-code-sdk) is MIT-licensed; the CLI itself is proprietary, licensed in object code form only.
tier_gate: personal data only via a Business & Enterprise managed-account organisation API key on a pinned Standard model under the Meta Global Processor Terms, with Meta-enabled ZDR; confirm in writing that the processor terms and ZDR cover Muse Code traffic and the models used; feedback/diagnostic upload and voice input off; never a subscription (Contributor/training by default, ToS 3.3), a personal Meta Account or a Contributor model

residual_risks: All inference runs on Meta-hosted Muse Spark; no first-party page documents a supported customer-controlled or local inference endpoint for Muse Code (the endpoint_transport base URL in Meta's SDK test harness is not a documented serving route, and ToS 10.1(xiv) bars modifying the harness to operate with non-Meta models).
ZDR and processor terms do not change the vendor-cloud boundary, and flagged content may be retained for up to 2 years even under ZDR.

name: Ante
deployment: local-capable (single binary; fully offline once its managed llama.cpp engine and a GGUF model are installed) / BYO cloud APIs
model_backend: Managed local llama.cpp/GGUF inference, attached llama.cpp-compatible servers, or user-configured cloud/OpenAI-compatible providers (including Antigma's optional Antix gateway).
data_handling_note: When an OTLP endpoint is set at runtime or embedded in the binary at build time, Ante exports metrics and application logs. The docs do not say whether official release binaries embed an endpoint, so treat them as possibly exporting by default. Exported log bodies are not scrubbed and may contain paths or tool arguments. ANTE_TELEMETRY=off disables export. Local logs, sessions (including copies kept on rewind) and auto-memory persist under ~/.ante; background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. Since v0.2.0, WebFetch spill files and staging downloads sit in the OS cache and temp directories, outside ~/.ante. Local GGUF inference keeps model traffic on the machine. With cloud presets, the provider's terms govern. The optional Antix proxy records request and response bodies on every call; Antigma states this traffic is not used to train its models, and the upstream model provider's policy still applies.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local GGUF inference (or an institution-approved endpoint) and set ANTE_TELEMETRY=off. With cloud presets, the selected provider's retention and training terms govern. The optional Antix proxy stores request and response bodies.
suitability_notes.special: Use locally provisioned GGUF inference on the same host (Ante-managed or institution-built llama.cpp) with ANTE_TELEMETRY=off; otherwise exported logs may contain paths or tool arguments. Exclude gateway mode, /term-driven cloud agents, any non-loopback endpoint, the default WebFetch tool and off-host MCP servers, and block host egress. Govern local logs, sessions, memory and the OS cache and temp files.

pricing: Prebuilt binary is free, including commercial use, during the alpha preview under the Binary Preview Terms. Repository source (SDK, protocol and support crates, ACP and gateway apps) is Apache-2.0. Cloud providers and the optional Antix gateway are metered separately (Antix prices not reviewed); local inference still requires hardware.
academic: No special academic entitlement is asserted; binary preview terms apply to all uses.
use_cases: fully offline/air-gapped coding assistance on sensitive or pre-publication code
single-binary install on locked-down or HPC-adjacent machines
BYO-key multi-provider terminal agent
headless scripting
notes: Preview-stage terminal coding agent with managed local-model support. The README labels it a beta preview; the Binary Preview Terms call it an alpha research preview. Releases follow semver since v0.2.0 (Sep 2026). The Apache-2.0 repository holds the SDK, protocol and support crates plus the ACP and Slack/Discord gateway apps. The core agent ships only as a prebuilt binary: the open-sourcing tracking issue (#21) still lists moving more core crates and shipping source with the binary as open.
tier_gate: fully offline same-host GGUF model + ANTE_TELEMETRY=off for regulated data

required_controls: Fully offline configuration only. Run the managed llama.cpp engine (installed in advance with `ante offline install`) or an institution-built llama.cpp on the same host, with a locally provisioned GGUF model, and attach no non-loopback endpoint. Cloud presets, Antix and remote or LAN-hosted endpoints are not acceptable.
Set ANTE_TELEMETRY=off for every Ante process; the docs do not say whether official binaries embed an OTLP endpoint.
Do not use gateway mode (Slack/Discord), and do not drive cloud-backed agent CLIs (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) through /term or Ante's tmux terminal sessions in this route.
Remove the WebFetch tool, which is enabled by default (--exclude-tools WebFetch, a --tools allow-list or a permission deny rule), and configure no MCP servers that reach beyond the host.

Keep no cloud provider API keys in the environment or Ante settings, and check the effective provider, telemetry and tool settings (including named profiles and project settings) before each sensitive session.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level and verify that the block holds; this also stops the background update checks, for which the docs describe no opt-out. Install reviewed releases through institutional software management.
residual_risks: Whether official binaries export telemetry by default is undocumented; if ANTE_TELEMETRY=off is missed for any process, exported log bodies may carry paths or tool arguments.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

WebFetch spill and staging files sit in the OS cache and temp directories outside ~/.ante; staging files fall outside the 48-hour cleanup. Rewinds keep abandoned dialog copies inside session directories, and background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends.

Ante labels any attached llama.cpp server as the 'local' provider, including one on another LAN host; confirm the endpoint is loopback/same-host, since a non-loopback attach is outside this local-only route.

The core is a closed-source preview binary that cannot be audited from source, and distribution may change or stop without notice. On networked hosts, background update checks contact the release manifest up to hourly; the update docs describe no opt-out.

name: Nanocoder
vendor: Nano Collective (volunteer-led community collective; fiscally hosted by Open Source Collective, no separate legal entity)
deployment: local-capable
model_backend: BYO: local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI, MLX Server, llama-swap, Atomic Chat); OpenAI-compatible cloud APIs and routers (e.g., OpenRouter, Requesty, OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, Together AI, Atlas Cloud, a project sponsor); native-SDK providers (e.g., Anthropic, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT/Codex)
data_handling_note: No vendor cloud: model requests go to the provider endpoint(s) the user configures; configured MCP servers and network tools (fetch_url; web_search via Brave when a key is set) can carry prompt-derived content to other hosts. Released v1.31.0 docs state no telemetry and name two self-initiated calls: an npm-registry version check on each interactive start (no off switch) and a models.dev metadata download, neither carrying code or prompts. Sessions are saved locally (autosave on, 30-day default retention); daily log files are written by default with pattern-based redaction (NANOCODER_LOG_DISABLE_FILE turns them off). Optional prompt scrubbing (default off) masks detected secrets and identifiers but leaves paths and URLs. A cloud endpoint subjects prompts to that provider's terms. No DPA or certification; these are project statements, not an independent network audit.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local endpoint, or a cloud API covered by an institutional processing agreement. Restrict network tools (fetch_url, web_search, MCP) and account for local session and log files. Prompt scrubbing is pattern-based and off by default; it is not anonymisation.
suitability_notes.special: Only a local model runtime (Ollama in local-only mode if used) on institution-controlled hardware qualifies, with egress blocked except approved hosts, network tools disabled, the effective configuration checked in each working directory, and sessions/logs on controlled storage. The npm version check cannot be switched off; per the docs it carries no content, but it still needs an egress decision.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free and MIT-licensed; the project states it has no paid tiers. Costs are the chosen API provider's usage fees; no API cost with local models.
academic: Free community open-source project.
use_cases: local-first coding assistance where code must stay on-machine
low-egress or offline work with local models (documented self-initiated calls: npm version check, models.dev metadata)
teaching agentic coding without vendor lock-in
BYO-key multi-provider terminal agent
notes: Community terminal agent (latest release v1.31.0, 2026-09-26; daily commits) with subagents, MCP, LSP tools, hooks, checkpointing, plan/architect modes and VS Code/ACP integration. v1.31.0 added an optional OS sandbox for shell commands and extended prompt scrubbing to tool results; a headless browser tool was merged on main after that release. GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION, but LICENSE.md and package.json state MIT. Privacy statements are project documentation, not an independent audit.
tier_gate: fully local model runtime (e.g., Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, vLLM) for regulated data

required_controls: Local-only provider configuration (e.g., Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, vLLM) on institution-controlled hardware; no cloud provider entries, including per-mode (modeProviders) and session-title (titleProvider) providers, and no cloud API keys in the environment.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Check the effective configuration in every working directory (nanocoder config list/diff): a project-level agents.config.json and NANOCODER_PROVIDERS are merged over the global file and can add providers or override nanocoder.* settings and disabledTools.

Block or allowlist network egress at host or network level and verify the block; account for the npm-registry version check (no setting to disable) and the models.dev metadata download; install a pinned version and update it centrally.
Remove network-capable tools via disabledTools (fetch_url, web_search) and approve each MCP server; review the browser tool once released.
Enable nanocoder.sandbox for execute_bash (macOS sandbox-exec, Linux bubblewrap; not supported on Windows) or run inside an isolated VM/container.
Keep sessions (30-day default) and logs on controlled encrypted storage; set sessions.retentionDays and NANOCODER_LOG_DISABLE_FILE per institutional policy.
residual_risks: No-telemetry statements are project documentation, not an independent network audit.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

A project-level agents.config.json in the working directory (for example in a cloned repository) is merged over the global configuration and can add providers or override nanocoder.* settings (including the sandbox) and disabledTools; the documented directory-trust prompt covers MCP servers and hooks, and whether it gates this file was not confirmed.
The OS sandbox does not restrict file reads and does not cover custom tools or MCP; headless and daemon-triggered runs execute tools without confirmation.
Open security-labelled issues on the project tracker as of 2026-10-10 (e.g., ACP sessions starting in auto-accept, fetch_url reaching internal addresses via DNS).
Local sessions, logs, semantic-memory files, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Qwen Code
deployment: local CLI (also desktop app, IDE extensions and an experimental local daemon/web UI via qwen serve); inference via cloud providers or local/self-hosted endpoints
model_backend: Multi-provider: Alibaba Model Studio (Coding Plan, Token Plan or standard API key; Beijing and international/Singapore endpoints); built-in third-party providers DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, Requesty; any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Vertex AI endpoint; local OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio). The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued 2026-04-15 and is no longer selectable.
data_handling_note: Docs state Qwen Code itself does not use prompts, code or responses for model training; training and retention follow the configured backend (own API key: that provider's terms; Alibaba Model Studio: Alibaba Cloud terms, whose international privacy page says customer data is never used for training but call data is stored, period not stated). Usage statistics are ON by default (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=true) and are sent to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; docs say they exclude prompts, responses, file content and PII, but the source also sends a pseudonymous installation ID, session ID, OS type/version, CLI version, model name and, for OpenAI-compatible auth (which includes local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio endpoints), the configured base URL. The ToS page's claim that API-key mode collects no additional data conflicts with this; disable with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false or QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false (the environment variable takes precedence). OpenTelemetry export is off by default; if enabled, logPrompts defaults to true. Automatic update checks and installations on startup (general.enableAutoUpdate) and a daily models.dev catalog download are also on by default (both can be switched off).

suitability_notes.personal: Only with a local/institution-hosted inference endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, an institutional OpenAI-compatible server) or a provider under an institutional DPA. Alibaba Model Studio (international) states no training on customer data but stores call data with no stated retention period; no DPA and no Beijing-region terms were reviewed here. Disable usage statistics (on by default).
suitability_notes.special: Only in a fully researcher/institution-controlled configuration: local CLI plus a local or institution-hosted inference endpoint (Ollama only in local-only mode) with every model role pinned to it, usage statistics disabled, automatic updates off, OpenTelemetry off or exported only to an institutional collector, the default-on web_fetch tool blocked by a deny rule, and Browser Use, Channels, Mem0, web search and remote MCP servers not used. Any commercial cloud backend is not acceptable.

pricing: Tool free and open source (Apache-2.0); free with local models. Inference is billed by the chosen backend. Alibaba Cloud international docs (updated 2026-09-28): Coding Plan Pro $50/month with limited slots (Lite closed; a Token Plan page says Pro is no longer available once sold out); Token Plan Personal Edition list prices $8-$80/month and Team Edition $30-$200/seat/month, with temporary discounts shown; pay-as-you-go API. Coding Plan and Token Plan Team keys are for interactive use only, not automated scripts. Beijing-region (CNY) prices not checked. The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued 2026-04-15.
academic: No academic or student program found on fetched Qwen Code or Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pages.
use_cases: terminal-based agentic coding with local open-weight models (Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio) for data-sensitive environments
scriptable headless code automation in pipelines (with a local endpoint or pay-as-you-go/own API key; Coding Plan keys are restricted to interactive use)
Qwen/Alibaba-ecosystem coding with the Model Studio Coding Plan or Token Plan
notes: Originally based on Gemini CLI v0.8.2 but independently developed since v0.1 with a multi-protocol provider layer, desktop app, agent plugins and its own release cadence - accepted as an independent open-source CLI agent, not a thin fork. Actively maintained: stable v0.25.0 on 2026-10-05, nightly/preview builds and daily commits. Since September: ToS/Privacy notice updated 2026-10-01 with a Chrome extension/Browser Use section; Browser Use (from v0.24.2) works in the signed-in Chrome profile and can pass page content, screenshots and cookies to the configured provider; Mem0 external memory bundled in v0.25.0; Channels relay sessions through Telegram, WeChat, DingTalk, Feishu and similar platforms. All are opt-in. Offline installation from a release archive with SHA256SUMS is documented.
tier_gate: local or institution-hosted endpoint + usage statistics off (default on) + web_fetch denied + no cloud integrations, for regulated data

required_controls: Point Qwen Code only at an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio) on the workstation or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, configured via modelProviders; no commercial cloud provider or Alibaba Model Studio entry or key in the configuration.

Pin every model role to that endpoint: set model.name to a local model, leave fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel and compactionModel empty (they then use the main model or, for vision, a same-provider model) or set them only to local models, leave imageModel empty, and do not configure subagents to use any other model. The settings docs state that advisorModel and visionModel send conversation content to the named model even when it uses another provider.
Keep cloud provider API keys out of the shell environment, .env files (Qwen Code auto-loads the first .env file it finds) and the env field of settings.json.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Disable usage statistics in two places: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false in the system settings file and QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false in the system-wide environment (default is enabled; events go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; the environment variable takes precedence over the setting, so a stray value of true re-enables collection).
Keep OpenTelemetry off (default) or export only to an institution-controlled collector with logPrompts=false.

Block the built-in web_fetch tool with a permissions.deny rule or tools.disabled (it is registered by default and only asks for confirmation in default approval mode); keep web search off; do not enable Browser Use, Channels, Mem0 or remote MCP servers for these sessions.
Keep artifact publishing at its default local mode (artifact.publisher=local); the source code also offers 'host' (user upload command) and 'oss' (Alibaba Cloud OSS upload) modes.

Set general.enableAutoUpdate=false (default true: update checks and installations on startup) and manage upgrades centrally; set QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=off in the shell environment to stop the daily models.dev download. On air-gapped hosts, install from a verified release archive (--archive with SHA256SUMS).

Enforce these settings in the system settings file (Linux /etc/qwen-code/settings.json, Windows C:\ProgramData\qwen-code\settings.json, macOS /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json), which overrides user and project settings. Before sensitive sessions, check the effective configuration: a project .qwen/settings.json overrides user settings, environment variables (including those loaded from .env files) override all settings files, and QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH can redirect the system file.

Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block before processing special-category data; on Linux, tools.executionSandbox with network "closed" can additionally confine tool commands.
residual_risks: Prompts and file contents go to whichever endpoint is configured; adding a cloud provider, switching models with /model or pointing a side-model setting (fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel, compactionModel) at another provider sends data off-host.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost baseUrl alone does not show that inference stays local.
Usage statistics default to on and include the configured base URL; a missed setting discloses endpoint metadata to Alibaba Cloud.
web_fetch is available by default and auto-approval modes can approve it without a prompt, so a missing deny rule lets the model fetch external URLs.
Browser Use operates in the signed-in Chrome profile and can capture page text, screenshots and cookies.
Local sessions, logs, memory and tool outputs under ~/.qwen require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Fast release cadence: defaults and integrations change often, so settings need re-checking after each upgrade.

name: Factory (Droids)
vendor: Factory (factory.com; website moved from factory.ai, product and API hosts remain *.factory.ai)
deployment: cloud-managed (Factory-operated control plane in the US, or in a Factory-operated EEA region on Enterprise; Droid runs on local or customer machines, CI or Factory-hosted Droid Computers) / enterprise customer-operated hybrid or fully air-gapped build / Factory Private: control plane in customer VPC or on-premises, air-gapped configurations available (private preview)
model_backend: Factory-managed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI plus a Droid Core open-weight pool, with an optional automatic Factory Router. BYOK custom models cover provider keys, cloud AI platforms (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI), OpenAI-compatible gateways and local servers such as Ollama or LM Studio. Airgap builds use only customer-configured models. Model availability and multipliers change.
data_handling_note: Factory states customer code is not used as training data. Individual terms (14 Jul 2026) let Factory use Customer Data internally to provide the service and to generate aggregated de-identified data, which it may freely use and retain for business purposes including improving its products. Product-level retention: CLI sessions are mirrored to Factory cloud by default (cloudSessionSync true; users can switch it off, org admins can pin it); forked sessions and AutoWiki content (wikiCloudSync, on by default) also sync to Factory cloud. Orgs can turn on auto-deletion of synced sessions after 14-365 days (sessionRetentionDays); no default deletion period is published. Factory-hosted operational logs follow Trust Center terms, which are not publicly readable. Personal data (privacy policy, 20 Aug 2026) is primarily stored on AWS US West and deleted no later than 10 years after last use unless contracted otherwise. ZDR is listed for Business and above; its scope relative to session sync is a contract question.
