Mythos-class Anthropic models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Telemetry: in connected deployments OTEL metrics (with user, session and repo attributes unless aggregate granularity is pinned) also go to Factory's collector; message-content spans are off by default and go only to a customer collector. Airgap builds send no runtime data to Factory.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Business/Enterprise contract with the DPA (EU SCCs; EU-region deployment for residency on Enterprise), and confirm its annex covers the research data subjects and data categories: the public annex lists only customers' end-users, staff and contractors, with contact and service-generated data. Switch off cloud session sync and AutoWiki cloud sync, or turn on a short sessionRetentionDays; restrict models to ZDR-covered endpoints and avoid opt-in Mythos-class retention; keep message-content telemetry off or on an institutional collector. Inference-layer ZDR alone is insufficient.
suitability_notes.special: Qualifying routes are the sales-gated enterprise airgap build, or a hybrid deployment with in-network models and collectors and cloud sync off; in connected (non-airgap) builds, OTEL metrics still reach Factory's collector. Factory Private (customer VPC/on-prem; announced 18 Sep 2026, private preview, no docs page) may qualify only once documentation or the contract places the control plane, inference and collectors inside institution-controlled infrastructure. Factory states Airgap Mode is cooperative, so isolation must come from institutional network controls. Managed cloud, Factory-hosted Droid Computers and the public DPA (which lists no special-category data) do not qualify.

compliance: Vendor-stated SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 (docs); reports are gated in the Trust Center and were not reviewed.
Public DPA (last updated 2 Sep 2026) with EU SCCs; its Annex lists no special-category personal data.
Public BAA template (last updated 29 Apr 2026); a BAA does not make cloud routes suitable for special-category data in this catalog.
Enterprise EU deployment keeps session content in the EEA; organization records, user profiles and billing data remain in the US deployment.
pricing: Pro $20/month, Plus $100, Max $200 (rolling 5-hour, 7-day and 30-day rate limits; prepaid Extra Usage from $10; Droid Core open-weight pool after Standard Usage; BYOK free up to an allowance). Teams $60/month per team plus $40/seat, up to 10 seats. Business and Enterprise custom: Business lists ZDR, SSO/SCIM and audit logs; Enterprise adds dedicated compute with partitioned inference, on-premise options and data residency. Factory Private and airgap builds are sales-gated. Confirm contract, model exceptions and session retention.
academic: Factory for Science offers free Droid access by application: personal licences for graduate students, postdocs and independent researchers (institutional email or evidence of active research) and team licences with admin controls for labs and institutions. The plan tier, usage limits and which privacy controls (ZDR, session sync/retention settings) apply are not published. A separate free-access application exists for open-source contributors.
use_cases: hosted or local asynchronous coding agents opening PRs from chat- or tracker-assigned tasks
air-gapped/on-prem autonomous coding for security-sensitive institutional codebases
enterprise-governed multi-agent software maintenance (code review, QA, incident response)
notes: Droid agents across the Factory App (desktop), Droid CLI, SDKs, headless exec and Slack/Linear/Jira/Teams delegations; Factory-hosted Droid Computers provide remote compute. The agent loop runs where Droid is installed, while model calls, session sync and metrics leave the machine in connected deployments. Docs describe cloud-managed (US or Factory-operated EU region), hybrid and fully air-gapped patterns; Factory Private (announced 18 Sep 2026, private preview) adds customer-VPC/on-prem control planes. Website moved to factory.com; service hosts remain *.factory.ai. Releases are near-daily (CLI v0.237.0, 9 Oct 2026).
tier_gate: special-category data: enterprise airgap build, or enterprise hybrid deployment with in-network models and collectors and cloud sync off (Factory Private only once documented or contracted; private preview); personal data: Business/Enterprise contract (ZDR, DPA with an annex covering the research data) with session sync off or short retention

required_controls: Use the enterprise airgap build, or a hybrid deployment with model endpoints, OTEL collectors and any session storage inside institution-controlled infrastructure; use Factory Private only after its documentation or contract establishes the same boundary.

Restrict models to in-network custom endpoints (modelPolicy allowedBaseUrls/allowCustomModels; airgap builds offer only customModels), and confirm a localhost Ollama endpoint is not serving Ollama Cloud models. Disable Factory-managed models, the Factory Router, cloud session sync, AutoWiki cloud sync (wikiCloudSync) and Factory-hosted Droid Computers.
In hybrid (connected) builds, pin telemetry.granularity: aggregate, because metrics also go to Factory's collector and there is no documented way to switch that off.
Enforce network isolation and sandbox egress rules, because Factory describes Airgap Mode as cooperative rather than an enforcement mechanism.
Limit MCP servers, plugins, hooks, web search/fetch tools and external integrations to in-boundary destinations.
residual_risks: Airgap builds and Factory Private are sales-gated. Factory Private is in private preview and has no page in the docs index, only an announcement.

Connected (non-airgap) deployments always send OTEL metrics to Factory's collector (session, model, tool and repo attributes; user identity unless aggregate), and hybrid LLM traffic may go to cloud providers unless restricted to in-network endpoints.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls; opt-in message-content spans are exported raw without redaction.
The agent can run arbitrary commands, so the boundary depends on the institution's network and sandbox policy.
Factory's BYOK docs state that Ollama Cloud models work through the same localhost Ollama endpoint, so a localhost base URL alone does not prove local inference.

name: Roomote
deployment: Roomote Cloud: one single-tenant deployment per workspace on Railway with task sandboxes at Modal, US-hosted. Self-hosted: one-command Docker Compose install on an own Linux server or VM (public HTTPS, or a private network with internal TLS per the operator reference), with local Docker task sandboxes by default. Railway/Render templates and hosted sandbox backends (Modal, E2B, Daytona, Blaxel, Box, Azure Container Apps) move hosting or execution to provider infrastructure.
model_backend: BYOK direct APIs (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Azure), gateways (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Vercel AI Gateway, Requesty) and linked subscriptions (e.g. ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot); self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, vLLM, generic /v1) are documented with setup pages, and every model role can inherit the coding model. Coding tasks use an embedded OpenCode harness and need tool-calling models. Optional judgment model: TypeSafe/OpenRouter/Vercel routes, a Roomote-operated service, or a local CPU sidecar on self-hosted stacks.
data_handling_note: Cloud (Cloud Privacy Policy and DPA, both last updated 2026-07-23): Customer Content (repositories, prompts, tasks, model outputs, integration credentials, logs, artifacts) is processed under a DPA with SCCs; 'We never use Customer Content to train AI models'. BYOK inference goes from the deployment to the customer-configured provider under the customer's own terms (model providers are not subprocessors). The managed 'Roomote inference' trial credit and the Roomote-operated judgment model are documented in the product docs but not in the Cloud Privacy Policy or subprocessor list, so their provider and retention are UNVERIFIED. Workspace deletion destroys the deployment and its backups; unconverted trials are deleted 7 days after expiry; account metadata up to 30 days; billing records up to 7 years. Subprocessors: Railway, Modal, Vercel, Resend, Stripe, Google, PostHog, Intercom (all US). Cloud usage telemetry (deployment ID, user counts, version) and anonymous analytics cannot be disabled. No SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Memory (optional; enabled on new Cloud deployments, off on self-hosted until enabled) gets embeddings through an OpenRouter or OpenAI key unless a self-run embeddings upstream is configured. Self-hosted: data stays on the operator's infrastructure and the providers it connects; content-free anonymous telemetry (usage events, daily instance report) is on by default and admin-disableable; a daily version check (instance ID and version) is documented as not optional; licensed (>10-user) deployments send licence/user-count data to Roomote even with analytics off (docs: activation with Roomote Cloud; operator reference: licence ID and registered-user count to the Ping service; the two sources conflict on mechanism).

suitability_notes.personal: Cloud: DPA with SCCs, US hosting, single-tenant deployment; BYOK inference runs under your own provider contract; no SOC 2/ISO 27001. Avoid the managed Roomote inference trial credit and the Roomote-operated judgment model for personal data: the Cloud Privacy Policy and subprocessor list state that Roomote is not in the inference path and do not describe either route. Memory, enabled on new Cloud deployments, sends content for embedding through the configured OpenRouter or OpenAI key, so that provider contract must cover it. Self-hosted: disable anonymous telemetry and use an institution-approved inference provider or local endpoint. Local Docker execution alone does not keep model traffic in the institution.
suitability_notes.special: Self-hosted route only: institution-controlled Linux host reached over a private network only (internal TLS; no Cloudflare or other third-party tunnel), local Docker sandboxes with egress=none, every model role pointed at an institution-run Ollama (local-only mode), vLLM or OpenAI-compatible endpoint that forwards nothing to external providers, and Memory off or run with local embeddings. Roomote Cloud, Railway/Render templates, hosted sandbox backends and cloud inference providers do not qualify. Documented configuration only; not tested hands-on.

pricing: Cloud: $49/mo up to 10 users, $249/mo for 11-50, $499/mo for 51-100, 100+ by contact; 7-day free trial without a card (includes a $5 managed-inference credit). Self-hosted: free up to 10 registered users with no licence key; $249/mo for 11-50 users; $499/mo for 51-100 users; 100+ by contact. Inference costs separate (BYOK).
academic: No academic or student programme found on first-party pages. FCL-1.0-ALv2 permits any non-competing use and explicitly names internal use, non-commercial education and non-commercial research; self-hosting is free up to 10 registered users.
use_cases: chat-assigned background coding tasks returned as reviewable PRs
self-hosted institutional coding agent where repositories (on self-managed GitLab or Gitea), task sandboxes and (via Ollama or vLLM) model inference stay on university infrastructure
team-shared agent fleet with cost analytics across BYOK inference providers
notes: Asynchronous, single-tenant coding-agent service with self-hosted execution; very active development (v1.17.0 on 2026-10-08, several releases per week), so re-check settings after upgrades. FCL-1.0-ALv2 is source-available: no competing commercial service and no bypassing the 10-user licence key; each release converts to Apache-2.0 on its second anniversary. A self-hosted sandbox alone does not make inference local: the special-category route depends on pointing every model role at an institution-run endpoint.
tier_gate: Special-category data: self-hosted deployment reached over a private network only (no third-party tunnel), with an institution-run inference endpoint that forwards nothing to external providers for all model roles (Ollama in local-only mode), telemetry off, sandbox egress=none, and Memory off or locally embedded. A licensed (>10-user) deployment reports licence/user-count data to Roomote; the docs site says paid seats need a current Roomote Cloud activation lease (up to 72 h), while the operator reference says keys are verified offline. Personal data: self-hosted or Cloud with an appropriate model-provider contract (not the managed Roomote inference credit). Cloud: non-sensitive and personal only.

required_controls: Self-host on an institution-controlled Linux server or VM (one-command installer); do not use Roomote Cloud or the Railway/Render templates
Reach the deployment over the private network only (--tls-mode internal, clients trust Caddy's local CA); do not front it with Cloudflare Tunnel or another third-party tunnel
Keep the default local Docker sandbox provider; do not configure hosted sandbox backends (Modal, E2B, Daytona, Blaxel, Box, Azure)
Set DOCKER_WORKER_EGRESS_POLICY=none

Connect only an institution-run Ollama, vLLM or OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a private network; remove every other inference provider (including any managed Roomote inference) and set every model role (coding, orchestration, helper, vision, audio/video, review, explore, advisor) and any fallback to it

The endpoint must serve only models hosted on institution-controlled hardware and must not forward requests to external providers (a LiteLLM-style gateway qualifies only if it meets this); verify with egress monitoring

If the endpoint is Ollama, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models
Set the judgment model to off or the local CPU sidecar (COMPOSE_PROFILES=judgment); leave TypeSafe/OpenRouter/Vercel judgment routes and Jev-based experiments disabled

Leave Memory disabled (the self-hosted default), or run it with local embeddings (COMPOSE_PROFILES=brain,local-inference) and the helper role on the institution endpoint; do not configure OpenRouter/OpenAI R_BRAIN_* keys
Keep no cloud provider API keys (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TypeSafe or R_BRAIN_* keys) in the deployment environment or .env
Turn off anonymous telemetry in Settings > Deployment
Use self-managed Git (GitLab with GITLAB_BASE_URL, or Gitea) and email/password sign-in; leave Slack/Teams/Telegram/Discord/email, web search (Exa), voice and third-party integrations unconfigured

Enforce egress at host or network level (allow only the institution inference endpoint, self-managed Git and any Roomote metadata endpoints the DPO accepts; open image pulls only in a controlled install/upgrade window) and verify it with egress monitoring

Decide with the DPO whether the metadata-only daily version check (and, on licensed >10-user deployments, licence/user-count reporting) may leave the network; the effect of blocking or redirecting it via R_PING_BASE_URL is undocumented, and the licence forbids circumventing licence-key functionality
Run upgrades as deliberate operator actions and re-verify the effective configuration (Settings and environment) after setup and after every upgrade
Obtain institutional DPO/IRB approval before processing special-category data
residual_risks: A daily version check to Roomote's ping service (instance ID and version) is documented as not optional; R_PING_BASE_URL is configurable, but behaviour when the check is blocked or redirected is not documented

First-party sources conflict on licensing: the docs Users page says paid keys are activated with Roomote Cloud (lease up to 72 hours, otherwise the free 10-user limit applies), while the operator reference says keys are verified offline and licensed deployments report licence ID and registered-user count to Roomote's Ping service even with analytics off

The operator reference prerequisites still list a stable public HTTPS origin, a required GitHub App and Slack/Teams sign-in, and the docs source-control checklist assumes a public HTTPS URL, so a fully private deployment with self-managed GitLab/Gitea is assembled from several pages, not documented end to end
Whether task sandboxes can clone from a private-network GitLab under egress=none is not documented (Gitea clone traffic is documented as routed through a local proxy)
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same local endpoint, so pointing Roomote at Ollama does not by itself keep inference local
Installer and upgrades pull images from GitHub Container Registry and the judgment sidecar downloads its model from Hugging Face; no offline or mirrored installation is documented
Docker sandboxes share the host and the documentation says they are not a multi-tenant isolation boundary
Agent quality on local models depends on tool-calling support and hardware; Roomote's recommended model catalog targets cloud providers
Network behaviour of the embedded OpenCode harness, including any built-in web fetch tool, was not separately reviewed; sandbox egress=none and host-level egress blocking are the backstop
Rapid release cadence can change defaults; re-verify configuration after each upgrade

name: GitLab Duo Agent Platform
deployment: GitLab.com (SaaS); GitLab Dedicated (vendor-operated single-tenant SaaS); Self-Managed (customer-operated) with GitLab-managed, hybrid or fully self-hosted AI Gateway and models, including offline licences. Not available on GitLab Dedicated for Government.
model_backend: GitLab-managed models via GitLab's AI Gateway (Anthropic Claude, with current defaults served through Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; OpenAI GPT; Google Gemini; Fireworks-hosted Codestral; open-weight GLM, Kimi, MiniMax). Defaults can change without notice. On Self-Managed: a self-hosted AI Gateway with customer-served models (e.g. vLLM) or customer cloud endpoints (Bedrock, Azure OpenAI). Hybrid features and Duo Core use GitLab's gateway; offline licences cannot use GitLab-managed models.
data_handling_note: GitLab does not train generative AI models; AI model sub-processors are barred from training on input/output. Product retention: chat and workflow history (chats user-deletable), also kept on GitLab.com for anti-abuse; expanded logging keeps traces; opt-in usage-data collection logs full prompts, responses and tool calls (with a self-hosted gateway these logs stay on customer infrastructure). GitLab documents a ZDR policy only with Fireworks AI, and it does not hold when prompt caching is on, which is the default (vendor holds prompts temporarily in memory; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models). Certain Anthropic and OpenAI models have limited vendor-side retention. Prompt-injection scanning via HiddenLayer runs on GitLab's AI Gateway and defaults to Log only on GitLab.com; 'No checks' sends no prompt data to third parties. Telemetry: aggregated or de-identified Snowplow usage metrics. A self-hosted AI Gateway keeps code, prompts and responses in the customer network; online licences still send billing metadata to GitLab, offline licences do not connect.

suitability_notes.personal: Accept GitLab's DPA/SCCs; review chat/workflow history and GitLab.com anti-abuse retention; keep usage-data collection and expanded logging off unless approved; decide on HiddenLayer prompt scanning and prompt caching (on by default; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models); prefer models without vendor-side retention, or self-hosted models.
suitability_notes.special: Only Self-Managed Premium/Ultimate with a fully self-hosted AI Gateway and on-premises models (offline licence preferred); no hybrid GitLab-managed features, Duo Core or cloud LLM backends; flows on institution runners with an internally mirrored executor image that includes duo-cli; editor-extension telemetry off.

compliance: Trust Center lists SOC 2 (GitLab.com, Dedicated), ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018, ISO/IEC 42001, CSA STAR and TISAX; documents gated, AI scope unverified
GitLab DPA with SCCs and public sub-processor list (AI: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS, Fireworks AI, HiddenLayer)
pricing: Premium $29/user/month billed annually; Ultimate custom. Agent Platform consumes GitLab Credits ($1/credit on-demand list price; commitment pools with volume discounts). Premium/Ultimate include $12/$24 credits per user/month as a limited-time promotion; Free tier can buy credits. Offline self-hosted use requires the Agent Platform Self-Hosted add-on under a flat-fee ELA.
academic: GitLab for Education: free Ultimate (unlimited seats, SaaS or Self-Managed) for accredited non-profit institutions, for teaching and non-commercial research only. Community-program subscriptions get no included credits; Agent Platform needs purchased or evaluation credits.
use_cases: automating issue-to-merge-request development flows on institutional GitLab instances
code review and CI/CD pipeline repair agents on research software repositories
air-gapped agentic coding on Self-Managed GitLab with self-hosted open-weight models for sensitive codebases
notes: Agentic software-lifecycle platform inside GitLab (foundational, custom and external agents, flows run as CI/CD jobs, Agentic Chat in UI/IDE/CLI, MCP client and server), GA since GitLab 18.8 (2026-01-15); actively developed (19.4, September 2026). Code is under the source-visible GitLab EE licence. Only Self-Managed with a fully self-hosted gateway and on-premises models qualifies for special-category data.
tier_gate: Premium/Ultimate (Free with purchased credits); special-category data only on Self-Managed with self-hosted AI Gateway and on-premises models

required_controls: Self-Managed Premium/Ultimate with a fully self-hosted AI Gateway on institution infrastructure; every model endpoint it calls is served on institution-controlled hardware inside the network (same host or separate inference servers, e.g. vLLM); no hybrid GitLab-managed features, no Bedrock/Azure OpenAI or other external model endpoints.
Offline licence (cloud-licensing exemption, Agent Platform Self-Hosted add-on, ELA) where no GitLab connection is acceptable; online licences must reach GitLab billing endpoints.
Duo Core off (it needs GitLab's AI Gateway); GitLab.com and vendor-operated GitLab Dedicated are not acceptable.

Flows only on institution runners using an executor image mirrored to an internal registry and pinned, v0.0.11+ (or custom) with duo-cli included, so jobs do not fetch duo-cli from gitlab.com or the image from registry.gitlab.com.
Editor-extension telemetry turned off (VS Code telemetry level 'off') on researcher machines.
residual_risks: Online licences send billing metadata (instance ID, hashed user ID, call count, timestamp) to GitLab; GitLab states prompts, code and responses stay in the network.
Chat/workflow history, expanded-logging traces and AI Gateway logs persist on the instance and need institutional retention, access and deletion controls.
IDE/CLI agents lack network egress controls unless the experimental local sandbox (off by default) is on; MCP servers, external agents and Slack integration can move data out.
GitLab editor extensions send usage and error telemetry to GitLab according to the editor's telemetry setting; whether Duo Snowplow telemetry is emitted from Self-Managed instances is not documented.

name: Clusy
deployment: cloud
model_backend: Plan-gated hosted models from DeepSeek (default Auto; mainland China), Moonshot, Alibaba (Qwen, Singapore), Cloudflare Workers AI (Kimi, GLM), AWS Bedrock (Claude) and Azure OpenAI (GPT); Claude and most GPT models need Max. BYOK for Anthropic/OpenAI keys on any plan; an optional local runner drives the user's own Claude Code/Codex CLI, with inference still at Anthropic/OpenAI. No local or self-hosted model route is documented.
data_handling_note: Clusy states it does not train, fine-tune or distil models on customer notebooks, prompts, chat or outputs. It does not send no-training/zero-retention instructions to every provider; provider-side training/retention on the default DeepSeek route is not established. Default Auto and inline completions (on by default; can be disabled in Settings > Models) use DeepSeek (mainland China). Per the Privacy Policy, a hosted-model turn whose provider fails is retried on DeepSeek whatever model was selected (local-runner docs say a dropped runner fails the turn instead; BYOK docs do not address fallback). Titles/tags and memory embeddings go to AWS Bedrock. Where a public IP is available, prompts carry it and an approximate location (opt-out by email). Hosted Fable 5.1 requests may be retained by AWS for up to 30 days for misuse review. BYOK applies the user's provider terms (key stored encrypted). Notebooks, files, chat and outputs persist until deletion; sub-agent logs 30 days; the performance-trace archive and security records have no set expiry. In-app PostHog analytics run by default (exclusion by email request). The local runner is a credential boundary, not a data boundary.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Suitable for public, anonymised or synthetic data. On Free the built-in model is locked to Auto (DeepSeek, mainland China); avoiding China routing there needs BYOK or the local runner. On every plan, inline completions (on by default) use DeepSeek unless disabled, and provider-failure fallback for hosted models can send a turn to DeepSeek; check institutional third-country or export rules even for non-sensitive work.
suitability_notes.personal: No personal-data recommendation: own-service no-training is documented, but provider controls are non-uniform, fallback can reach DeepSeek in mainland China without user choice, and content/trace retention remains material. A DPA is offered on request; institutional review would still be required.
suitability_notes.special: Terms prohibit GDPR special-category data and HIPAA PHI without a separate written agreement, and Clusy signs no BAAs. Execution and inference are cloud-only; the local runner does not keep data off Clusy's cloud.

pricing: Free $0; Plus $12/month; Pro $30/month; Max $90/month (10x Plus usage) or $200/month (30x); Enterprise by call (higher limits, dedicated capacity, SSO, custom billing). Models, GPUs, RAM and checkpoint storage vary by tier. The pricing page lists paused-sandbox retention (Free released after 3 days, paid 'indefinite'), but docs say there is no guaranteed retention period; Terms and docs also disagree on whether the default model and CPU are unmetered on paid plans.
academic: No academic or student program on pricing, product or documentation pages; Terms mention only discretionary promotional or sponsorship credits.
use_cases: exploratory ML experiments on public or non-sensitive datasets with agent-driven notebook execution
parallel branched model-architecture comparisons on rented GPUs
agentic analysis over non-sensitive Databricks/Snowflake tables
R or Python statistical analysis of public datasets in agent-driven notebooks
notes: Privacy Policy revised 23 Sep 2026 (minor: Opus 5.5 added to the safety-filter retry, second Azure region); Terms text changed after 12 Sep without a new 'last updated' date. Since September: native R notebooks and an in-sandbox terminal whose recent commands and output are summarised to the agent. Sandboxes reach the public internet: GPU sandboxes have no outbound restriction and Clusy does not inspect what a sandbox sends; connecting GitHub clones repositories, including private ones, to Clusy's servers. No SOC 2/ISO 27001 certification; DPA on request; no HIPAA BAA. An October engineering blog says a local/remote execution bridge will 'soon' deploy; not documented as a product feature. Retained cautiously for public/nonsensitive work; no personal or special-category route approved.
tier_gate: no qualifying route; personal data would at minimum need a signed DPA, a written commitment excluding mainland-China routing (Clusy says the product alone cannot guarantee this) and institutional review; Enterprise terms are not public. Special-category data is excluded by the Terms without a separate written agreement, and no route qualifies even with one because execution and inference run only in vendor-operated cloud.

residual_risks: Cloud control/provider processing remains outside customer-controlled infrastructure; paired-machine execution does not establish a local-only route.
Code runs only in third-party E2B (CPU) and Modal (GPU) sandboxes operated for Clusy; the documented local runner is a credential boundary, not a data boundary.
Terms exclude GDPR special-category data and HIPAA PHI without a separate written agreement; no BAAs are signed.

Per the Privacy Policy, provider-failure fallback for hosted models can send a turn to DeepSeek in mainland China regardless of the selected model; inline completions also go to DeepSeek unless disabled.

name: Ada (Automated Data Analyst)
vendor: Sainesh Nakra (independent open-source project; GitHub: saineshnakra)
deployment: Local or self-hosted Streamlit app on researcher/institution hardware; the public demo runs on Streamlit's hosted servers (streamlit.app)
model_backend: None required (deterministic pandas calculations). Optional OpenAI API layer (Responses API, needs a key) for a query-planner fallback and a narrative 'strategic read' only. The strategic read is button-triggered; the planner call fires automatically when a submitted Ask ADA question cannot be rule-parsed and a key is present (the user then confirms the returned plan before local execution). ADA documents no other provider, custom endpoint or local-model option.
data_handling_note: Without a key, parsing, cleaning, schema detection, charts, anomaly/forecast and rule-parsed Ask ADA answers are computed in-process with pandas (docs/privacy.md). Uploads stay in memory and are not written to disk; parsed files sit in a server-process cache (at most 8 files, up to 1 hour) that is not tied to the browser session and clears on restart. With the optional OpenAI layer, the planner receives the typed question plus column names, types and roles; it is called automatically when a key is present and a submitted question cannot be rule-parsed (the user then confirms the returned plan before local execution). The strategic read is button-triggered and receives typed context, schema, computed summary, evidence and recommendations. Raw rows are not sent, but evidence sentences can name segment labels (e.g. a customer or product name). Requests set store=False and send a hashed session identifier; OpenAI's API terms still apply (no training by default; abuse-monitoring logs kept up to 30 days unless OpenAI approves ZDR). Framework and browser requests: pinned Streamlit 1.59.2 sends usage statistics by default (browser.gatherUsageStats = true) and the repo config does not turn this off; with the repo's server.headless = true and no server.address set, Streamlit looks up the host's external IP at checkip.amazonaws.com on startup (server-side; reveals the host IP, not data); the app stylesheet loads Google Fonts in the browser (fonts.googleapis.com, with font files from fonts.gstatic.com). The docs' 'no network call' statement therefore holds for ADA's own code, not for these framework/browser requests. SECURITY.md: the no-raw-row boundary does not make a public hosted app an approved environment for regulated data.

suitability_notes.personal: Run locally or on an institution-controlled server; do not use the public hosted demo. Keep the OpenAI layer off for identifiable data: evidence sent to OpenAI can name segment labels such as person names, and with a key present a typed question that the rule parser cannot read is sent to the planner on submit. Set browser.gatherUsageStats = false.
suitability_notes.special: Only customer-operated execution with no OpenAI key configured and egress to the OpenAI API blocked (the sidebar key field stays open to any user), Streamlit usage statistics disabled, server.address bound (e.g. 127.0.0.1) or outbound traffic blocked so Streamlit's external-IP lookup cannot leave the host, browser font requests (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com) blocked or accepted, and the server-process upload cache access-controlled on shared hosts.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free (MIT-licensed open source). Optional OpenAI API usage is billed to whichever OpenAI key is configured (the user's own key, or a deployment owner's server key).
academic: No academic programme; the software is free under the MIT licence.
use_cases: quick exploratory analysis of tabular research data without sending anything to an LLM
natural-language questions over CSV/Excel with auditable deterministic calculations
teaching example of a privacy-first LLM-optional analysis architecture
notes: Single-maintainer community project built around business-style tables (a measure, a date, a segment); last maintainer commit 2026-09-21, no tagged releases. Deterministic local core; the optional OpenAI planner proposes a plan that is validated against the data and confirmed by the user before local execution, and model-generated code is never executed. The qualifying route keeps the OpenAI layer off and governs Streamlit telemetry, outbound requests, hosting, the upload cache and logs.
tier_gate: fully local or institution-hosted run with no OpenAI key, Streamlit usage statistics off and outbound traffic blocked, for regulated data

required_controls: Run on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware; bind to localhost (server.address = 127.0.0.1) or place behind institutional authentication. Setting server.address to a specific address (not 0.0.0.0 or ::) also stops Streamlit's headless startup lookup of the host's external IP at checkip.amazonaws.com.
Configure no OPENAI_API_KEY (environment or .streamlit/secrets.toml) and block egress to the OpenAI API, because the sidebar key field lets any user enable the optional layer.

Set browser.gatherUsageStats = false in .streamlit/config.toml (Streamlit default is true; the repo config does not set it), and check the effective configuration on the running host as well as the repo file.

Block or explicitly accept browser requests to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com loaded by the app stylesheet; block all other egress from the host at host or network level and verify that the block works.
Govern the server-process upload cache (at most 8 files, 1-hour TTL, cleared on restart), session memory, host logs and retention.
residual_risks: Single-maintainer project with no stated support commitment; security fixes land only on the latest commit of main (SECURITY.md).
Pins Streamlit 1.59.2 while upstream is at 1.65.0 (2026-10-02); framework updates depend on the maintainer.
On a shared deployment the parsed-upload cache belongs to the server process, not to one user's session.
Local sessions, logs, the host and its network need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Microsoft Copilot Analyst
deployment: cloud (Microsoft 365 tenant service boundary)
model_backend: Reasoning model with Python execution; the current Analyst model and its operator are not documented. Microsoft Copilot draws on Microsoft-hosted models (e.g. Azure OpenAI) and AI subprocessors whose use admins can switch per tenant (OpenAI-operated models, on by default for eligible commercial tenants; Anthropic models, on by default outside EU/EFTA/UK). Microsoft says OpenAI-operated models serve the same GPT-based Copilot experiences. The 2025 launch and GA posts named OpenAI o3-mini; treat that as historical.
data_handling_note: Microsoft states Analyst runs inside the Microsoft 365 commercial data processing boundary and inherits Microsoft 365 privacy, security and compliance commitments. Prompts, responses and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train foundation LLMs; interactions are stored encrypted as Copilot activity history in the tenant, governed by Purview retention policies and user deletion. Optional user feedback may be used to improve Copilot (not foundation-model training) and is admin-controllable. Copilot opted out of Azure OpenAI abuse-monitoring human review; Anthropic models carry Anthropic-operated safeguards to detect illegal content. Models are Microsoft-hosted or come from AI subprocessors under Microsoft's DPA: OpenAI-operated models (on by default for eligible commercial tenants since 24 Jul 2026; in the EU Data Boundary with documented exceptions; outside in-country processing commitments; in certain Copilot experiences OpenAI's Responses API is used with ZDR subject to OpenAI's limits) and Anthropic models (on by default for most commercial tenants outside EU/EFTA/UK, off by default inside them; excluded from the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments). Admins can also opt in to 'Anthropic models with Data Retention', processed by Anthropic as an independent processor outside Microsoft's DPA with up to 30-day retention (longer if flagged); the fetched Microsoft docs do not say whether Analyst can use them. LLM calls can route to other regions under high load; EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary (Anthropic models excepted). Python-sandbox data handling is not separately documented (unverified).

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional tenant with a Copilot licence, the Microsoft DPA and Purview retention. Keep AI independent-processor model routes disabled, including 'Anthropic models with Data Retention' (processed by Anthropic outside Microsoft's DPA), and review the tenant's AI-subprocessor settings: Anthropic models sit outside the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments, and OpenAI-operated models sit outside in-country processing commitments.
suitability_notes.special: Microsoft-operated cloud is not researcher/institution-controlled infrastructure; HIPAA/GDPR/ISO claims and the tenant service boundary do not change that under this catalog's rules. No local or self-hosted option exists.

compliance: Microsoft organizational data protection and compliance scope depend on tenant, region, model and contract.

Microsoft's Copilot privacy page lists GDPR, ISO 27001, HIPAA and ISO 42001 offerings for Microsoft Copilot; certifications for OpenAI-operated subprocessor models are maintained by OpenAI, and 'Anthropic models with Data Retention' fall under Anthropic's own terms and DPA.
pricing: Analyst is included in the Microsoft Copilot user subscription license (USL), which requires a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan and carries fair-use usage limits. In posts dated 23 and 25 Sep 2026 Microsoft describes pairing the USL with usage-based billing (UBB) in Copilot Credits for Cowork, Code, Autopilot, new advanced experiences in apps and frontier models (no effective date stated); for enterprise customers UBB stays off until an admin creates a spending policy. US list prices on 2026-10-10: Microsoft 365 Copilot (enterprise) USD 30.00/user/month paid yearly (USD 31.50 paid monthly); Microsoft 365 Copilot Business add-on (eligible Business plans, up to 300 users) USD 21.00/user/month paid yearly, promotional USD 18.00 for the first year (offer 1 Jul-31 Dec 2026). Regional prices vary; confirm the institutional licence.
academic: Microsoft's education page lists Microsoft 365 Copilot as an academic offering at USD 18 per user/month (footnote: US prices accurate as of October 2025; regional prices vary). That page does not name Analyst; Microsoft states Analyst comes with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and is reached with a work or school account. Confirm EDU SKU contents and local price with the institution's licensing partner.
use_cases: statistical analysis of institutional spreadsheets and uploaded datasets inside the university M365 tenant
chain-of-thought data exploration with inspectable Python code
report/insight generation grounded in tenant documents under existing M365 governance
notes: Organizational cloud data analyst with inspectable Python execution, included in the per-user Copilot licence (USL) under Microsoft's September 2026 pricing model. Product family now branded Microsoft Copilot. Check the tenant's AI-subprocessor settings before personal-data use; organizational no-training does not make vendor-cloud processing a controlled-infrastructure route.
tier_gate: Copilot USL licence on a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan; for personal data: institutional tenant + Microsoft DPA + Purview retention, with AI independent-processor model routes (incl. 'Anthropic models with Data Retention') left off

residual_risks: Microsoft-operated cloud is not researcher/institution-controlled infrastructure; HIPAA/GDPR/ISO claims and the tenant service boundary do not change that under this catalog's rules. No local or self-hosted option exists.

name: Zerve
deployment: Zerve SaaS / BYOC with the Zerve-hosted control plane: execution and storage in the customer's AWS account (self-serve CloudFormation on Pro and Team) or on an existing GKE or AKS cluster (plan not stated in docs; pricing lists multi-cloud hosting under Enterprise) / Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed: whole platform via private Helm chart on customer Kubernetes, on-premises or own cloud, with a documented air-gapped pattern
model_backend: SaaS agent models are selectable in Model Settings (docs: Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock). The pricing FAQ lists BYOK for OpenAI and Anthropic, with other providers or self-hosted models on request. Self-Managed supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, or any customer-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway. Public docs name no validated self-hosted model.
data_handling_note: The Terms of Service (effective 9 Jan 2026) let Zerve use Customer Data only as needed to provide, operate and maintain the product. Product improvement may use statistical data derived from use of the product, but not Customer Data itself. No AI-specific training, prompt-retention or ZDR statement was found, and training and retention by the managed model providers are undocumented, so data handling stays unknown. The privacy policy (effective 22 Jan 2024) says the Services are hosted in the US and that personal data is kept while the account is open. It names analytics subprocessors and lists OpenAI and Exafunction (Codeium) as AI subprocessors; Anthropic, a model provider named in the product docs, is not listed. The Terms reserve Zerve's right to keep residual copies of Customer Data for backup purposes. BYOC keeps execution and storage in the customer cloud but uses the Zerve-hosted control plane (the AWS BYOC doc places it in eu-west-1). Hosting location is inconsistent across first-party sources: the 2024 privacy policy says the Services are hosted in the US; the AWS BYOC doc puts the control plane in eu-west-1. Self-Managed runs the whole platform in the customer environment and can route all agent traffic through a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible gateway.

suitability_notes.personal: Use SaaS or BYOC only under an institutional agreement/DPA that fixes model-provider routing, no-training terms, content retention/deletion and hosting location. The public privacy policy (January 2024) lists OpenAI but not Anthropic, and it places hosting in the US while the AWS BYOC doc puts the control plane in eu-west-1. BYOC alone is insufficient: the control plane stays Zerve-hosted and model routing is not documented for it. Self-Managed with a controlled gateway is the stronger route.
suitability_notes.special: Only Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed can qualify. The whole platform must run on institution-controlled Kubernetes (on-premises or institutional cloud; the Self-Managed docs include an air-gapped pattern). All agent traffic must go through an institution-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers; verify by egress testing that AI blocks also use the gateway. Zerve's gateway docs describe a gateway that holds provider credentials and makes the outbound calls itself, and they name no self-hosted model, so the in-boundary upstream is the institution's responsibility. SaaS, BYOC and direct provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, OpenRouter) do not qualify.

pricing: The pricing FAQ gives Pro at $25 and Team at $50 per user/month. The plan cards show $18.75 and $37.50 per user/month, labelled 'Save 25%'; the static page does not state which billing period is shown by default. Agent tasks are billed at model API cost plus 20%. BYOK and self-hosting reduce orchestration credits but do not remove them. The page contradicts itself on free credits (150 on the plan card, 300 in the first 30 days, 50 per month) and on BYOK gating (Pro on the card and in the FAQ, Team in the plan list). Enterprise is custom-priced, covers multi-cloud and on-premises air-gapped hosting, and can be bought via AWS Marketplace.
academic: No academic discount on the pricing page. A University Partnerships page offers teaching-focused curriculum integration with sandbox access, hackathons and guest lectures on request. The Terms of Service allow free Education Accounts for academic/non-profit noncommercial use at Zerve's discretion; eligibility and limits are not published.
use_cases: AI-assisted notebook analysis (Python, R, SQL) with persistent institutional knowledge for research data teams
self-managed or BYOC data-science workspace inside the institution's own infrastructure
conversational analysis reports and APIs/apps deployed from notebooks
notes: Agentic data-science notebook platform (Python, R, SQL) with SaaS, BYOC and Enterprise Self-Managed options. The separate Self-Managed documentation (LLM Providers page updated 14 Sep 2026) covers an air-gapped install pattern and a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, which makes a configured special-category route possible when the gateway is backed by institution-hosted models. No self-hosted model is named or validated. The home page shows an ISMS badge image (file ISMS_Badge.webp, alt text 'Zerve Logo') and the platform page says 'SOC 2 compliant', but Zerve publishes no certificate scope, audit report or trust centre, so compliance stays empty. Pricing-page contradictions are recorded explicitly.
tier_gate: Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed with an institution-operated LLM gateway to institution-hosted models for special-category data; institutional contract/DPA with verified model routing, training and retention terms for personal data on SaaS/BYOC

required_controls: Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed install on institution-controlled Kubernetes (on-premises or institutional cloud); Zerve SaaS and BYOC do not qualify

All agent traffic routed through an institution-operated OpenAI-compatible gateway (LLMGW_API_BASE) whose upstreams are institution-hosted models; the gateway serves only models on institution-controlled hardware and forwards nothing to external providers; no install-level or organization-level provider keys; verify by egress testing that AI blocks on the compute backend also use the gateway
Egress blocked except to the gateway, with build images, base images and package indexes mirrored internally (documented air-gapped pattern)
Agent internet search and external integrations disabled or blocked
Institutional OIDC identity provider with an access claim rule; institution-operated Postgres, Redis, Vault and object storage
Contract confirming that no telemetry, usage metering or licence check sends data outside the boundary; DPO or data-steward approval before use
residual_risks: Zerve's gateway documentation assumes the gateway holds provider credentials and calls cloud providers; in-boundary inference exists only if the institution backs it with self-hosted models, which Zerve does not document.

Public docs name no self-hosted model. The gateway must serve OpenAI-format streaming and tool calls and map provider/model names to local models, and agent quality with open-weight models is unverified.
The docs say the gateway carries all agent traffic; gateway coverage of AI blocks is implied by the egress section but not stated.

The Enterprise page claims air-gapped installs run with zero external traffic, yet the pricing FAQ says credits are charged for orchestration even when self-hosted; how Self-Managed installs meter credits, check licences or send telemetry to Zerve is not publicly documented.
The Helm chart and images come from Zerve's private registry under an enterprise contract, so the install cannot be inspected before purchase.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: LM Studio Bionic
deployment: Desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux x64/ARM64) that runs inference on-device with local models; optional vendor Secure Cloud models (US-hosted) and web search; LM Link (preview) for inference on the user's own remote devices. Enterprise page advertises deployment on own infrastructure or edge devices via sales; no public deployment documentation.
model_backend: Local open-weight models via the LM Studio runtime (llama.cpp, MLX; experimental Splash Metal backend for specific Qwen models on M3-or-newer Macs since Bionic 1.1.5); since Bionic 1.1.8, when LM Studio 0.4.26+ is running, Bionic uses LM Studio for local inference; remote local models via LM Link; optional US-hosted open models in LM Studio Secure Cloud (model names change and differ between vendor pages). Local voice transcription uses Voxtral. Vision subagents can be set to a local or cloud model.
data_handling_note: Local route: local models run inference on-device and, with local or LM Link models, no LM Studio account is needed. The LM Studio Desktop App Privacy Policy (effective June 2026) states that local use transmits no messages, chat histories or documents, that the application has no telemetry or user-specific tracking, and that network contact is limited to update checks (app/OS version, IP) and model search/download (anonymized queries). Voice input is transcribed locally. LM Link, if used, uploads the device list to LM Studio servers for discovery. Cloud route (Secure Cloud models, web search): the pricing page states that cloud inference is US-hosted and the policy states transfer to the United States; per the policy, requests are processed transiently, not retained and not used for training, all processing parties, including third-party search providers, operate under 'Zero Data Retention or substantially equivalent terms', and Element Labs acts as processor. The policy does not name Bionic, which the docs describe as a separate app from LM Studio.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local models with Secure Cloud, web search and other network tools disabled, and governed project folders. Secure Cloud (US-hosted inference) and web search are vendor-side processing under ZDR claims, with transfer to the United States stated in the privacy policy, and need institutional review (GDPR transfer, processor terms) before use with personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only local models on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware, with Secure Cloud, web search, LM Link, MCP servers, URL skill installs, browser access and shell Auto Review unused; if LM Studio 0.4.26+ runs alongside Bionic (it then serves Bionic's local inference), the same restrictions apply there. Secure Cloud is vendor cloud and remains unsuitable for special-category data despite ZDR.

pricing: Pricing page (checked 2026-10-10): Free USD 0 (Bionic agent, local models, offline voice transcription, LM Link up to 5 devices, limited web search); Bionic+ USD 20/month (US-hosted cloud open models, discounted bulk tokens, web search and page extraction); Pro USD 100/month (5x Bionic+ usage limits, early access). Credits cover cloud usage beyond the plan allowance. Teams: centralized credit billing via organizations; team subscription plans listed as coming soon. Enterprise via sales.
academic: No academic or education discount listed on the pricing page (checked 2026-10-10).
use_cases: offline-capable coding agent over local repositories with inline diff review
local document/PDF/spreadsheet/slide processing with open-weight models
local multilingual voice dictation of prompts and notes
occasional burst to larger open models via ZDR cloud for non-sensitive tasks
notes: Desktop agent for coding and document work, separate from the LM Studio app, with local open-weight models and local voice dictation; optional Secure Cloud models (US-hosted) and web search under vendor ZDR terms; LM Link (preview) for remote inference on own devices. Since Bionic 1.1.8, a running LM Studio 0.4.26+ serves Bionic's local inference. Agent tools include shell, Git, file editing, an in-app browser, skills and MCP servers. Controlled-data suitability applies only to local inference with cloud models, web search, LM Link and other network tools disabled. Proprietary closed-source app; frequent releases (Bionic 1.1.x, latest listed 1.1.8 in October 2026).
tier_gate: any plan (local models need no account); local models only for regulated data, with Secure Cloud models (Bionic+/Pro allowance or personal/organization credits), web search (limited web search is included even on Free), LM Link, MCP and other network tools unused

required_controls: Use only downloaded local models on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware; no Cloud model as session, root/default or vision/sub-agent model.
Do not sign in for or use Secure Cloud; keep Settings > General > Web Search off.
Do not use LM Link remote models (they take inference off the local device and depend on vendor device discovery).
If LM Studio 0.4.26+ runs alongside Bionic (Bionic then uses it for local inference), apply the same controls there: local models only, LM Link off, local API server not exposed to the network.
Disable MCP servers (including organization-managed MCPs), skills installed from URLs, in-app browser/website access and computer control.

Set shell commands to disabled or manual review; do not use Auto Review (its Shell Reviewer subagent model is undocumented and safe read-only commands, including GitHub queries, are auto-approved) or allow-all; review diffs and commands.
Block outbound network at OS/firewall level outside approved update and model-download windows, because no egress test of Bionic exists.
Store projects on encrypted, access-controlled institutional storage with defined retention for session history and project files.
residual_risks: The no-telemetry statement comes from the LM Studio Desktop App Privacy Policy, which does not name Bionic; no network-egress test of Bionic was performed.
Update checks and model search/download still contact vendor and CDN services (app/OS version, IP address).
The agent can run shell commands, browse and call MCP tools; misconfiguration or prompt injection can move data off-device.
Bionic serves local API endpoints (/v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages); their network binding is not documented.
Proprietary closed-source app; local behaviour cannot be independently audited.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Juggler
deployment: Local desktop app plus headless server (macOS, Windows, Linux; source build or official binaries). The server can run on a workstation, dev box or lab server (repo includes Docker packaging) with desktop or browser clients. Accepts loopback connections only by default; LAN access is opt-in and unauthenticated; official binaries add WAN remote-access modes that source builds lack.
model_backend: BYO: Anthropic API and Claude Code CLI, OpenAI API and Codex (ChatGPT plan), GitHub Copilot, Gemini, Mistral, Moonshot Kimi, Z.AI, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and external ACP agents (e.g. Gemini CLI); local: Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI
data_handling_note: Per the README, no Juggler service sits in the model path: prompts, code and keys go straight to the chosen provider, and Juggler keeps copies only on local disk. Project state (conversations, session, bash output) is written to <project>/.juggler/, API keys to ~/.juggler/credentials.json (0600), and logs to the platform log directory (10 MB x 5 rotation, 14-day sweep, configurable). Default-on outbound traffic besides the model provider: with Updates on Automatic (the default) the server polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h, sending version, OS and architecture plus a first-of-day/month mark used to count installs, source builds included (Updates can be set to Off, but a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio; official macOS desktop builds also auto-download found updates); the web UI loads a diff script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com on each page load; and the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies unless disabled. No privacy policy or telemetry statement was found. Hosted backends, background 'cheap model' jobs, ACP agents, MCP servers, extensions and the official binaries' WAN modes each add separate boundaries.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local models or a provider approved under institutional terms, keep loopback-only access, set Updates to Off where install pings to juggler.studio are not acceptable, and disable the built-in Web Search and Web Fetch tools when prompts may carry personal data (they run without approval). Conversations, bash output and logs persist on disk; there is no privacy policy or DPA.
suitability_notes.special: Only on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware with local inference (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI), background 'cheap model' jobs on the same local model or switched off, no hosted-provider keys stored, Updates set to Off or juggler.studio egress blocked, the built-in Web Search and Web Fetch tools disabled, cdnjs.cloudflare.com egress blocked or explicitly accepted, loopback-only access, the Default or Read-only strategy (also for `juggler run`, which defaults to YOLO), and no ACP agents, WAN mode, Exa extension or remote MCP server. Young single-maintainer project without a privacy policy; prefer a reviewed source build for air-gapped or clinical environments.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free download, open source (AGPL-3.0-or-later application; Apache-2.0 SDK, bundled extensions and examples). No Juggler account and no resold tokens: model costs go to the chosen provider. LICENSING.md says official binaries may bundle proprietary paid ('pro tier') components; no paid plan or price was published as of 2026-10-10. Commercial licensing for uses the AGPL does not permit is on contact.
academic: No academic or student program found; free open source.
use_cases: inspectable agentic coding: in the Default strategy, writes and shell commands from Juggler's own tools wait for approval (ACP-agent backends run their own tools outside this), and every recorded model transaction (prompt, tools, output, tokens) can be opened
coding agents on sensitive codebases with local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI)
self-hosted headless server on lab hardware with desktop or browser clients
teaching how agent tool-calling works (branching threads, editable context trees, MCP tool inspection)
notes: GUI-first local agent workbench (Go server, desktop app, browser clients) with persistent on-disk sessions; very active single-maintainer project (eight releases, 14 Sep to 9 Oct 2026). Loopback-only by default; LAN mode is unauthenticated; extensions run unsandboxed with the app's privileges. Default-on egress besides the model provider: the update check contacts juggler.studio and counts installs, the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval, and the web UI loads a script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com; for offline or regulated use set Updates to Off and disable the web tools. Official binaries are built from a private repository and add proprietary WAN modes.
tier_gate: local inference (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) + default loopback-only access + Updates set to Off + built-in Web Search/Web Fetch disabled for regulated data

required_controls: Run a reviewed source build on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware (an official binary only with Updates Off, accepting its unauditable private components), with inference only through local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) under the same control.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Point the background 'cheap model' (tab naming, reply suggestions, auto-approve reviewer, extension text generation) at the same local model, or switch it off.
Store no hosted-provider credentials (Settings or ~/.juggler/credentials.json) and keep cloud API keys out of the environment, so no model role can reach a hosted provider.

Keep the default loopback-only access; never enable the passwordless LAN mode (p or --public) on shared networks (over HTTPS, LAN mode also uses Google's public STUN server for WebRTC); in Docker, where --public is used, publish the port only to localhost or an isolated network; do not use the official binaries' WAN modes.

Set Settings > Updates to Off (default Automatic polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h with version, OS, architecture and an install-count mark; official macOS desktop builds also auto-download updates) or block that egress, and confirm with egress monitoring after each upgrade. With Updates Off, a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio (without the install mark), so do not use it where that egress is not accepted.

Disable the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch capabilities in Settings > Extensions for every project (stored as plugins.disabled in <project>/.juggler/config.json), or deny the WebSearch and WebFetch tools globally with a beforeTool hook in ~/.juggler/hooks; both run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies.
Block or explicitly accept outbound requests to cdnjs.cloudflare.com: the web UI loads diff_match_patch from it on each page load (allowed by the CSP, no integrity attribute).

Use the Default or Read-only strategy so writes and shell commands need manual approval; do not use YOLO, the Auto-approve reviewer, or `juggler run` without an explicit --strategy (it defaults to yolo); do not use ACP agents (they bypass Juggler's strategies and their permission requests are auto-allowed by default); keep the Exa extension (ships disabled) and remote MCP servers off; install only reviewed extensions.

Before each sensitive session, check the effective settings of the project in use (providers, cheap model, strategy, disabled tools); the web-tool disable list is stored per project, so a new project starts with the web tools enabled unless the global beforeTool hook denies them.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level, allowing only the local model runtime and any host explicitly accepted under these controls, and verify that the block holds; shell commands and extensions run with the user's privileges, so in-app settings alone do not stop egress.

Apply institutional access, retention and backup controls to <project>/.juggler/, ~/.juggler/credentials.json and the platform log directory, and keep .juggler/ out of shared repositories and sync folders.
residual_risks: No privacy policy, telemetry statement or DPA; the update ping and install counting are described only in source-code comments, and how juggler.studio handles request logs is undocumented.
Young project (repository created June 2026) with one principal maintainer, rapid releases and no LTS; network behaviour can change between versions.
The server binds all interfaces and relies on an application-level LAN gate (403 for non-loopback requests); a host firewall is still advisable.
Shell commands run with the user's full privileges; SECURITY.md states the shell filter is not a security control, and agent tools can read files in the home directory, including stored API keys.
Extensions are unsandboxed JavaScript; their declared permissions are disclosure, not containment.
Built-in web tools are enabled by default and disabled per project; a new project or a new version can re-expose them unless a global hook or network egress control is in place.
The UI runs a third-party script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com without an integrity check, in a page that can approve tool calls (supply-chain exposure).
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Official binaries are built from a private repository and may include proprietary components that cannot be audited from the public source.

name: OpenSquilla
vendor: Beijing TokenRhythm Technologies Co., Ltd. (OpenSquilla open-source project)
deployment: local/self-hosted: desktop app (macOS/Windows) or CLI/TUI with a gateway server bound to 127.0.0.1 by default; Docker/Compose publishes the port on 127.0.0.1 with token auth; LAN/public binding is opt-in. Vendor describes fully offline on-prem use; default-on network reporting and update checks must be disabled for that.
model_backend: BYOK cloud providers (20+, e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Qwen), the optional TokenRhythm Studio API (aggregates third-party hosted models), or local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio/OVMS and custom OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints. The SquillaRouter classifier and default embeddings run on-device.
data_handling_note: Configuration, sessions, logs, memory, scheduler state and caches stay on the user's machine. Prompts, tool results and selected files go to the configured provider. Per the policy, web search, channels, browser automation and other integrations contact external services when enabled. Since v0.5.5 (2026-09-23), one default-on Network reporting switch with no consent prompt covers V1 install and daily turn/token counts plus V2 reliability diagnostics and product/growth analytics. V2 events carry a hashed OS-machine-ID device token; V1 events carry a hashed MAC/IP-derived install ID. The policy excludes prompts, file contents and paths from these uploads; servers can see the source IP. OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true stops all statistics uploads and update checks but does not erase queued events. The retention period and controller of the telemetry server are not documented. The install-ID provider header is retired, but the code still attaches session, turn and execution correlation IDs to TokenRhythm Studio requests unless that variable is set. TokenRhythm Studio's privacy policy (version dated 2026-09-03) allows de-identified training on calls to its own models and processes those calls in China. It forwards other calls to third-party model vendors, and the account keeps call logs and conversation records.

suitability_notes.personal: Use self-hosted local models and set OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true before first start (reporting is on by default); govern local state and verify egress. Hosted providers have their own terms; TokenRhythm Studio's policy allows de-identified training on calls to its own models, so review its terms before sending personal data there.
suitability_notes.special: Only with customer-controlled local models (Ollama only in local-only mode), network reporting disabled before first start, hosted routes, Browser Use and community skill hubs avoided, and egress verified. Telemetry service retention and controller remain undocumented.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); no paid tiers for the software found. The optional TokenRhythm Studio API is pay-as-you-go with per-model prices published in CNY per 1M tokens, plus a pilot program offering free token credits.
academic: No academic or student program found.
use_cases: self-hosted agent runtime on lab or institutional hardware (gateway bound to localhost by default)
local-model agentic coding and data tasks with sandboxed shell and file tools
token-budget-constrained agent workflows (routing/ensembles reducing token spend)
on-premises offline use with on-device routing and embeddings (network reporting disabled)
notes: Young self-hostable desktop/CLI/gateway agent; the repository moved to the TokenRhythm GitHub organization (old URLs redirect). v0.5.5 expanded default-on reporting to device-keyed reliability and growth analytics; its release notes list only the opt-out variables and link PRIVACY.md. One switch disables all reporting and update checks. Telemetry retention and controller terms are not published. Controlled use requires disabling reporting before first start and enforcing network boundaries.
tier_gate: fully self-hosted + local models + network reporting disabled before first start for regulated data

required_controls: Institution-controlled infrastructure only: fully self-hosted with local model backends (Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio/OVMS or an institution-run compatible endpoint that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers); TokenRhythm Studio and hosted providers avoided.

Set OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true (or [privacy] disable_network_observability = true) before first start; the legacy OPENSQUILLA_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED alone does not stop V2 statistics.

Keep the gateway on 127.0.0.1 or behind token auth and an institutional firewall; paste the gateway token instead of passing it as a URL query, which writes it to the gateway access log; do not enable Browser Use, web search, channels or community skill hubs for regulated data.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
residual_risks: Network reporting is on by default and keyed to a hashed OS machine ID; a first start before the opt-out is set can upload install and usage statistics. Telemetry server retention and controller are not documented.
Local sessions, logs, memory, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls; disabling reporting does not erase locally queued events.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

name: Pi
vendor: Earendil Works / Mario Zechner and contributors
deployment: local CLI with local/self-hosted or cloud inference
model_backend: Cloud APIs/subscriptions (including Earendil's optional Radius gateway, early alpha) or local inference through the built-in llama.cpp router integration, or Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang and other compatible endpoints configured in models.json.
data_handling_note: Local JSONL sessions persist under ~/.pi/agent/sessions by default; --no-session disables persistence. Install/update telemetry (a ping to pi.dev carrying version, OS, runtime and architecture in the User-Agent, plus provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and Cloudflare) is on by default; analytics defaults off. Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0; the telemetry setting does not control the pi.dev version check. --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1 stops automatic network activity (version check, pi.dev model-catalog refresh, package update checks, telemetry, /bug upload), not model, tool or MCP traffic. /share uploads a session to an organization-visible Radius artifact when Radius sign-in is configured, otherwise to a secret GitHub gist that anyone with the link can view; /bug can upload a report to radius.pi.dev. Built-in MCP client, extensions and tools can add external traffic. Provider terms govern cloud inference.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a governed local endpoint with telemetry off and /share, /bug upload and Radius unused, or a separately approved direct cloud-provider agreement (not Radius, whose alpha terms advise against personal data); protect session files.
suitability_notes.special: Only local/customer-operated inference with offline mode, telemetry, sharing, Radius, and unreviewed MCP servers and extensions disabled qualifies.

compliance: MIT source is not a product compliance certification.
Optional Radius alpha terms (1 September 2026) state they are not a data processing agreement and advise against submitting personal, sensitive or regulated data.
pricing: MIT software is free; no Pi software subscription is required. Cloud provider usage/subscriptions and local hardware costs are separate. The optional Radius gateway bills usage against prepaid organization credits at per-model rates listed in Radius's pricing docs, plus a payment-processing fee.
academic: Available without academic eligibility; model-provider offers are separate.
use_cases: coding
repository editing
terminal automation
research software development
notes: Actively maintained extensible terminal coding agent (interactive, print/JSON, RPC and TypeScript SDK); package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent reached 1.0.0 on 1 October 2026 and 1.1.0 on 7 October 2026. Canonical repository earendil-works/pi (redirects from badlogic/pi-mono). Built-in MCP, llama.cpp, codemode and tool-search extensions load by default; --no-mcp disables MCP for one run, --no-extensions disables all built-ins, and a -builtin:<name> entry in the extensions setting disables one persistently. Radius is an optional Earendil-hosted gateway and artifact service in early alpha. Session sharing, bug-report upload, MCP servers and extension installation require separate review.
tier_gate: Local endpoint; --offline with install telemetry/analytics off; no /share, /bug upload, Radius or unreviewed MCP; no cloud inference

required_controls: Configure an institution-controlled local endpoint (llama.cpp router via /login llama.cpp, or models.json). Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0, keep enableAnalytics false, and run with --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1.
Prohibit /share, /bug uploads and Radius sign-in; disable built-in MCP (--no-mcp, or "-builtin:mcp" in the extensions setting) or allowlist MCP servers, and review extensions and packages.
Restrict shell tools and network egress (container or VM per Pi's isolation guide); govern local JSONL history or use --no-session.
residual_risks: Only local/customer-operated inference with telemetry, sharing, Radius and external integrations disabled qualifies.
Pi runs tool calls without per-call approval and has no built-in sandbox; context files load regardless of project trust.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Zencoder
vendor: For Good AI Inc. (dba Zencoder Inc.)
deployment: Local IDE plugins (VS Code, JetBrains, Android Studio) and Zenflow desktop app using Zencoder-managed cloud models and services / Enterprise private deployment with customer-operated model endpoints; Zenflow can also run on a customer-operated Ubuntu VM over SSH (remote hosts, Zenflow 2.5.1+, still marked experimental)
model_backend: Managed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI plus Zencoder Auto (routes across Zencoder-self-hosted and vendor models) and Auto+; third-party agent runtimes (Claude Code and Codex in IDE agents and Zenflow; Gemini CLI in Zenflow); BYOK; or custom settings.json endpoints (OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini APIs), including documented local Ollama/vLLM.
data_handling_note: Managed cloud: ToS (updated 15 Jun 2026) §4.1 permits training on Free-account content (including lapsed trials); Trial/Paid training needs 'further consent', while benchmarking and service improvement remain permitted. Zencoder docs and Enterprise pages say code is never used for training; the ToS is the binding text. Managed model providers may retain requests for limited periods; BYOK follows the user's provider terms. Docs list chat messages as retained per org settings and Enterprise retention as configurable, so there is no universal zero storage despite a docs 'zero-storage' claim. ToS §5.3(a) bars personal data in Your Content without exception; the AUP bars personal and regulated sensitive data unless the applicable Governing Terms (e.g. an Enterprise Agreement) or authorized product settings expressly permit it. ToS §4.3 (IDE/hosted services) and Zenflow terms §4.2 (with or without an account) allow usage telemetry, stated to exclude content. The private route (custom local/VPC models, useDefaultProviders:false) serves chat and agent runs from customer endpoints; sign-in, telemetry and integrations remain separate egress paths.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Free-account content (including lapsed trials) may be used for model training; Trial and paid accounts require further consent for training, while benchmarking and service improvement remain permitted.
suitability_notes.personal: Standard self-serve terms (Free, Pro, Pro Plus, Pro Max) bar personal data in submitted content (ToS §5.3(a); AUP). Use only under a written Enterprise agreement that expressly permits personal data, with a DPA, no training consent and acceptable product/provider retention, preferably on the private local-model route.
suitability_notes.special: Only private operation with local models (useDefaultProviders:false), all external traffic controlled, and a written agreement that expressly permits special-category data qualifies; standard terms prohibit personal data.

compliance: Vendor states SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 plus GDPR compliance; the Trust Center (trust.forgood.ai) offers certificates and SOC 2 Type II/SOC 3 reports on request. Audit scope not confirmed.

Trust Center subprocessors: Anthropic and OpenAI (AI/ML), Google Cloud (infrastructure, EU/US), Amplitude (analytics), Atlassian, FrontEgg, HubSpot, Slack. xAI is not listed although Grok models are in the managed catalog, and Google is listed for cloud infrastructure only although Gemini models are offered.
pricing: Free $0 (no bundled credits; BYOK); Pro $45/user/month ($40 billed annually; 30,000 credits), Pro Plus $95 ($85; 80,000), Pro Max $195 ($175; 180,000); Enterprise custom (prepaid usage, private deployment). 7-day trial with 5,000 credits; model credit multipliers; top-ups from $20.
academic: No current academic entitlement is asserted.
use_cases: coding
repository editing
terminal automation
research software development
notes: AI agent platform with IDE agents (VS Code, JetBrains, Android Studio) and the Zenflow desktop app; Zenflow Work is a business-task surface outside this catalog's scope. The documented private route uses customer-operated model endpoints and is listed as an Enterprise feature; the default managed service has different training, retention and contract terms. Docs state that further private-deployment controls are still being built.
tier_gate: Enterprise agreement with private deployment that expressly permits personal/special data; customer-operated local models with useDefaultProviders:false; sign-in, telemetry and integration egress controlled
