required_controls: Enterprise agreement covering private deployment that expressly permits personal and special-category data (standard ToS §5.3(a) and the AUP prohibit personal data in submitted content), with a DPA and no training consent.

Declare only customer-operated local model endpoints in settings.json and set useDefaultProviders:false; disable third-party CLIs, cloud BYOK keys, cloud integrations/MCP connectors and cloud multi-repo indexing.
Control and verify egress: Zencoder sign-in, usage telemetry/analytics, auto-updates and any remaining calls to Zencoder services.
residual_risks: Docs document only the model-routing steps and state that additional private-deployment controls are still being built.
IDE plugins require Zencoder sign-in and Zenflow collects usage telemetry with or without an account; exclusion of content from telemetry rests on vendor statements.

Agent logs (structured logs panel) and the MCP audit trail (added August 2026) record model responses and tool inputs/outputs; their storage location is not documented and traces can be passed to vendor support by Operation ID. Sessions, logs, tools and integrations need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Poolside Agent CLI
deployment: local CLI; inference via Poolside-hosted Platform (the recommended login option), OpenRouter, or a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible endpoint (local Ollama/vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference in a VPC, on premises or air-gapped)
model_backend: Poolside Laguna models with public weights on Hugging Face (Laguna XS.2 and M.1 Apache-2.0; Laguna XS 2.1 and S 2.1 OpenMDW-1.1), served by Poolside Platform, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible server; Laguna XS.2 is documented for laptops with 32 GB RAM or an 8 GB NVIDIA GPU.
data_handling_note: The Poolside Terms (updated 21 Jul 2026) cover Poolside Platform, Chat, Console and the Agent CLI; installing pool binds the user to them. Content (prompts, code, output) may be used to train Poolside models unless the user selects the Training Opt-Out; even after opt-out, content tied to Feedback or flagged for safety review may still be used, and via OpenRouter the third-party platform's settings may govern. Poolside also collects content-free Product Metrics; what the CLI sends in local mode is not documented and no telemetry switch is documented. The CLI checks for a newer version at startup, /share returns a web trajectory-viewer link for the session, and /feedback can attach logs that may contain prompt and response text. The privacy policy (updated 21 Jul 2026) gives need-based retention with no fixed period; a DPA (updated 27 Apr 2026) is incorporated by reference for personal data. With locally pulled Laguna weights on Ollama/vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference, Poolside docs state code and model traffic stay on the local machine or inside the customer environment; Ollama ':cloud' model tags run in Ollama's cloud even through the localhost endpoint. Built-in web_fetch is on by default, and remote HTTP/SSE MCP servers are not subject to sandbox network rules.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer a local or institution-operated endpoint. If Poolside-hosted inference is used, set the training opt-out (the DPA is incorporated in the Terms); feedback and safety-flagged content remain usable for training and hosted retention periods are not stated.
suitability_notes.special: Only with locally pulled open-weight Laguna on Ollama (cloud features disabled, no ':cloud' tags) or vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference on institution hardware, on premises or air-gapped; web tools, remote MCP servers, /share and /feedback log attachments off; sandbox network policy allow-list (the 'off' value sets no policy) plus host-level egress blocking to Poolside, verified. The standard Terms bar using any Product, including the locally run CLI, for protected health, biometric and other heightened-regulation data unless Poolside permits it in writing, so written permission or an enterprise agreement is a precondition.

compliance: Published DPA with SCCs and UK Addendum (updated 27 Apr 2026); the Trust Center returned HTTP 403, so no certification is asserted.
Standard Terms prohibit processing highly sensitive or regulated data (including PHI and biometric data) with any Product unless Poolside permits it in writing.
pricing: Poolside Platform API keys are offered free for developer access, and the models page says hosted Laguna use is free for a limited time (limits and end date not stated); paid access with a larger context window goes through OpenRouter at OpenRouter's prices; self-managed and on-premises deployments require contacting Poolside (no public price; poolside.ai links no pricing page). Model weights are downloadable under their own licences.
academic: No academic or student program found on fetched pages.
use_cases: local agentic coding with an open-weight Laguna model served by Ollama on a laptop or workstation
institution-operated coding agent against self-managed Poolside inference on premises or air-gapped
non-interactive pool exec runs in scripts and CI against a controlled endpoint
ACP integration of the same local agent in JetBrains or Zed
notes: Terminal coding agent from a foundation-model lab that publishes Laguna weights and documents both a local Ollama route and self-managed (including air-gapped) inference bundles. The CLI is proprietary under the Poolside Terms; model licences are separate. The changelog starts at v1.0.0 (28 Apr 2026); GitHub releases run from v1.0.3 (27 May 2026) to v1.0.16 (14 Aug 2026), which is still the latest version on the download server on 10 Oct 2026, with no maintainer issue replies since late August. Research-community adoption is not yet established.
tier_gate: training opt-out, or a local/institution-operated endpoint, for personal data; for special-category data, Poolside's written permission plus locally pulled or self-managed inference with Ollama cloud, web tools, remote MCP and sharing disabled and vendor egress blocked

required_controls: Obtain Poolside's written permission or an enterprise agreement first: Terms section 2.2 prohibits using any Product, including the CLI, for PHI, biometric and other heightened-regulation data.

Connect pool only to locally pulled Laguna weights on Ollama or vLLM, or to self-managed Poolside inference on institution hardware; do not use Poolside Platform or OpenRouter keys, and disable Ollama cloud features (no ':cloud' model tags).
Disable web_search and web_fetch, keep remote HTTP/SSE MCP servers off, and run the local sandbox with network policy allow-list limited to the local endpoint; 'off' configures no network policy.
Do not use /share or /feedback with log attachments; review logs.zip before any sharing.
Block and verify outbound traffic from the CLI host to Poolside services (startup version check, Product Metrics); no telemetry switch is documented.
residual_risks: CLI Product Metrics, update-check and trajectory-sharing behaviour in local mode are undocumented; only network-level verification can confirm no egress.
Without a sandbox, shell tools run on the host with the host's network access; approvals are documented as a convenience, not a security boundary.
Local logs, trajectories and session history stay on disk and can contain prompt and response text; they need institutional access and retention controls.
Proprietary CLI Terms and the separate open-weight model licences (Apache-2.0, OpenMDW-1.1) both apply and can change independently; the CLI release cadence has paused since v1.0.16 (14 Aug 2026).

name: Snowflake CoCo
deployment: Snowflake cloud service. CoCo in Snowsight runs each session in a Snowflake-managed Cloud Agents container (commercial regions only). The CoCo CLI and Desktop run locally, act on local files and shell, and the CLI can also run tools in a Snowflake-managed container. All model inference is remote: per Snowflake, open-weight models run on Snowflake GPUs and frontier models on cloud-provider endpoints, reached through cross-region inference.
model_backend: Cortex models granted to the active role, chosen per session or as an account default (Auto, Auto Intelligent, Auto Efficient or a pinned model). By default all users inherit access to all models. The Service Consumption Table lists Claude, OpenAI GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi models for CoCo, many marked Preview. Snowflake states that frontier models run on cloud-provider infrastructure: Claude on AWS Bedrock, GPT on Azure OpenAI, Gemini on GCP. Some models carry Snowflake's Model and Service Pass-Through Terms.
data_handling_note: Snowflake states that AI inputs and outputs, including Usage Data, are not used to train models made available to other customers. CoCo inputs are classified as Usage Data and outputs as Customer Data. On all three surfaces, CoCo writes every prompt and response trace to SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS in the customer account; rows cannot be modified, only an AI_OBSERVABILITY_ADMIN role can delete them, and no automatic expiry is stated. CLI and Desktop also keep full conversations (file content, tool output, SQL) under ~/.snowflake/cortex/conversations/. The CLI --private flag disables conversation persistence and server-side logging. Ratings and feedback comments go to Snowflake. CoCo requires cross-region inference: prompts and outputs go transiently to the processing region and are not persisted there. Routing is an account parameter (any region, one cloud, or a region group such as AWS_EU or AZURE_EU). The documented default differs between pages and by account age, so check the effective value. Retention at the cloud-provider model endpoints and for Snowsight chat history is not stated. By default, Cloud Agents sandboxes have read-only HTTPS egress to package registries; admins can disable non-Snowflake egress.

suitability_notes.personal: Only under an institutional Snowflake agreement whose DPA and AI terms are confirmed to cover CoCo inputs, which are contractually Usage Data rather than Customer Data. Also required: cross-region routing pinned to an acceptable geography; an actively restricted model list (all models are granted by default); least-privilege roles or Restricted Session Scope; a retention schedule for AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS; and Cloud Agents non-Snowflake egress and web search disabled. Confirm Snowsight chat retention and the pass-through model terms.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. Inference always runs on Snowflake-managed or cloud-provider model infrastructure, which the institution does not control. Not appropriate for identifiable health, genetic or clinical data under this catalog's rule, whatever the contract.

compliance: Scope depends on the Snowflake contract, edition, region and AI terms; no CoCo-specific certification is asserted here.
pricing: Billed by token consumption in AI Credits per million tokens, at per-model rates in the Service Consumption Table (Table 6(e), effective 9 Oct 2026). Table 2(b) lists On Demand AI Credit prices of $2.00 (Global) and $2.20 (Regional), with capacity pricing by contract value. Individual CLI/Desktop subscriptions start with a 30-day trial and include a fixed monthly usage allowance. Cloud Agents currently carries no additional charge. Warehouse compute and storage are billed separately.
academic: No academic or student program for CoCo found on fetched pages.
use_cases: agentic SQL and Python notebook authoring over Snowflake tables
dbt projects and Streamlit apps from the local CLI or Desktop under Snowflake RBAC
machine learning and data engineering workflows with built-in Snowflake skills
sandboxed shell and Python execution in Snowsight Cloud Agents
notes: Snowflake's data-platform coding agent (also documented as Cortex Code) across Snowsight, Desktop and CLI. Snowsight sessions run in the Cloud Agents sandbox. The Cortex Agents Coding Agent API (GA 26 Aug 2026) gives developers the same runtime. Relevant mainly where an institution already holds research data in Snowflake.
tier_gate: institutional Snowflake agreement covering CoCo inputs, with pinned cross-region routing, an admin model allow-list, event-table retention and egress controls; not for special-category data

residual_risks: Cloud-only: inference always runs on Snowflake GPUs or on cloud-provider model endpoints (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP), none of which the institution controls. Contractual no-training and no-persistence statements do not make it suitable for special-category data under this catalog's rule.

name: Notebook Intelligence
vendor: Plmbr GitHub organization (maintainer Mehmet Bektaş); community open-source project
deployment: local-capable / self-hosted JupyterLab or JupyterHub extension; cloud provider dependent
model_backend: Provider-dependent. Default mode supports four providers: GitHub Copilot; OpenAI- or LiteLLM-compatible endpoints, cloud or self-hosted (e.g. vLLM/TGI); and Ollama, local or on a host set through OLLAMA_HOST at server launch. Claude mode uses the Claude Code CLI for chat and the Anthropic API (or a configured Base URL) for inline chat and auto-complete. An experimental ACP mode, off by default, runs OpenAI Codex as its only agent type. Launcher tiles open the Claude Code, opencode, Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI or Codex CLIs in a terminal when they are installed.
data_handling_note: NBI runs inside the user's Jupyter Server and has no central server of its own. It documents no external telemetry: its in-process usage events go nowhere unless an administrator registers a listener. Prompts, surrounding cell source and attached files go to the configured provider. Saved cell outputs are sent when a notebook or cell is attached or read. Ollama keeps inference on the configured host. Claude mode is available to users by default (user-choice) and sends data to Anthropic through the Claude Code CLI outside NBI's provider list; ACP mode is off by default. Launcher tiles run agent CLIs directly in a terminal. API keys are stored in plaintext in ~/.jupyter/nbi/config.json. A remembered Copilot token is encrypted with a shared default password unless one is set.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama or an institution-operated endpoint, or a cloud provider route covered by an approved DPA or no-training agreement. On shared hubs, pin the provider and set Claude mode by admin policy. Clear sensitive cell outputs before attaching notebooks, and protect the plaintext key file.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset applied in full, plus extra controls. The preset disables the Copilot, OpenAI-compatible and LiteLLM-compatible providers with environment re-enabling blocked, forces Claude and ACP modes off, disables the command-execute and file-edit tools, and serves Ollama on hardware the institution controls. In addition, hide all coding-agent launcher tiles, remove agent CLIs from the image, block egress to external LLM hosts, GitHub and npm, and pin the NBI version. A self-hosted vLLM/TGI route keeps the OpenAI-compatible provider enabled, and its Base URL is not documented as admin-lockable, so network egress control must enforce it. A LiteLLM proxy that forwards to cloud models does not qualify. The developer calls the preset a starting point, not a HIPAA certification, and it is not institutional approval.

compliance: self-hosted
pricing: Free and open source (GPL-3.0); provider charges, where applicable, are paid directly to the chosen provider.
academic: free
use_cases: AI chat, inline edit and autocomplete in JupyterLab notebooks
Agent mode that edits, runs and fixes notebook cells
Chatbook natural-language notebook cells
Claude Code sessions inside JupyterLab; experimental Codex via ACP
Administrator-pinned providers, models and feature policies on managed JupyterHub
Local-model notebook assistance with Ollama for sensitive datasets
notes: JupyterLab extension with its own agent mode, admin policy controls, optional Claude Code mode and experimental ACP (Codex) mode. The repository moved to the plmbr GitHub organization. Agent modes and launcher tiles bypass the provider list unless they are separately disabled, so the sensitive-data preset must be applied as a whole and enforced with network egress controls.
tier_gate: Regulated data only with the documented local-only preset (cloud providers, Claude mode and ACP mode forced off), coding-agent launcher tiles and CLIs removed, egress blocked, and Ollama or an egress-enforced self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure

required_controls: Apply the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset in full. Set disabled_providers to github-copilot, openai-compatible and litellm-compatible with allow_enabling_providers_with_env=False. Disable nbi-command-execute and nbi-file-edit with allow_enabling_tools_with_env=False. Set claude_mode_policy and acp_mode_policy to force-off.

Serve models from Ollama on institution-controlled hardware (OLLAMA_HOST set at server launch). If a vLLM/TGI endpoint is used through the OpenAI-compatible provider instead, enforce its Base URL with network egress control, since that field is not documented as admin-lockable. Do not use LiteLLM proxies that forward to cloud models.

Hide all coding-agent launcher tiles with disabled_coding_agent_launchers (claude-code, opencode, pi, github-copilot-cli, codex) and remove those CLIs from the image or PATH, because the tiles are independent of claude_mode_policy and the CLIs stay usable from a terminal.

Block egress to external LLM hosts, github.com, codeload.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com and registry.npmjs.org at the network layer. Pre-install MCP servers and host skills manifests internally. Pin the NBI version and review the changelog before upgrades. Protect the ~/.jupyter/nbi/ secrets.
residual_risks: Claude mode (user-choice by default) and ACP mode reach their own backends outside NBI's provider list. Agent-CLI launcher tiles and the Jupyter terminal are separate surfaces, so disabling providers alone does not make a deployment local-only.
NBI has no provider allowlist mode, so a new built-in provider added in a minor release would auto-enable unless the version is pinned. User config overrides base config for endpoint fields.

Saved cell outputs are sent when notebooks or cells are attached, and API keys are stored in plaintext. Local sessions, staged uploads, logs and tool actions need institutional access, retention and egress controls. The developer describes the preset as a starting point, not a HIPAA compliance certification.

name: MLJAR Studio
deployment: local desktop app (Windows, macOS incl. Apple Silicon, Linux via Ubuntu .deb) with local Python execution; AI via hosted MLJAR AI by default, or with the perpetual licence via BYOK cloud providers or local/self-managed model servers
model_backend: Hosted MLJAR AI by default (underlying model providers not disclosed); with the perpetual licence: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, or local/self-managed servers (Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM, llama.cpp, custom OpenAI-compatible)
data_handling_note: Notebook code and Python run locally. MLJAR AI, a hosted service, is the default LLM provider; its underlying model providers, prompt retention and processing location are not published. The AI policy points to the Privacy Policy for MLJAR AI details, but that policy covers the mljar.com website and accounts and has no MLJAR AI retention or provider terms. The AI policy also states that by default no data is transmitted externally, which conflicts with the hosted default in the provider docs and with the home-page claim that data stays on the computer. MLJAR states it does not train its own models on customer data unless agreed, and does not control how external providers train. With own keys, prompts go to that provider under its terms. A local model keeps prompts on the machine. DataFrame enrichment sends each unique cell value of the chosen column to the provider Studio selects. First launch needs sign-in or licence activation, and AI Provider Settings run a licence access check. Desktop-app telemetry and offline operation are not documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local or institution-operated model endpoint (perpetual licence required), or an own-key provider covered by an approved DPA/no-training agreement. The default hosted MLJAR AI route has no published retention, subprocessor or DPA terms.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the perpetual licence and a local or institution-operated model server on controlled hardware. Leave MLJAR AI, OpenAI, OpenRouter and Ollama Cloud unused, along with conversation publishing, MLJAR-hosted Mercury deployment and cloud database connections. Verify at the network layer that chat, AutoLab, Workflows and enrichment requests reach only that endpoint, and that sign-in, licence and update traffic carries no data.

pricing: Pricing page on 2026-10-10: Free $0 (50 prompts/month), Pro $20/month (500 prompts), Business $60/month (2,000 prompts); perpetual licence $199 one-time with one year of updates, required for Ollama/local servers and own provider keys. EULA: perpetual licence covers 1 user and 3 devices; newer releases after the update period need a renewal. The MLJAR AI docs describe extra hosted usage as an add-on that requires the perpetual licence, which differs from the pricing page; verify at purchase.
academic: No academic or student programme is stated on the pricing page.
use_cases: Natural-language exploratory analysis of CSV/Excel data with generated, inspectable Python code
AutoML and AI-run AutoLab experiments on tabular research data
AI-assisted notebooks with local Python execution and whole-notebook AI edits
Local-model data analysis via Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM or llama.cpp for private datasets
notes: Desktop AI data analyst built on local Python notebooks, from the vendor of the open-source mljar-supervised AutoML package; Studio itself is proprietary. The local-model route needs the perpetual licence. The default hosted MLJAR AI route has undisclosed model providers and retention, and the vendor's AI policy misstates the default. Desktop telemetry is undocumented.
tier_gate: perpetual licence + local or institution-operated model server for regulated data; hosted MLJAR AI not for personal data without a DPA

required_controls: Buy the perpetual licence and configure a local or institution-operated model server (Ollama in Local mode, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM, llama.cpp or custom OpenAI-compatible); confirm the endpoint executes on controlled hardware.

Switch away from the default MLJAR AI provider; do not use OpenAI, OpenRouter or Ollama Cloud; do not publish conversations, deploy Mercury apps to MLJAR hosting, or connect cloud databases (e.g. Databricks, Snowflake, Supabase).

Verify with institutional network controls that model requests from chat, AutoLab, Workflows and enrichment reach only the configured endpoint, and restrict sign-in, licence-check and extension-update traffic.
residual_risks: MLJAR AI is the default provider and its model providers, retention and processing location are undisclosed; the AI policy's statement that no data leaves the machine by default conflicts with this.
Licence activation and the AI Provider Settings access check contact MLJAR; air-gapped operation and desktop-app telemetry are not documented.
Local notebooks, sessions and app logs (documented app-data and log folders) require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: JASP
vendor: JASP Team (open-source project supported by the University of Amsterdam; institutional support via JASP Services B.V.)
deployment: Local desktop application; the optional AI assistant (off by default) sends requests to a user-configured OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint: a shipped cloud preset or a Custom Provider URL, which can be a local or institution-operated server
model_backend: Bring-your-own key/endpoint. Shipped presets in v0.98.1: OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Xiaomi, xAI (all cloud). Custom Provider accepts any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint; release notes list local models as supported
data_handling_note: JASP runs no AI service of its own; data handling follows the configured endpoint. The AI is off until enabled; the enable dialog states that information from the data set, analyses, output and chat messages may be processed by the AI service and warns against sensitive or restricted data. Tool calls return dataset metadata (file path, column names and types, row counts) and analysis results. All shipped presets are cloud providers, and JASP's own blog recommends free API tiers while noting that free use means paying with your data. JASP's privacy policy (2018, no AI mention) says the software collects no user data but states it does not apply to the software itself. Update checks are opt-in. The full AI request body is written to the JASP log, which persists only if logging to file is enabled.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-approved paid provider under a DPA/no-training agreement, or a local/institution-operated endpoint via Custom Provider. Do not use free API tiers, which may use submitted data.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a Custom Provider pointing to a local or institution-operated OpenAI-compatible model server, no cloud preset key stored, and network egress verified. The local route rests on one release-note line and the Custom Provider endpoint field; there is no dedicated setup guide and the pull request lists only cloud providers as tested.

pricing: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). The AI assistant needs a user-provided API key/model, so provider costs or free-tier data terms apply. Teams and institutions can contact JASP Services B.V. for professional support (no prices published).
academic: free
use_cases: Natural-language creation and execution of statistical analyses in a GUI
Plain-language annotation and interpretation of analysis output
AI-composed reports combining several analyses
Teaching statistics with configurable AI personas
External agent or MCP access to JASP analyses through an optional local JSON-RPC server
notes: Established open-source statistics package; optional agentic AI assistant added in 0.98.0 (2026-07-01; pull request titled 'JASP AI Beta'). Latest release v0.98.1 (2026-07-07); repository commits continue (2026-10-10). Data handling depends entirely on the configured endpoint; all shipped presets are cloud providers.
tier_gate: Custom Provider with local or institution-operated endpoint for regulated data; approved paid provider (no free tier) for personal data

required_controls: Configure a Custom Provider pointing to a local or institution-operated OpenAI-compatible model server; store no keys for cloud presets or free tiers.
Keep the MCP/JSON-RPC server disabled (default), or loopback-only behind a host firewall, because it has no authentication.
Keep logging to file off, or treat JASP log files as regulated data; verify network egress from the workstation.
residual_risks: AI requests carry dataset metadata, analysis output and chat text to the endpoint; a misconfigured or switched provider sends them off-boundary.
When enabled, the JSON-RPC server accepts unauthenticated calls that can load files and read results, and its bind address is configurable.
The AI feature was labelled beta at release and the local-model route has no dedicated documentation or listed testing.
Local sessions, exported reports and logs require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: IBM Bob
deployment: IBM-hosted SaaS on IBM Cloud (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo region) / Enterprise self-hosted backend on customer-managed Red Hat OpenShift, including disconnected (air-gapped) clusters
model_backend: SaaS: IBM selects the model automatically per task; users and organisations cannot choose or restrict models, and the FAQ does not name providers. Self-hosted: exactly one customer-provided core model through the Model Gateway, either a self-hosted open-weight model from IBM's supported list (at review: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, Poolside Laguna S 2.1; Mistral Medium 3.5 only with the IBM Z package) or a frontier model via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI; openai/gpt-oss-20b is the documented guardrail model for air-gapped deployments.
data_handling_note: SaaS (IBM Cloud): the FAQ says prompts, code and responses are held only in temporary memory for the interaction, are never written to persistent storage and are not used to train models; IBM calls this 'effectively zero-retention' and points to the IBM Bob Service Description (not reviewed) for contractual terms. The data-residency page says conversation data stays in the selected region (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo) and expires at session end; account, admin, billing and user-management data are kept in US East regardless of region. Client telemetry (actions, features, errors; IBM says no code or prompts) is on by default and can be switched off; Enterprise Bobalytics needs it on. Bob keeps completed tasks for 14 days by default (configurable in Settings). Self-hosted (Enterprise entitlement): the backend runs on the customer's OpenShift cluster; inference runs wherever the single configured core model is served, on premises for the supported open-weight models or at AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI in hybrid configurations. IBM's install guide lists telemetry as disabled for air-gapped installs and on by default (can be disabled) for connected installs. Usage metering reports only the active-user count (automatic 24-hourly upload when connected, manual upload when air-gapped).

suitability_notes.personal: SaaS only under an accepted institutional agreement and the IBM DPA: no training and in-memory payload handling are documented, but account, admin and billing data stay in US East whatever region is chosen. The self-hosted route is preferable.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Enterprise self-hosted deployment on institution-operated OpenShift, installed by the air-gapped method (on-premises inference only, telemetry disabled per IBM's install guide) with a supported open-weight core model and the gpt-oss-20b guardrail served on premises. Hybrid/frontier-model configurations and SaaS do not qualify.

compliance: IBM's Bob FAQ states 'IBM is ISO 27001 certified' at company level; penetration-test summaries and ISO 27001 certificates for Bob are offered under NDA. Bob-specific certification scope and audit reports not reviewed
pricing: SaaS: 30-day free trial (50 Bobcoins, no payment); Pro $20/month (50 Bobcoins), Pro+ $60/month (180), Ultra $200/month (1000); 1 Bobcoin = $0.50; prices indicative, vary by country, exclude taxes; opt-in overage. Enterprise (team admin, Bobalytics, on-premises/air-gapped deployment) via sales; self-hosted needs a self-hosted entitlement and its price is not published. Premium Packages (e.g. Java Modernization $20/month) cost extra.
academic: No academic or student programme listed on the pricing page.
use_cases: agentic coding in a standalone desktop IDE (macOS, Windows, Linux)
terminal and CI automation through Bob Shell
codebase understanding and modernization (Java, IBM i, IBM Z packages)
institution-hosted, air-gapped coding assistant on OpenShift with on-premises models
notes: IBM's agentic IDE and terminal assistant (Bob IDE, Bob Shell). The self-hosted option became generally available on 30 September 2026 and is Enterprise-only. The Bob backend runs on customer-managed OpenShift 4.20-4.22 (amd64); model serving is sized separately, and IBM's recommended vLLM settings for the 550B Nemotron 3 Ultra come from H200 testing at tensor-parallel size 8. This first self-hosted release has no in-place upgrades, no Admin UI activity logs and no Bobalytics. Product focus is enterprise software delivery and modernization, so research use needs an institutional platform team. The public IBM/ibm-bob GitHub repository carries an Apache-2.0 licence but holds only a README and the issue tracker; the product itself is proprietary.
tier_gate: Enterprise self-hosted entitlement, air-gapped installation on institution-operated OpenShift with a supported open-weight model and guardrail served on premises; SaaS and hybrid/frontier-model configurations do not qualify for special-category data

required_controls: Deploy Bob self-hosted (Enterprise self-hosted entitlement) on an institution-operated OpenShift cluster using the air-gapped installation method (mirrored images; IBM documents on-premises inference only and telemetry disabled for this method).
Configure the single core model as a supported open-weight model served on premises (e.g. Red Hat OpenShift AI or vLLM) plus the gpt-oss-20b guardrail; configure no hybrid or frontier model endpoint.

Turn off client telemetry in Bob IDE and Bob Shell, use the offline usage-metering upload, manage client updates through the UpdateMode group policy, block egress (including Bobalytics links, external MCP servers and browser tools), and set task-history retention to the approved period.
residual_risks: IBM documents telemetry as disabled for air-gapped installs, but does not state what the IDE and Shell clients send, or where, when connected to a self-hosted backend; confirm with network monitoring before use.
On-premises model serving needs substantial GPU capacity and its own hardening; vLLM collects anonymous usage stats unless VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS or DO_NOT_TRACK is set.
First self-hosted GA release: no in-place upgrades and no Admin UI activity logs; security logging is the customer's responsibility at OpenShift level.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Coder Agents
software_license: AGPL-3.0 (repository core, including the coderd chat/agent code); enterprise/ directory under Coder's license-key-gated Enterprise licence
deployment: self-hosted only: agent loop in the customer's Coder control plane (servers, Kubernetes or Docker), workspaces on customer infrastructure; air-gapped installs documented; no SaaS component
model_backend: Administrator-configured providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (self-hosted models, internal gateways, LiteLLM); optional per-user BYOK.
data_handling_note: The agent loop, chat history (Coder PostgreSQL database) and tool execution stay inside the customer's Coder deployment; prompts, attachments and tool results go only to the configured LLM provider, whose own retention and training terms apply unless a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint is used. Retention defaults keep chats indefinitely: auto-archive is off by default, and only archived conversations are purged (default 30 days after archiving; turning retention off keeps them indefinitely). Chat debug logging (full LLM requests and responses) is off by default; if enabled, debug data is kept 30 days by default. Deployment telemetry to Coder is on by default and, per the source code, includes per-chat metadata (IDs, status, message and token counts, configured provider and model names) but not message content, plus the administrator email; CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false turns it off. Licences with usage publishing send hourly Agent Time totals (licence JWT and deployment ID, no chat data) to Coder's Tallyman server, shared with Metronome; air-gapped customers must arrange an alternative with Coder.

suitability_notes.personal: Self-hosted deployment with either a self-hosted model endpoint or a provider covered by an institutional agreement/DPA; disable BYOK where personal keys are not allowed, and set retention and telemetry.
suitability_notes.special: Only with control plane, PostgreSQL and workspaces on institution infrastructure, a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model as the only enabled provider, BYOK disabled, telemetry and update checks off, debug logging off, retention/auto-archive set, and all egress (workspace templates, MCP servers, provider-native web search, STUN/DERP, usage reporting) controlled.

pricing: Pricing page: Community free (open source), Premium billed annually per user (price not shown), AI Premium custom. The pricing page lists up to 5 active Coder Agents for Community and Premium and unlimited for AI Premium; the Agents docs instead say a Premium licence with Agent Hours has no concurrency cap until the purchased hard limit is reached. Infrastructure and model costs are separate.
academic: No academic programme listed on the pricing page; the Community edition is free, and Coder's site links to free homelab licences (terms not checked).
use_cases: delegating coding tasks to an agent that provisions and works in self-hosted Coder workspaces
API-triggered background coding automation on institutional infrastructure
institution-wide self-hosted coding agent with centrally governed models, including on-premises models
notes: Standalone Go agent built into the Coder control plane; Coder states it is not a wrapper around Claude Code or Codex. Generally available in Coder v2.37.0 (1 September 2026; GA blog 9 September). It needs a running Coder deployment with workspace templates, so it suits institutions with a platform or research-computing team rather than individual researchers. Coder's separate Agent Relay connects cloud-hosted agents such as Cursor to Coder workspaces and does not keep inference in-house.
tier_gate: Self-hosted Coder deployment on institution infrastructure with a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model as the only provider; Community runs up to 5 concurrent agents (pricing page also lists 5 for Premium; AI Premium unlimited)

required_controls: Run the Coder control plane, PostgreSQL and workspaces on institution-controlled infrastructure; configure only a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model endpoint and disable AI Gateway BYOK.

Set CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false and CODER_UPDATE_CHECK=false, disable public STUN and use Coder's built-in or institutional DERP relays, and agree an alternative to Tallyman usage reporting with Coder if a licence with usage publishing is used.
Restrict workspace-template, MCP-server and web-search egress, keep chat debug logging off, and set auto-archive and conversation/debug retention to the institution's policy.
residual_risks: Chats are kept indefinitely by default (auto-archive off); chat history, attachments and any debug logs persist in the Coder database, whose access, backup and retention are the institution's responsibility.
Agent workspaces have full internet access unless templates restrict outbound network access.
Agent quality depends on the self-hosted model chosen; some tools (computer use) need Anthropic or OpenAI providers.
GA only since Coder v2.37.0 (September 2026) with frequent releases and API changes; pin versions and review release notes.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Kimi Code CLI
deployment: local CLI/TUI (single binary or npm) with a local web UI; Kimi-managed cloud inference by default; Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Google endpoints configurable
model_backend: Kimi Code managed service via /login OAuth (membership quota; managed API at api.kimi.com) or a Kimi Platform API key (default base_url api.moonshot.ai); Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible (base_url override, usable for institution-hosted servers), OpenAI Responses, Google GenAI and Vertex AI provider types configurable in config.toml.
data_handling_note: Default managed route: the kimi.com privacy policy (Beijing Moonshot, effective 2026-08-31, linked from the Kimi Code page) uses de-identified input/output to optimise models; users can opt out of training by contacting customer service; storage in the PRC. API-key route: the Kimi Open Platform policy (Moonshot AI Pte. Ltd., Singapore, last update 2025-04-30) lists training among uses with no training-specific opt-out stated; terms for platform.kimi.com keys were not assessed. Which policy governs global-region logins (kimi login --region global) is not established. No DPA found. CLI: anonymous telemetry on by default, with or without sign-in (telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to disable); per source code it sends device ID, model, session ID, crash and API-error events with paths, emails, URLs and tokens scrubbed, to a Kimi collector (default mainland-cn region profile); the opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0 (2026-09-04). Auto-update on by default; signed-in users' web fetches use the managed Kimi fetch service unless an endpoint is set; /feedback can attach diagnostic logs and codebase context; Remote Control (paid membership, signed in) relays sessions through Kimi's relay. Sessions, logs and credentials are stored under ~/.kimi-code.

suitability_notes.personal: Only with an institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a third-party provider under an institutional agreement, with telemetry disabled and no Kimi OAuth sign-in. The managed Kimi routes have no verified DPA and their policies permit training use (PRC or Singapore storage).
suitability_notes.special: Only with a self-hosted/institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, telemetry=false, no /login to the managed service, no Remote Control or /feedback, auto-update and plugin marketplace controlled, and network egress limited to that endpoint and verified at the network layer.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification; no Kimi Code DPA, certification or data-residency commitment was found.
pricing: CLI free (MIT). Managed Kimi Code use requires a Kimi membership: Plus and above on current plans (Andante and above on legacy plans); the Go tier has no coding quota. Subscribed members can opt in to pay-as-you-go Extra Usage (RMB balance, not available for Enterprise) after quota. Membership prices were not captured (UNVERIFIED). Kimi Platform API keys are billed by the Open Platform; third-party API and self-hosted inference costs are separate.
academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.
use_cases: terminal agentic coding and repository editing
driving sessions from Zed or JetBrains over ACP
coding against an institution-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint for data-sensitive work
notes: TypeScript successor of the archived Python kimi-cli (archived, 'no longer maintained'); v2.0.0 released 2026-09-17, 2.1.1 on 2026-09-24. Includes ACP mode, a plugin marketplace, a local web UI and Remote Control (available without a flag since 0.42.0; started with kimi rc; requires a signed-in paid membership). TUI built on pi-tui (MIT); the VS Code extension (Apache-2.0) and Kimi Code Desktop are separate surfaces. The docs document base_url override and a vLLM-compatibility fix but no dedicated local-model guide.
tier_gate: Institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, telemetry=false, no Kimi OAuth sign-in and no Remote Control for regulated data

required_controls: Configure only an institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible provider (base_url to a self-hosted server); do not run /login to the Kimi Code managed service or use a Kimi Platform API key.

Set telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1; set disable_feedback_survey=true and do not use /feedback; set [upgrade].auto_install=false; do not start Remote Control (kimi rc), which relays through Kimi's service.

Point KIMI_CODE_PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_URL to a local file or block it; restrict MCP servers, web search/fetch and online /provider catalog import; limit network egress to the approved endpoint and verify it at the network layer.
Protect ~/.kimi-code session, log and credential files under institutional retention rules.
residual_risks: No dedicated local-model guide; the endpoint override must be validated together with network egress before use.
Telemetry is on by default and posts to a Kimi collector; its opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0, so a regression could leak metadata unless egress is blocked.
Managed-route policies permit training use and differ by route and region; an accidental managed sign-in moves data to Moonshot under those terms.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Deep Agents Code
deployment: local Python CLI (dcode) that runs a local LangGraph dev server on localhost; tools run locally or in optional remote sandboxes; inference via the chosen provider, including local Ollama
model_backend: Any LangChain-compatible chat model. OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini integrations are included by default. Extras include Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Groq, Fireworks, Hugging Face, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter and LiteLLM, among others. Also local Ollama, OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints (configurable base_url), and ChatGPT sign-in (openai_codex).
data_handling_note: BYOK: no dcode-hosted inference service is documented, so provider terms govern inference. If no model is set, startup falls back to an OPENAI, ANTHROPIC or GOOGLE key found in the environment. LangSmith tracing is off unless a LangSmith key is stored via /auth or the shell already sets LANGSMITH_TRACING=true with a key. It sends agent operations and tool calls to LangSmith. --no-tracing or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false disables it. Default-on network calls: a PyPI update check and auto-install at session start, and an hourly pricing-catalog refresh from raw.githubusercontent.com. Also, on each launch, langgraph-cli sends a usage ping (OS, OS version, Python and CLI version, command name, anonymised flags) to a Supabase endpoint unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. The dcode docs do not mention this ping. Optional cloud services: Tavily web search, remote sandboxes, MCP servers. Sessions, history and credentials live under ~/.deepagents. Offloaded conversation archives are deleted after 30 days by default.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama, an institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement. Pin allowed models (managed [models].allowed). Keep LangSmith tracing off unless LangSmith itself is approved. Set LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. Control remote sandboxes, Tavily web search and MCP servers.
suitability_notes.special: Only with local Ollama (or an institution-hosted endpoint inside the controlled network) enforced by a managed model allowlist. Also required: tracing disabled, LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1, update checks and pricing refresh disabled, no remote sandboxes, no web-search key, and egress limited to the local endpoint.

compliance: The MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification. LangSmith tracing, Tavily web search and remote sandboxes are separate services with their own terms.
The required local server runtime (langgraph-api, langgraph-runtime-inmem) is Elastic-2.0 licensed according to PyPI metadata (source-available, not OSI).
pricing: Free MIT software. Model-provider usage, optional LangSmith tracing, web search and any remote sandbox provider are billed separately. Local Ollama inference has hardware cost only.
academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.
use_cases: terminal coding agent with local Ollama models
repository editing and test running with approval controls
group-wide agent settings (model allowlist, approval mode, tracing, updates) enforced by administrators via managed_config.toml
notes: Terminal coding agent built on the Deep Agents SDK; package deepagents-code (classifier Beta; 0.1.83 on 2026-10-07). Forked from deepagents-cli at v0.1.0 (2026-05-12, per changelog). deepagents-cli is now marked as deprecated deployment tooling. dcode launches a local LangGraph dev server, whose langgraph-cli wrapper sends an anonymous usage ping unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. Administrators can enforce settings, including a model allowlist, with managed_config.toml.
tier_gate: Local Ollama or institution-controlled endpoint pinned by managed model allowlist; tracing, LangGraph CLI analytics, update checks, remote sandboxes and web search off for regulated data

required_controls: Use local Ollama (or an institution-hosted endpoint inside the controlled network) only. Enforce it with managed_config.toml [models].allowed (e.g. ollama:*) so startup cannot fall back to cloud keys in the environment and classifier or subagent models stay local.

Disable LangSmith tracing (DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false), LangGraph CLI analytics (LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1), update checks ([update] check=false), pricing-catalog refresh (prices_auto_update=false) and remote sandboxes. Store no Tavily web-search key.
Restrict MCP servers and shell egress to the local endpoint; govern ~/.deepagents session, history and credential files.
residual_risks: Beta software with near-daily releases; behaviour and defaults can change between versions.
The bundled LangGraph server runtime is Elastic-2.0 with no public GitHub source; its network behaviour was not inspected. Verify egress in the deployed configuration.
The LangGraph CLI analytics ping is on by default and is not documented in the dcode docs; a missed environment variable re-enables it.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: Oh My Pi
vendor: Stencil Labs, Inc. / Can Bölük (fork of Pi by Mario Zechner)
deployment: local CLI/TUI with local or cloud inference; optional Stencil-hosted services (encrypted /share server, /collab relay, auto-QA collector, and with an invite-only stencil.so account omp stream/clip); self-run auth broker
model_backend: Cloud APIs, OAuth/coding-plan subscriptions and documented local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) plus custom OpenAI-compatible providers; downloadable on-device models (local catalog) for auxiliary tiny and speech roles. Unset role chains fall back to built-in priority lists that can include cloud services.
data_handling_note: Provider terms govern cloud inference. Several network paths are on by default: a startup update check, marketplace plugin-update notices, and a background model-catalog refresh from catalog.stencil.so. Auto-QA (dev.autoqa) is on by default; the first report opens a consent dialog, and on Yes the model-written reports plus model, version and install ID go to qa.omp.sh. Unset tiny-role title generation uses an online model. OTLP export starts only when an endpoint is configured. /share uploads an encrypted session to my.omp.sh/s by default (or a secret gist); /collab uses the wss://my.omp.sh relay (autoStart off); omp stream/clip send screen content to live.omp.sh. Stencil's Privacy Policy (effective 2026-10-02) covers omp and its supporting services and allows training on Content unless the user opts out in account settings; Stencil's Terms bar GDPR Art. 9 data from the hosted Services. Local use of the MIT software is governed by the licence alone.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local or institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement; set dev.autoqa false, leave OTLP unset, and do not use /share, /collab, stream or clip.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a local server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint on controlled infrastructure, explicit local tiny/memory/judge roles with empty fallback chains, auto-QA, update checks, sharing, collaboration, streaming, web_search, browser and cloud security scans off, and egress limited to the local endpoint. Stencil-hosted services are excluded by Stencil's own Terms for Art. 9 data.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification.
pricing: MIT software is free. Cloud provider APIs/subscriptions and local hardware costs are separate. Stencil's Terms reference Paid Services for its hosted offerings; no omp price was found.
academic: Available without academic eligibility; no academic programme found.
use_cases: terminal coding with local open-weight models
language-server and debugger-assisted repository editing
coding sessions with persistent project memory
notes: Fork of Pi (rca-pi) that has diverged substantially (README: about 80k lines of Rust core, LSP/DAP tools, agent memory, collaboration; over 13,000 commits by the lead maintainer); not a thin fork. v18.8.7 released 2026-10-09 with near-daily releases; large open-issue backlog (about 2,170 open issues on 2026-10-10). Session sharing, collaboration relay, streaming, auth broker and extensions require separate review.
tier_gate: Local endpoint and explicit local-only role chains; auto-QA, update checks, OTLP, sharing, collaboration, streaming and web search off; no cloud inference or Stencil-hosted services for regulated data

required_controls: Configure only a local provider (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint) on institution-controlled hardware; assign tiny, memory and judge roles to local models with explicit empty fallback chains so no role falls back to online defaults.

Set dev.autoqa: false (or PI_AUTO_QA=0) rather than relying on the consent dialog; set startup.checkUpdate false and marketplace.autoUpdate off; leave OTLP endpoints unset; prohibit /share, /collab, omp stream/clip and Stencil login.

Disable or egress-block web_search, browser, URL reads and cloud security scans; restrict extensions, project inputs (hooks, MCP), shell tools and network egress to the local endpoint; govern local session files.
residual_risks: Default-on update checks, catalog refresh from catalog.stencil.so, install-ID consumers and model-weight downloads create outbound traffic; verify egress in the deployed configuration.

Stencil-hosted supporting services fall under a privacy policy that allows training on Content unless opted out and Terms that prohibit GDPR Art. 9 data; one accepted consent dialog or share command moves data there.
Very fast release cadence; settings and defaults can change between versions.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

name: DeepSeek Harness
deployment: local Node launcher (dsh, npm @deepseek-ai/dsh) with web, headless, ACP and SDK profiles; Python runtime wheel packages the same command; macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (64-bit) desktop app; inference via DeepSeek official model services or user-configured providers
model_backend: DeepSeek API key (official model services); built-in third-party providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM) and custom OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoints, including company gateways and self-hosted servers.
data_handling_note: The Harness privacy policy (last update 2026-09-20) separates official model services from custom model services. On the official route DeepSeek collects session logs (inputs, uploaded files, model outputs, tool invocations, plugin configuration), uses personal data to train and improve its models, keeps input data for as long as the account exists, and stores data in the PRC; a training opt-out is listed only among rights that may be available depending on jurisdiction. With custom model services no login is needed and DeepSeek Harness does not store or process inputs/outputs server-side; the chosen provider's terms govern. Desktop analytics add available login identity and follow an application-owned collection switch with no user settings surface (default not stated); ordinary Web clients collect no product events; session telemetry defaults to feedback-only. Whether the Web UI's DeepSeek API-key route falls under this Harness policy or separate DeepSeek Open Platform terms was not checked; both send data to DeepSeek. The vendor labels the project an unaudited developer preview.

suitability_notes.personal: Not recommended during the developer preview: the vendor states the software is unaudited and not production-ready and advises against exposing sensitive data. The official DeepSeek route uses data for training, with PRC storage. This is stricter than comparable open-source CLIs with a local-endpoint route; reassess at the first stable release.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate during the developer preview even though custom self-hosted endpoints are documented: the vendor states the software is unaudited and not production-ready, and the Harness privacy policy says the Services are not designed or intended to process sensitive personal data. Reassess after a stable release with a verified institution-controlled endpoint and telemetry configuration.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification; the vendor states no security audit has been performed.
pricing: Software free (MIT licence). The documented DeepSeek route needs a DeepSeek API key from platform.deepseek.com; model charges not captured here. Third-party and custom endpoints are billed by their providers.
academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.
use_cases: repository exploration and editing in a local workspace via the web profile
headless one-shot agent jobs from the shell
plugin-extended agent workflows on nonsensitive data
notes: GitHub repository created 2026-08-13; all 26 releases so far are pre-releases (npm latest 0.2.0-rc.2; dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2 on 2026-10-09). The vendor warns of compatibility-breaking changes. Daily merges; GitHub issues are disabled and feedback goes through GitHub Discussions. Third-party plugins (dsh-plugin topic) can add code execution and network access; the vendor advises reviewing them and running in a disposable VM or container.
tier_gate: Nonsensitive/public work only during developer preview

residual_risks: Vendor designates the project an unaudited developer preview that must not be treated as secure or production-ready.
Official model services use data for training and store it in the PRC; the desktop analytics default is not documented.
Third-party plugins can add code execution and network egress.
